articles.title: All to play for: On the World chess championship in Geneva
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Chess is one sport where both the young and the old can excel

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The World chess championship opened in Geneva with a game worthy of the occasion. Both the defending champion, D. Gukesh, and his challenger, Javokhir Sindarov, produced chess of top quality, and the draw was a just result . Given that the Indian was playing with black pieces and that he had gone into the match as the less favoured of the two, Gukesh could be a little happier with the game than his Uzbek rival. The Chennai Grandmaster was in considerable time trouble on multiple occasions, but managed to solve his problems and found proper answers to the questions posed to him on the board by the confident Sindarov. The match has only begun, and there is plenty of chess left. It is a long match of 14 games, played in the classical time control, and the man who reaches 7.5 points will be the champion. The well-contested opening game would have given Gukesh, and his team comprising his coach and ‘seconds’, enough confidence, after several disappointing performances since he became the youngest World champion in history , at 18, by defeating China’s Ding Liren in Singapore two years ago. That match too had gone down the wire, with Gukesh winning the last of the 14 games, thanks to a terrible mistake towards the end by his rival. Sindarov is just six months older than Gukesh, making the Geneva match the youngest in the 140-year-old history of the World championship: both players are 20. It is remarkable that Gukesh has already seen the highs and lows of life at such a young age. For his opponent, the last one year has been better than a dream: from World No. 26 he has risen to No. 4. Chess is getting younger. The next World championship could also very well have two young contenders. Grandmasters are usually said to peak when they are around 30 and chess is one game that even older players have continued to excel in. Viswanathan Anand was 48 when he won the World rapid chess championship . The match between Gukesh and Sindarov has attracted considerable interest from across the sporting world. After the 1972 match between Boris Spassky and Bobby Fischer — the defining moment of world chess — the World championship has earned a reputation as one of the planet’s most important sporting events. No battle between two of the world’s most talented men in chess has ever disappointed.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: chess / World Chess Championship 2026 / India / Singapore / history

1. Core Context & Background: Chess is one sport where both the young and the old can excel

That match too had gone down the wire, with Gukesh winning the last of the 14 games, thanks to a terrible mistake towards the end by his rival. Sindarov is just six months older than Gukesh, making the Geneva match the youngest in the 140-year-old history of the World championship: both players are 20. • 1. Core Context & Background: Chess is one sport where both the young and the old can excel
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The World chess championship opened in Geneva with a game worthy of the occasion. Both the defending champion, D. Gukesh, and his challenger, Javokhir Sindarov, produced chess of top quality, and the draw was a just result . Given that the Indian was playing with black pieces and that he had gone into the match as the less favoured of the two, Gukesh could be a little happier with the game than his Uzbek rival. The Chennai Grandmaster was in considerable time trouble on multiple occasions, but managed to solve his problems and found proper answers to the questions posed to him on the board by the confident Sindarov. The match has only begun, and there is plenty of chess left. It is a long match of 14 games, played in the classical time control, and the man who reaches 7.5 points will be the champion. The well-contested opening game would have given Gukesh, and his team comprising his coach and ‘seconds’, enough confidence, after several disappointing performances since he became the youngest World champion in history , at 18, by defeating China’s Ding Liren in Singapore two years ago. That match too had gone down the wire, with Gukesh winning the last of the 14 games, thanks to a terrible mistake towards the end by his rival. Sindarov is just six months older than Gukesh, making the Geneva match the youngest in the 140-year-old history of the World championship: both players are 20. It is remarkable that Gukesh has already seen the highs and lows of life at such a young age. For his opponent, the last one year has been better than a dream: from World No. 26 he has risen to No. 4. Chess is getting younger. The next World championship could also very well have two young contenders. Grandmasters are usually said to peak when they are around 30 and chess is one game that even older players have continued to excel in. Viswanathan Anand was 48 when he won the World rapid chess championship . The match between Gukesh and Sindarov has attracted considerable interest from across the sporting world. After the 1972 match between Boris Spassky and Bobby Fischer — the defining moment of world chess — the World championship has earned a reputation as one of the planet’s most important sporting events. No battle between two of the world’s most talented men in chess has ever disappointed.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: chess / World Chess Championship 2026 / India / Singapore / history

articles.title: Transfer assumption: On the SAD(B)-BJP alliance in Punjab
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: BJP and SAD(B) cannot count on their support bases adding up

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Few parties understand the arithmetic of the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system, and the necessity for alliances in States where they are minor players, better than the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) . The BJP has never shied away from partnerships with little ideological cohesion if they keep it electorally relevant. India’s FPTP system is unforgiving to smaller parties in a crowded polity if their support base is limited and dispersed. Votes translate into seats only if the support crosses a certain threshold. In Punjab , the BJP, despite its best efforts, has remained confined to sections of urban Hindu voters. Even after years of poaching leaders from the perennially fractious Congress , and after polling nearly a fifth of the vote in the 2024 general election without winning a seat, it realises that it cannot be relevant without a partner with a wider rural base. The Shiromani Akali Dal (Badal) walked out of the BJP -led National Democratic Alliance in 2020 over the Centre’s farm laws, which were later repealed, as the farmers’ agitation threatened its base in rural Punjab. But much water has flowed down the many rivers of the northern State since then. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has consolidated its hold in a crowded political space and is set to complete a full term. The Panthic vote, which used to be the SAD(B)’s core support base, has now fragmented. The SAD(B) appears to believe that it can regain ground only by expanding beyond its Panthic and rural constituencies, and that the farmers’ anger against the BJP is baggage from the past. It is this expedient calculation that now binds the two parties, despite six years of bitter attacks against each other. And it is also why the Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has pointedly called the SAD(B) the “big brother” in Punjab after sealing the alliance. The SAD(B)’s calculation may not work out as well as it hopes it would. Farmers’ anger against the BJP-led Centre has not entirely dissipated in rural Punjab. In earlier alliances, the two parties transferred votes to each other effectively, partly because their voters had fewer alternatives. But a revived Congress and an entrenched AAP have shown that they can win over urban Hindu voters wary of the Akalis and rural voters who are not inclined to back parties allied with the BJP. That these two sections will simply add up for the alliance is not certain. At best, the alliance consolidates enough of the anti-AAP vote to make this a clear three-cornered contest. Punjab is a sensitive border State and one of India’s granaries. It is also among India’s most indebted States, with a stagnating agrarian economy and a government that has expanded welfare expenditure despite strained finances. It needs a serious competition of ideas on what welfare it can afford and how to revive growth. The SAD(B)-BJP alliance , with its Panthic appeal on one side and Hindu consolidation on the other, instead offers a rehash of familiar identity politics. With AAP failing to deliver on governance, and the Congress stuck in its old ways, Punjab’s voters will have to decide who they dislike the least.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: political parties / Bharatiya Janata Party / Punjab / voting / Indian National Congress / General Elections 2024 / Shiromani Akali Dal / Aam Aadmi Party / agriculture / economy / welfare

✍️ Editorial & Opinion Paragraph #2 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Transfer assumption: On the SAD(B)-BJP alliance in Punjab

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 11:55:57 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: BJP and SAD(B) cannot count on their support bases adding up

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Few parties understand the arithmetic of the first-past-the-post (FPTP) system, and the necessity for alliances in States where they are minor players, better than the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) . The BJP has never shied away from partnerships with little ideological cohesion if they keep it electorally relevant. India’s FPTP system is unforgiving to smaller parties in a crowded polity if their support base is limited and dispersed. Votes translate into seats only if the support crosses a certain threshold. In Punjab , the BJP, despite its best efforts, has remained confined to sections of urban Hindu voters. Even after years of poaching leaders from the perennially fractious Congress , and after polling nearly a fifth of the vote in the 2024 general election without winning a seat, it realises that it cannot be relevant without a partner with a wider rural base. The Shiromani Akali Dal (Badal) walked out of the BJP -led National Democratic Alliance in 2020 over the Centre’s farm laws, which were later repealed, as the farmers’ agitation threatened its base in rural Punjab. But much water has flowed down the many rivers of the northern State since then. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has consolidated its hold in a crowded political space and is set to complete a full term. The Panthic vote, which used to be the SAD(B)’s core support base, has now fragmented. The SAD(B) appears to believe that it can regain ground only by expanding beyond its Panthic and rural constituencies, and that the farmers’ anger against the BJP is baggage from the past. It is this expedient calculation that now binds the two parties, despite six years of bitter attacks against each other. And it is also why the Union Home Minister, Amit Shah, has pointedly called the SAD(B) the “big brother” in Punjab after sealing the alliance. The SAD(B)’s calculation may not work out as well as it hopes it would. Farmers’ anger against the BJP-led Centre has not entirely dissipated in rural Punjab. In earlier alliances, the two parties transferred votes to each other effectively, partly because their voters had fewer alternatives. But a revived Congress and an entrenched AAP have shown that they can win over urban Hindu voters wary of the Akalis and rural voters who are not inclined to back parties allied with the BJP. That these two sections will simply add up for the alliance is not certain. At best, the alliance consolidates enough of the anti-AAP vote to make this a clear three-cornered contest. Punjab is a sensitive border State and one of India’s granaries. It is also among India’s most indebted States, with a stagnating agrarian economy and a government that has expanded welfare expenditure despite strained finances. It needs a serious competition of ideas on what welfare it can afford and how to revive growth. The SAD(B)-BJP alliance , with its Panthic appeal on one side and Hindu consolidation on the other, instead offers a rehash of familiar identity politics. With AAP failing to deliver on governance, and the Congress stuck in its old ways, Punjab’s voters will have to decide who they dislike the least.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: political parties / Bharatiya Janata Party / Punjab / voting / Indian National Congress / General Elections 2024 / Shiromani Akali Dal / Aam Aadmi Party / agriculture / economy / welfare

articles.title: Spinning wheels: on urban mobility in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Karnataka needs a coherent policy on urban mobility

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: While Karnataka has spent years disputing motorcycle owners’ right to carry paying passengers, Bengaluru — with the dubious distinction of having one of the world’s highest travel times per unit distance — struggles with inadequate public transport capacity and lacklustre intermediate options. The Supreme Court ruling on November 20 to dismiss Karnataka’s appeal was thus straightforward, allowing motorcycles to be registered as transport vehicles. The State has often called bike taxis unsafe, yet has not improved the prospects of safer options. Earlier this year, the Centre for Science and Environment estimated the number of buses in urban centres nationwide to be 70% short of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs benchmark and that 400 cities with populations between a lakh and 10 lakh altogether lacked organised bus services. In March, the BMTC reported a fleet of around 7,000 buses in Bengaluru, versus the 13,000 by 2025 envisaged by the Comprehensive Mobility Plan. Expanding the number of Metro stations also creates more demand for travel to and from stations, but the operating costs of the public transport corporation expected to serve that demand are not covered by the resulting increase in rail ridership. Overall, Karnataka has struggled to set up a consistent transport policy. An expert committee recommended against bike taxis in Bengaluru for first- and last-mile connectivity and in favour of better walking infrastructure and bicycle rentals in 2019, only for the State to launch the electric bike-taxi scheme in 2021, then rescind it in 2024 over safety concerns and drivers’ disputes. The market for short booked journeys is also dysfunctional. But while allowing bike taxis could temper autorickshaw fares, the State must investigate drivers’ operating costs, the difference between the paid and the received amounts, and prevent large platforms from exploiting the market. Finally, while the Union Road Transport Ministry has reported that 46.2% of all road deaths involved two-wheeler users, two-wheelers’ safety relative to autorickshaws and cabs, by the number and distance of journeys, is unclear. ✍️ Editorial & Opinion Paragraph #4 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Spinning wheels: on urban mobility in Karnataka

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 12:02:31 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Karnataka needs a coherent policy on urban mobility

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: While Karnataka has spent years disputing motorcycle owners’ right to carry paying passengers, Bengaluru — with the dubious distinction of having one of the world’s highest travel times per unit distance — struggles with inadequate public transport capacity and lacklustre intermediate options. The Supreme Court ruling on November 20 to dismiss Karnataka’s appeal was thus straightforward, allowing motorcycles to be registered as transport vehicles. The State has often called bike taxis unsafe, yet has not improved the prospects of safer options. Earlier this year, the Centre for Science and Environment estimated the number of buses in urban centres nationwide to be 70% short of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs benchmark and that 400 cities with populations between a lakh and 10 lakh altogether lacked organised bus services. In March, the BMTC reported a fleet of around 7,000 buses in Bengaluru, versus the 13,000 by 2025 envisaged by the Comprehensive Mobility Plan. Expanding the number of Metro stations also creates more demand for travel to and from stations, but the operating costs of the public transport corporation expected to serve that demand are not covered by the resulting increase in rail ridership. Overall, Karnataka has struggled to set up a consistent transport policy. An expert committee recommended against bike taxis in Bengaluru for first- and last-mile connectivity and in favour of better walking infrastructure and bicycle rentals in 2019, only for the State to launch the electric bike-taxi scheme in 2021, then rescind it in 2024 over safety concerns and drivers’ disputes. The market for short booked journeys is also dysfunctional. But while allowing bike taxis could temper autorickshaw fares, the State must investigate drivers’ operating costs, the difference between the paid and the received amounts, and prevent large platforms from exploiting the market. Finally, while the Union Road Transport Ministry has reported that 46.2% of all road deaths involved two-wheeler users, two-wheelers’ safety relative to autorickshaws and cabs, by the number and distance of journeys, is unclear. The State should require aggregators to report injuries and fatalities and investigate the consequences of drivers’ earnings being linked to the number of trips undertaken. The Union government’s 2025 Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines already address passenger security, fares, and insurance while allowing States to authorise privately registered motorcycles through aggregators. Karnataka should exercise this additional power. A large national programme is required to address funding for public transport, which is necessary even when it is not immediately profitable.

articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Developed nations must bear much of the cost of carbon emissions

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: COP31 ended in Antalya, Türkiye, with a whimper. The 190-odd countries that had convened for nearly 12 days — a close to 50-hour overshoot — failed to agree on an overarching political statement , called a cover text, that acts as a stepping stone to future, collective global action on climate change. Usually, cover texts evolve as a final synthesis of deliberations ; the COP31 leadership, helmed by Türkiye and Australia, thought it fit to push for a cover text early in the proceedings. The headline sought was a global electrification target: 35% of global final energy consumption will come from electricity by 2035, in the hope that this would reduce direct fossil fuel emissions. Country-blocks outside the EU, such as coalitions of the least developed countries, island nations, some South American countries — reportedly 130 countries — were also insistent on fossil fuel language. While COP 31 made some progress on old pathways, such as the Just Transition agreement, it is perplexing that the delegations could not make progress on the other big prong of negotiations: climate finance. The increase in solar panel installations and the significant shift towards battery use in grid storage and transport did not come cheap: the cost of the land required for their installation, their intermittent nature of being dependent on weather, grid upgrades all carry costs. It is global markets, imperfectly connected, but connected, that have managed to bring it to this stage over decades. However, it is no longer prudent to sweep this under the rug by scuttling experimental approaches — namely carbon capture — as inimical to the broader commitment to eschew fossil fuel. When the primary framework climate agreement was crafted three decades ago, nobody envisaged AI and the drain that data centres portended or the wars that would see the vociferous antagonists of coal immediately shore up their gas reserves. While COP 31 made some progress on old pathways, such as the Just Transition agreement, it is perplexing that the delegations could not make progress on the other big prong of negotiations: climate finance. The increase in solar panel installations and the significant shift towards battery use in grid storage and transport did not come cheap: the cost of the land required for their installation, their intermittent nature of being dependent on weather, grid upgrades all carry costs. It is global markets, imperfectly connected, but connected, that have managed to bring it to this stage over decades. India and China, major fossil emitters, with large, still indigent populations, are also leaders in total clean energy installations. Therefore it stands to reason that developed countries, which have committed to providing climate finance in recognition of their historical emissions, make good on past promises to shoulder the cost of the carbon emissions that are responsible for warming. Economic crises are a feature, and not a bug, of the interconnected financial system enveloping the world and there are, undeniably, challenges to diverting the necessary finance towards countries most vulnerable to climate change impact. However, it is no longer prudent to sweep this under the rug by scuttling experimental approaches — namely carbon capture — as inimical to the broader commitment to eschew fossil fuel. When the primary framework climate agreement was crafted three decades ago, nobody envisaged AI and the drain that data centres portended or the wars that would see the vociferous antagonists of coal immediately shore up their gas reserves. Without honest good-faith dialogue, the COP is at risk of being a sideshow: a mortal blow to multilateralism.

articles.title: Just verdict: on Myanmar and the International Court of Justice
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Rohingya cannot return unless Myanmar turns democratic

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: On November 19, the International Court of Justice held that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. It is for the first time that the court has found any state responsible for the crime. The verdict, with nine votes to six, was not lightly reached. Genocide requires proof of an intent to destroy a group. In the absence of direct evidence of a plan, the court could infer that intent only if it was “the only reasonable inference” from the facts, a high bar to affix responsibility. The facts it accepted are harrowing. In 2017, in what Myanmar’s army called “clearance operations” against the insurgent Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, at least 10,000 Rohingya were killed, 1,834 raped and 392 villages destroyed in northern Rakhine State. Over 7,00,000 fled to Bangladesh. Then Army chief Min Aung Hlaing, now Myanmar’s “civilian” President, called the “Bengali problem” an “unfinished job”. Myanmar argued that it had only been fighting insurgents or at worst, driving the Rohingya out or punishing them. The court said that the army drew no distinction between fighters and civilians, had no plan to move anyone, fired on fleeing people and killed children on a scale that could not be explained as punishment. Seen alongside decades of discrimination, the evidence pointed to an intent to destroy. The incidents of 2017 were no aberration. The army drove lakhs of Rohingya into Bangladesh in 1978 and 1991-92. The junta stripped the Rohingya of citizenship in 1982 and the state branded them as “foreigners” in Arakan, disenfranchising them in 2015. While the junta’s Bamar-Buddhist vision has oppressed every minority, the Rohingya have been subjected to the most brutality. More than 1.2 million are in Bangladesh, living in dilapidated conditions, made worse due to diminished international aid. The court ordered Myanmar to allow their safe, voluntary and dignified return and to compensate them, but it has no means of enforcing its judgment. Only the UN Security Council can, but it will be subject to vetoes by Myanmar’s backers, China and Russia. On the very day of the verdict, the two joined the U.S. in Shenzhen to declare the “immunities of State officials” of “paramount importance”. Others, India among them, have courted the regime in Naypyitaw regardless, following sham elections that made the junta leader civilian President earlier this year. And Rakhine State, mired in civil war, is now mostly held by the Arakan Army which is accused of atrocities against the Rohingya. Only a truly democratic, federal, plural and peaceful Myanmar can bring the Rohingya home in safety.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: international court or tribunal / Myanmar / Rohingya crisis / crime / armed Forces / sexual assault / Bangladesh / Citizenship / welfare / United Nations / China / Russia / India / democracy

The facts it accepted are harrowing. In 2017, in what Myanmar’s army called “clearance operations” against the insurgent Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, at least 10,000 Rohingya were killed, 1,834 raped and 392 villages destroyed in northern Rakhine State. Over 7,00,000 fled to Bangladesh. Then Army chief Min Aung Hlaing, now Myanmar’s “civilian” President, called the “Bengali problem” an “unfinished job”. Myanmar argued that it had only been fighting insurgents or at worst, driving the Rohingya out or punishing them. The court said that the army drew no distinction between fighters and civilians, had no plan to move anyone, fired on fleeing people and killed children on a scale that could not be explained as punishment. Seen alongside decades of discrimination, the evidence pointed to an intent to destroy. The incidents of 2017 were no aberration. The army drove lakhs of Rohingya into Bangladesh in 1978 and 1991-92. The junta stripped the Rohingya of citizenship in 1982 and the state branded them as “foreigners” in Arakan, disenfranchising them in 2015. While the junta’s Bamar-Buddhist vision has oppressed every minority, the Rohingya have been subjected to the most brutality. More than 1.2 million are in Bangladesh, living in dilapidated conditions, made worse due to diminished international aid. The court ordered Myanmar to allow their safe, voluntary and dignified return and to compensate them, but it has no means of enforcing its judgment. Only the UN Security Council can, but it will be subject to vetoes by Myanmar’s backers, China and Russia. On the very day of the verdict, the two joined the U.S. in Shenzhen to declare the “immunities of State officials” of “paramount importance”. Others, India among them, have courted the regime in Naypyitaw regardless, following sham elections that made the junta leader civilian President earlier this year. And Rakhine State, mired in civil war, is now mostly held by the Arakan Army which is accused of atrocities against the Rohingya. Only a truly democratic, federal, plural and peaceful Myanmar can bring the Rohingya home in safety.

articles.title: G.O. issued on CAS for teachers of aided arts and science colleges
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The eligibility criteria and procedures to be followed for CAS will be implemented ‘in strict adherence’ to guidelines issued through a G.O. of January 11, 2021.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Keeping up with its announcement made during the demand for grant on August 24, the Tamil Nadu Higher Education Department issued a Government Order (G.O.) on Tuesday, awarding Career Advancement Scheme (CAS) monetary benefits to teachers of government-aided Arts and Science colleges. According to the G.O., the government has sanctioned ₹11.75 crore as recurring monthly expenditure for awarding CAS to eligible teachers, with effect from September 1. A total of 6,116 teachers will benefit from the scheme. According to the G.O., the eligibility criteria and procedures to be followed for CAS will be implemented “in strict adherence” to guidelines issued through a G.O. of January 11, 2021. The scheme would be implemented only after proper verification of the eligibility of each teacher. A screening and selection committee will scrutinise promotion requests and applications, and the Regional Joint Director will forward the minutes and recommendations to the Director of Collegiate Education. After being vetted, the files would be sent back to the Regional Joint Director who would forward the same, along with service records, to audit teams nominated by the Director-General of Audit. After receiving the observations from the audit teams, the Regional Joint Director would issue relevant CAS orders.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The G.O. warns that the responsibility of any miscalculation or error would fall squarely on the officer who issues the CAS order. The excess amount paid will be recovered from the teacher, while action will be initiated against erring officials.

• 1. Core Context & Background: The eligibility criteria and procedures to be followed for CAS will be implemented ‘in strict adherence’ to guidelines issued through a G.O. of January 11, 2021.
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Keeping up with its announcement made during the demand for grant on August 24, the Tamil Nadu Higher Education Department issued a Government Order (G.O.) on Tuesday, awarding Career Advancement Scheme (CAS) monetary benefits to teachers of government-aided Arts and Science colleges. According to the G.O., the government has sanctioned ₹11.75 crore as recurring monthly expenditure for awarding CAS to eligible teachers, with effect from September 1. A total of 6,116 teachers will benefit from the scheme. According to the G.O., the eligibility criteria and procedures to be followed for CAS will be implemented “in strict adherence” to guidelines issued through a G.O. of January 11, 2021. The scheme would be implemented only after proper verification of the eligibility of each teacher. A screening and selection committee will scrutinise promotion requests and applications, and the Regional Joint Director will forward the minutes and recommendations to the Director of Collegiate Education. After being vetted, the files would be sent back to the Regional Joint Director who would forward the same, along with service records, to audit teams nominated by the Director-General of Audit. After receiving the observations from the audit teams, the Regional Joint Director would issue relevant CAS orders.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The G.O. warns that the responsibility of any miscalculation or error would fall squarely on the officer who issues the CAS order. The excess amount paid will be recovered from the teacher, while action will be initiated against erring officials.

articles.title: Over 600 tonnes of waste generated on Maha Deepam day removed in Tiruvannamalai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Most of the collected wastes would be dumped at the 15 acre-landfill site near the Girivalam path

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: More than 2,400 sanitary workers removed over 600 tonnes of garbage that was generated on Maha Deepam day. Officials of Tiruvannamalai Corporation said that apart from the civic body, sanitary workers of District Rural Development Agency (DRDA) were also roped in for the mammoth exercise, which was started on Monday, a day before Maha Deepam as the town witnessed steady flow of pilgrims. “Rain also delayed removal of garbage on streets and the Girivalam Path. Nonetheless, sanitary workers worked round-the-clock, in shifts, to keep the town clean of wastes,” K. Balasubramanian, Corporation Commissioner, told The Hindu. Apart from sanitary staff from Tiruvannamalai Corporation, civic workers from big municipalities such as Ambur, Arcot, Arani, Arakkonam, Polur, Vandavasi, Vaniyambadi, and Gudiyatham were also roped in for the purpose. Along with Corporation Commissioner Mr. Balasubramanian, Collector Vandhana Garg inspected the work and interacted with sanitary workers. Corporation officials said that waste generated on Maha Deepam day this year was the highest (600 metric tonnes) as against that generated in 2025 (450 metric tonnes), 2024 (350 metric tonnes), and 2023 (210 metric tonnes), due to increase in footfall. Around 45 lakh devotees visited the town on Maha Deepam day. Disposable food plates formed the majority of waste, followed by those of sugarcane and sweet corn. District administration has allowed 250 individuals and organisations for annadhanam (free food). Many volunteers and groups were also provided free food on the day.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Most of the collected wastes would be dumped at the 15 acre-landfill site of the civic body near the Girivalam path. Food and other organic wastes would be recycled to make manure for farming and terrace gardens in Tiruvannamalai.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Over 600 tonnes of waste generated on Maha Deepam day removed in Tiruvannamalai

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 12:32:59 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Most of the collected wastes would be dumped at the 15 acre-landfill site near the Girivalam path

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: More than 2,400 sanitary workers removed over 600 tonnes of garbage that was generated on Maha Deepam day. Officials of Tiruvannamalai Corporation said that apart from the civic body, sanitary workers of District Rural Development Agency (DRDA) were also roped in for the mammoth exercise, which was started on Monday, a day before Maha Deepam as the town witnessed steady flow of pilgrims. “Rain also delayed removal of garbage on streets and the Girivalam Path. Nonetheless, sanitary workers worked round-the-clock, in shifts, to keep the town clean of wastes,” K. Balasubramanian, Corporation Commissioner, told The Hindu. Apart from sanitary staff from Tiruvannamalai Corporation, civic workers from big municipalities such as Ambur, Arcot, Arani, Arakkonam, Polur, Vandavasi, Vaniyambadi, and Gudiyatham were also roped in for the purpose. Along with Corporation Commissioner Mr. Balasubramanian, Collector Vandhana Garg inspected the work and interacted with sanitary workers. Corporation officials said that waste generated on Maha Deepam day this year was the highest (600 metric tonnes) as against that generated in 2025 (450 metric tonnes), 2024 (350 metric tonnes), and 2023 (210 metric tonnes), due to increase in footfall. Around 45 lakh devotees visited the town on Maha Deepam day. Disposable food plates formed the majority of waste, followed by those of sugarcane and sweet corn. District administration has allowed 250 individuals and organisations for annadhanam (free food). Many volunteers and groups were also provided free food on the day.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Most of the collected wastes would be dumped at the 15 acre-landfill site of the civic body near the Girivalam path. Food and other organic wastes would be recycled to make manure for farming and terrace gardens in Tiruvannamalai.

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Development' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Majority (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Majority' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Over 600 tonnes of waste generated on Maha Deepam day removed in Tiruvannamalai", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Most of the collected wastes would be dumped at the 15 acre-landfill site near the Girivalam path.

C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Over 600 tonnes of waste generated on Maha De' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Over 600 tonnes of waste generated on Maha De' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Most of the collected wastes would be dumped at the 15 acre-landfill site near the Girivalam path."

📰 Farmers stage protests; seek waiver of loans

🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Members of the 50 associations led by Easan Murugasamy said that farmers were only reminding the TVK government of its poll promise of complete waiver of farm loans. The government had recently urged farmers to repay their loans availed at cooperative banks by November 30, so that they may avail fresh loans from December 1. In the context of Farmers stage protests; seek waiver of loans, empirical assessment and ground-level enforcement remain essential to address implementation challenges across jurisdictions.

articles.title: Large-sized pancreatic stones removed via keyhole surgery
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: A 41-year-old male patient got relief from debilitating pain after large-sized pancreatic stones measuring up to 3 cm were removed through laparoscopic surgery at a city hospital. The patient, who was diagnosed with acute-on-chronic calcific pancreatitis accompanied by pancreatic diabetes, had severely atrophic pancreas.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A team of surgeons led by surgical gastroenterologist and director at GEM Hospital P. Senthilnathan extracted the calculi with zero abdominal scars or stitches. The patient was discharged just four days after the surgery. Speaking to presspersons on Wednesday, he said that in chronic calcific pancreatitis, stones accumulate in the central duct and cause severe blockages, excruciating pain, and secondary diabetes. “If left untreated, chronic inflammation can even increase the risk of pancreatic cancer. While smaller stones can be managed medically or endoscopically, large stones require surgery.“ The pancreas was choked with dozens of stones, including giant calculi measuring 3 cm x 1 cm lodged across the head, neck, and tail of the main pancreatic duct, and stones up to 2 cm x 2 cm trapped inside the minor duct, he added.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: As these stones sit dangerously close to major blood vessels, they must be extracted without fracturing or damaging the surrounding tissue, which is why such cases are almost universally managed through traditional open surgery, Dr. Senthilnathan added.

📰 Large-sized pancreatic stones removed via keyhole surgery

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 12:27:37 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: A 41-year-old male patient got relief from debilitating pain after large-sized pancreatic stones measuring up to 3 cm were removed through laparoscopic surgery at a city hospital. The patient, who was diagnosed with acute-on-chronic calcific pancreatitis accompanied by pancreatic diabetes, had severely atrophic pancreas.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A team of surgeons led by surgical gastroenterologist and director at GEM Hospital P. Senthilnathan extracted the calculi with zero abdominal scars or stitches. The patient was discharged just four days after the surgery. Speaking to presspersons on Wednesday, he said that in chronic calcific pancreatitis, stones accumulate in the central duct and cause severe blockages, excruciating pain, and secondary diabetes. “If left untreated, chronic inflammation can even increase the risk of pancreatic cancer. While smaller stones can be managed medically or endoscopically, large stones require surgery.“ The pancreas was choked with dozens of stones, including giant calculi measuring 3 cm x 1 cm lodged across the head, neck, and tail of the main pancreatic duct, and stones up to 2 cm x 2 cm trapped inside the minor duct, he added.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: As these stones sit dangerously close to major blood vessels, they must be extracted without fracturing or damaging the surrounding tissue, which is why such cases are almost universally managed through traditional open surgery, Dr. Senthilnathan added.

articles.title: Broad-based pressure on food prices continues: RBI Bulletin
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: CPI inflation peaked to 6.1 % (y-o-y) in October 2026 from 5.5% in September 2026, slightly above the upper tolerance level of 6%–last observed in October 2024.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: High-frequency data up to November 19 indicate continuing broad-based pressure on food prices, according to the November edition of the RBI Bulletin, released on Wednesday. . Prices of all major cereals and pulses picked up. Edible oil prices recorded a broad-based increase, led by mustard oil, the RBI officials said in the State of the Economy article. Vegetable prices presented a mixed picture, with onion prices rising moderately, tomato prices correcting sharply and potato prices picking up. The Indian basket of crude oil declined to $95 per barrel during November 1-18. “The pressure on prices was primarily driven by ‘food and beverages’,” the officials pointed out. Inflationary pressures were, however, not confined to food. Fuel and core inflation also firmed up, with 11 of the 12 CPI divisions registering sequential increases in October. Within food and beverages, inflation rose across most sub-components, with notable spikes in vegetables, cereals, pulses and oils and fats, reflecting positive month-on-month price momentum. Fuel inflation recorded a relatively moderate uptick. Geographically, inflation increased in both rural and urban areas in October, with food and beverages inflation remaining above 6% in both segments. While most States and Union Territories recorded inflation in the 4-6% range, the number reporting rates above 6% increased. On the external front, geopolitical instability in West Asia continued to weigh on the global economic outlook. Although crude oil prices retreated from their October peaks, the absence of a durable peace kept markets volatile. “Apart from extant geopolitical risks, the recent pullback in AI stocks lends uncertainty to the global financial outlook,” the officials said. Despite the challenging global environment and hawkish monetary policy stances adopted by major central banks, the RBI maintained that India’s domestic growth drivers and macroeconomic fundamentals remained important buffers.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “The Indian economy continues to maintain the resilience in economic activities as evident from high-frequency indicators,” they said.

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #13 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Broad-based pressure on food prices continues: RBI Bulletin

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 10:39:05 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: CPI inflation peaked to 6.1 % (y-o-y) in October 2026 from 5.5% in September 2026, slightly above the upper tolerance level of 6%–last observed in October 2024.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: High-frequency data up to November 19 indicate continuing broad-based pressure on food prices, according to the November edition of the RBI Bulletin, released on Wednesday. . Prices of all major cereals and pulses picked up. Edible oil prices recorded a broad-based increase, led by mustard oil, the RBI officials said in the State of the Economy article. Vegetable prices presented a mixed picture, with onion prices rising moderately, tomato prices correcting sharply and potato prices picking up. The Indian basket of crude oil declined to $95 per barrel during November 1-18. “The pressure on prices was primarily driven by ‘food and beverages’,” the officials pointed out. Inflationary pressures were, however, not confined to food. Fuel and core inflation also firmed up, with 11 of the 12 CPI divisions registering sequential increases in October. Within food and beverages, inflation rose across most sub-components, with notable spikes in vegetables, cereals, pulses and oils and fats, reflecting positive month-on-month price momentum. Fuel inflation recorded a relatively moderate uptick. Geographically, inflation increased in both rural and urban areas in October, with food and beverages inflation remaining above 6% in both segments. While most States and Union Territories recorded inflation in the 4-6% range, the number reporting rates above 6% increased. On the external front, geopolitical instability in West Asia continued to weigh on the global economic outlook. Although crude oil prices retreated from their October peaks, the absence of a durable peace kept markets volatile. “Apart from extant geopolitical risks, the recent pullback in AI stocks lends uncertainty to the global financial outlook,” the officials said. Despite the challenging global environment and hawkish monetary policy stances adopted by major central banks, the RBI maintained that India’s domestic growth drivers and macroeconomic fundamentals remained important buffers.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “The Indian economy continues to maintain the resilience in economic activities as evident from high-frequency indicators,” they said.

Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Macroeconomic (Adjective)
समष्टि अर्थशास्त्र — पूरे देश की अर्थव्यवस्था (GDP, महंगाई, RBI नीति, रोज़गार) से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Fiscal-scale, National-economic, Aggregate  |  ✖ Ant: Microeconomic, Individual, Local
Resilience (Noun)
लचीलापन और मज़बूती — किसी बड़े संकट या मंदी के बाद तेज़ी से वापस उभरने की क्षमता।
✓ Syn: Robustness, Endurance, Adaptability  |  ✖ Ant: Fragility, Vulnerability, Weakness
Inflation (Noun)
महंगाई (मुद्रास्फीति) — जब बाज़ार में वस्तुओं के दाम बढ़ें और रुपये की खरीद शक्ति कम हो जाए।
✓ Syn: Price-escalation, Hyperinflation, Dearness  |  ✖ Ant: Deflation, Disinflation, Recession

B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Broad-based pressure on food prices continues: R' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Broad-based pressure on food prices continues' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Broad-based pressure on food prices continues' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "CPI inflation peaked to 6.1 % (y-o-y) in October 2026 from 5.5% in September 2026, slightly above the upper tolerance level of 6%–last observed in..."

articles.title: Net FDI fell to more than 5.5-year low in September 2026, as outflows jumped 40%
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Despite September’s performance, net FDI in the first half of the financial year was more than 20% higher than in the same period last year

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Net foreign direct investment (FDI) into India in September 2026 fell to its lowest level in at least 5.5 years, with outflows exceeding inflows by nearly $5 billion, data released by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) shows. This was driven by a simultaneous slump in gross inflows and a jump in outflows. However, net FDI in the first half of the financial year (April-September 2026) was more than 20% higher than in the same period of the previous year. September’s net FDI figure of -$4.95 billion was the lowest since at least March 2021, the earliest month for which data is accessible. Direct investment refers to the inflows that give the investor substantial control over an asset or means of production, as opposed to portfolio investments, which are typically more in the nature of speculative purchases of minor shareholding. Gross inflows, or the total amount of direct investment entering the country, fell to $5.9 billion in September 2026, 46.6% lower than in August, and 17.6% lower than in September of last year. According to the RBI, around two-thirds of the gross inflows were channelled into manufacturing, communication, and computer services sectors, with Singapore and the U.S. as the major source countries. Total outflows climbed to $10.8 billion in September 2026, nearly 40% higher than in August, and 15% higher than in September last year. Within this, repatriation of profits by foreign companies in India grew to $6.4 billion, nearly 37% higher than in the same month last year, and the highest since at least March 2021. Outward investments made by Indian companies grew to a five-month high of $4.4 billion in September 2026. The RBI says that of the outward investments, manufacturing, and financial, insurance and business services sectors accounted for about four-fifths of the amount that flowed out of India, with The Netherlands, Singapore and the U.S. serving as the major destinations.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: economy (general) / foreign investment / economic indicator

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #14 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Net FDI fell to more than 5.5-year low in September 2026, as outflows jumped 40%

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 09:11:09 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Despite September’s performance, net FDI in the first half of the financial year was more than 20% higher than in the same period last year

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Net foreign direct investment (FDI) into India in September 2026 fell to its lowest level in at least 5.5 years, with outflows exceeding inflows by nearly $5 billion, data released by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) shows. This was driven by a simultaneous slump in gross inflows and a jump in outflows. However, net FDI in the first half of the financial year (April-September 2026) was more than 20% higher than in the same period of the previous year. September’s net FDI figure of -$4.95 billion was the lowest since at least March 2021, the earliest month for which data is accessible. Direct investment refers to the inflows that give the investor substantial control over an asset or means of production, as opposed to portfolio investments, which are typically more in the nature of speculative purchases of minor shareholding. Gross inflows, or the total amount of direct investment entering the country, fell to $5.9 billion in September 2026, 46.6% lower than in August, and 17.6% lower than in September of last year. According to the RBI, around two-thirds of the gross inflows were channelled into manufacturing, communication, and computer services sectors, with Singapore and the U.S. as the major source countries. Total outflows climbed to $10.8 billion in September 2026, nearly 40% higher than in August, and 15% higher than in September last year. Within this, repatriation of profits by foreign companies in India grew to $6.4 billion, nearly 37% higher than in the same month last year, and the highest since at least March 2021. Outward investments made by Indian companies grew to a five-month high of $4.4 billion in September 2026. The RBI says that of the outward investments, manufacturing, and financial, insurance and business services sectors accounted for about four-fifths of the amount that flowed out of India, with The Netherlands, Singapore and the U.S. serving as the major destinations.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: economy (general) / foreign investment / economic indicator

A. Despite September’s performance, net FDI in the first half of the financial year was more than 20% higher than in the same period last year.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Net FDI fell to more than 5.5-year low in Septem' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Net FDI fell to more than 5.5-year low in Sep' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Net FDI fell to more than 5.5-year low in Sep' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Despite September’s performance, net FDI in the first half of the financial year was more than 20% higher than in the same period last year."

articles.title: Duty-free raw sugar imports up to 10 lakh tonnes allowed till March 2027
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The industry expects more imports in the coming days and this will ensure supply of adequate quantity of sugar in the domestic market throughout the sugar season.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Duty-free imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar will be permitted until the end of March 2027, according to a notification issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) on Wednesday. A notification issued on August 20 had allowed duty-free imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes of sugar under the Tariff Rate Quota (TRQ) scheme until December 31, 2026. Separately, the DGFT has allowed sugar mills time until September 30, 2027, to process the imported raw sugar and sell it in the domestic market. The Indian Sugar and Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association Director General Deepak Ballani told The Hindu that price parity had prevailed over the past, making it viable for Indian importers to source raw sugar from international markets, primarily Brazil. Some imports have already begun. The industry expects more imports in the coming days and this will ensure supply of adequate quantity of sugar in the domestic market throughout the sugar season. It will also keep the prices stable, he said.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Agriculture / imports / food / economy (general) / agriculture / farms / consumer goods

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: The Commerce and Industry Ministry released the provisional Service Producer Price Indices (PPI) for the second quarter of 2026-27
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Air passenger services recorded 35.52% inflation in the July-September quarter, recording the highest rate of price rise among the seven major services for which the inflation data was released on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). Securities transaction services and banking services, however, recorded a deflation of 6.93% and 3.96% respectively, the provisional Service Producer Price Indices (PPI) for the second quarter of 2026-27 released by the Commerce and Industry Ministry showed. The PPI has inflation data for seven major services — Banking, Securities Transaction, Insurance, Management of Pension Funds, Railways, Air (Passenger), and Telecom — with base year 2022-23. Service PPI measures the change in the average prices received by producers on production of a service. As per the data, inflation in Air (Passenger) Services rose 35.52% YoY in the second quarter, compared to 31.94% in the first quarter. Annual inflation in the railway passenger service price index rose 2.17% during the September quarter, lower than 3.50% in the June quarter. Inflation in 'Banking Service Contribution' was 3.86% in Q2 of FY27, higher than 2.62% in Q1. The 'Banking Service Price' witnessed 3.96% deflation in Q2, vis-a-vis 4.98% deflation in Q1. Securities Transaction Service Prices saw a deflation of 6.93% in Q2, compared to 1.32% deflation in June quarter. Pension fund management, insurance and telecom services recorded an inflation of 1.01%, 0.49% and 0.54%, respectively in September quarter, compared to 5.48%, 0.98% and 0.72%, respectively in the June quarter.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The government would eventually include more services in the Service PPI data.

articles.title: Global climate talks must shut door on fossil fuel ‘clout’

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The breakdown in the Antalya summit has deepened the crisis of confidence in climate diplomacy, making transparency and accountability in the negotiating process more urgent than ever.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The failure of the United Nations climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, to agree on its central political statement, with countries unable to bridge their differences over fossil fuels and other key questions of climate action, has exposed the fragility of international climate cooperation. It should also sharpen scrutiny of who gets access to climate negotiations, whose interests they represent and what safeguards keep decisions accountable to the public. The Türkiye summit ended without agreement on an overarching statement. UN climate chief Simon Stiell said he shared the “deep disappointment” of many that the conference was unable to reach consensus on a statement that typically sends a policy signal to all nations. Some separate negotiating decisions were reached though. Nevertheless, the absence of a political consensus was a serious setback. The breakdown does not show that fossil fuel lobbying caused the impasse. But it does make more urgent a separate question about the credibility of the process. A forum that asks governments to make decisions in the global public interest must be transparent about who is seeking to shape those decisions, what interests they represent and how conflicts are managed. The international climate negotiations that take place every year still lack a comprehensive, enforceable system to identify and manage conflicts of interest involving powerful commercial interests, including fossil fuel companies and state-owned energy businesses. The Antalya conference has underlined why that gap matters. The fossil fuel industry’s record of muddying the waters is well documented. A 2017 study by Geoffrey Supran and Naomi Oreskes compared 187 ExxonMobil communications between 1977 and 2014, including internal documents, scientific publications and paid newspaper advertorials. It found that as the company’s communications became more public, they increasingly expressed doubt about climate science. The researchers concluded that ExxonMobil had contributed to climate science while promoting doubt about it in its advertorials. An industry team discussed a 1998 draft of the Global Climate Science Communications Plan at the American Petroleum Institute’s headquarters. The plan’s stated goal was to persuade a majority of the American public that significant uncertainties remained in climate science and to raise questions among policymakers. This history matters because companies with large investments in oil, gas and coal have a financial stake in how quickly those fuels are phased down, which technologies receive support and how the costs of the transition are distributed. That does not mean every company representative at a climate summit is there to obstruct progress, or that attendance proves influence over a decision. It, however, does mean commercial interests need to be visible and the process needs rules to prevent undue influence. The scale of corporate participation in Antalya brings the issue into sharper focus. An analysis by a coalition of non-profits identified 103 major polluter groups with delegations at the summit, including fossil fuel businesses, financiers and companies from other high-emitting sectors. It also identified 30 banks whose fossil fuel financing between 2021 and 2025 amounted to more than $2.2 trillion. These are the coalition’s classifications, not official UN figures. They do not establish that the companies or banks influenced the negotiations. But they show the scale of commercial interests present at a conference whose purpose is to limit global warming.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Lien Vandamme of the Center for International Environmental Law says the problem goes beyond the number of corporate participants. Although the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) has introduced limited disclosure requirements, she argues that it still lacks a policy to curb corporate influence. “There is currently no policy to curb corporate influence within the UNFCCC process, and this is a fundamental problem,” she says. Once companies gain access, she argues, it becomes extremely difficult to monitor how they use it to influence negotiations.

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #17 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Global climate talks must shut door on fossil fuel ‘clout’

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 10:41:40 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The breakdown in the Antalya summit has deepened the crisis of confidence in climate diplomacy, making transparency and accountability in the negotiating process more urgent than ever.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The failure of the United Nations climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, to agree on its central political statement, with countries unable to bridge their differences over fossil fuels and other key questions of climate action, has exposed the fragility of international climate cooperation. It should also sharpen scrutiny of who gets access to climate negotiations, whose interests they represent and what safeguards keep decisions accountable to the public. The Türkiye summit ended without agreement on an overarching statement. UN climate chief Simon Stiell said he shared the “deep disappointment” of many that the conference was unable to reach consensus on a statement that typically sends a policy signal to all nations. Some separate negotiating decisions were reached though. Nevertheless, the absence of a political consensus was a serious setback. The breakdown does not show that fossil fuel lobbying caused the impasse. But it does make more urgent a separate question about the credibility of the process. A forum that asks governments to make decisions in the global public interest must be transparent about who is seeking to shape those decisions, what interests they represent and how conflicts are managed. The international climate negotiations that take place every year still lack a comprehensive, enforceable system to identify and manage conflicts of interest involving powerful commercial interests, including fossil fuel companies and state-owned energy businesses. The Antalya conference has underlined why that gap matters. The fossil fuel industry’s record of muddying the waters is well documented. A 2017 study by Geoffrey Supran and Naomi Oreskes compared 187 ExxonMobil communications between 1977 and 2014, including internal documents, scientific publications and paid newspaper advertorials. It found that as the company’s communications became more public, they increasingly expressed doubt about climate science. The researchers concluded that ExxonMobil had contributed to climate science while promoting doubt about it in its advertorials. An industry team discussed a 1998 draft of the Global Climate Science Communications Plan at the American Petroleum Institute’s headquarters. The plan’s stated goal was to persuade a majority of the American public that significant uncertainties remained in climate science and to raise questions among policymakers. This history matters because companies with large investments in oil, gas and coal have a financial stake in how quickly those fuels are phased down, which technologies receive support and how the costs of the transition are distributed. That does not mean every company representative at a climate summit is there to obstruct progress, or that attendance proves influence over a decision. It, however, does mean commercial interests need to be visible and the process needs rules to prevent undue influence. The scale of corporate participation in Antalya brings the issue into sharper focus. An analysis by a coalition of non-profits identified 103 major polluter groups with delegations at the summit, including fossil fuel businesses, financiers and companies from other high-emitting sectors. It also identified 30 banks whose fossil fuel financing between 2021 and 2025 amounted to more than $2.2 trillion. These are the coalition’s classifications, not official UN figures. They do not establish that the companies or banks influenced the negotiations. But they show the scale of commercial interests present at a conference whose purpose is to limit global warming.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Lien Vandamme of the Center for International Environmental Law says the problem goes beyond the number of corporate participants. Although the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) has introduced limited disclosure requirements, she argues that it still lacks a policy to curb corporate influence. “There is currently no policy to curb corporate influence within the UNFCCC process, and this is a fundamental problem,” she says. Once companies gain access, she argues, it becomes extremely difficult to monitor how they use it to influence negotiations.

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Enforcement (Noun)
सख्ती से कानून लागू करना — किसी नियम या आदेश का ज़मीनी स्तर पर पालन करवाना।
✓ Syn: Implementation, Execution, Administration  |  ✖ Ant: Neglect, Abandonment, Waiver
Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Accountability (Noun)
जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता।
✓ Syn: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability  |  ✖ Ant: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility

A. The breakdown in the Antalya summit has deepened the crisis of confidence in climate diplomacy, making transparency and accountability in the...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Global climate talks must shut door on fossil fu' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Global climate talks must shut door on fossil' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Global climate talks must shut door on fossil' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The breakdown in the Antalya summit has deepened the crisis of confidence in climate diplomacy, making transparency and accountability in the..."

C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.

articles.title: Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Jensen Huang’s return

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Wall Street’s main indexes rallied sharply on Monday (November 23, 2026), led by a ​nearly 7% jump in the tech-heavy Nasdaq, as investors rushed back into AI-linked stocks ⁠after Nvidia said it had reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Mr. Huang’s return. Mr. Huang resigned ‌as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The chipmaker is widely regarded as a cornerstone of the AI trade, and ‌its sharp rebound helped lift sentiment across the sector after weeks of heavy selling. “Huang’s return ‌marks ⁠one of the biggest reversals in the history of the stock market. Never has so ⁠much value rested on the shoulders of a single executive,” said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation. “Wall Street envisioned a stock market without his leadership and didn’t like what it saw.” The Nasdaq-100 was on track to add more than $2 trillion ​in market value on Monday (November 23). The Nasdaq ‌Composite and the S&P 500 were on track for their biggest one-day gains since markets surged after Mr. Trump paused his “Liberation Day” tariff package in April 2025. Chip stocks gained, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 13.4% and also on track for its best session since April 2025.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The rally was broad-based in ‌the tech sphere, with the so-called Magnificent Seven stocks Tesla, Amazon , Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet climbing ​between 5.8% and 12.4%.

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #18 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 12:26:40 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Jensen Huang’s return

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Wall Street’s main indexes rallied sharply on Monday (November 23, 2026), led by a ​nearly 7% jump in the tech-heavy Nasdaq, as investors rushed back into AI-linked stocks ⁠after Nvidia said it had reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Mr. Huang’s return. Mr. Huang resigned ‌as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. The chipmaker is widely regarded as a cornerstone of the AI trade, and ‌its sharp rebound helped lift sentiment across the sector after weeks of heavy selling. “Huang’s return ‌marks ⁠one of the biggest reversals in the history of the stock market. Never has so ⁠much value rested on the shoulders of a single executive,” said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation. “Wall Street envisioned a stock market without his leadership and didn’t like what it saw.” The Nasdaq-100 was on track to add more than $2 trillion ​in market value on Monday (November 23). The Nasdaq ‌Composite and the S&P 500 were on track for their biggest one-day gains since markets surged after Mr. Trump paused his “Liberation Day” tariff package in April 2025. Chip stocks gained, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 13.4% and also on track for its best session since April 2025.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The rally was broad-based in ‌the tech sphere, with the so-called Magnificent Seven stocks Tesla, Amazon , Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet climbing ​between 5.8% and 12.4%.

A. Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jens' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.

articles.title: Ukraine says it struck two oil refineries in Russia's Samara region
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Samara’s regional governor, ​Vyacheslav Fedorishchev, said on social media that local air defence ⁠forces had downed 145 Ukrainian drones overnight, causing power outages

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Industrial facilities in the city of Syzran, in Russia’s Samara region, came ‌under Ukrainian drone attack overnight, and one person was killed ‌in a Ukrainian drone strike on ‌the ⁠regional capital, Samara, local authorities ⁠said on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). Syzran and Samara, located on the Volga River, host three major oil refineries. According ​to unverified ‌reports on social media, at least two of them, the Syzran and Kuibyshev oil refineries, were attacked. Reuters could ‌not independently verify that. Samara’s regional governor, ​Vyacheslav Fedorishchev, said on social media that local air defence ⁠forces had downed 145 Ukrainian drones overnight, causing power outages. “There are consequences ‘on the ‌ground’ that you yourselves can see. But let me remind you that you must not play into the enemy’s hands. Do not publish any photos or videos showing the aftermath ‌of the attack,” he wrote on VKontakte, ​Russia’s Facebook equivalent. Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries subsided somewhat after U.S. ⁠President Donald Trump’s mid-October declaration of an ⁠energy ceasefire. But they have picked up again sharply since the ‌end of last month.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Russian President Vladimir Putin pledged retaliation for ​the Ukrainian strikes on Tuesday (November 24).

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #19 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Ukraine says it struck two oil refineries in Russia's Samara region

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 11:39:47 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Samara’s regional governor, ​Vyacheslav Fedorishchev, said on social media that local air defence ⁠forces had downed 145 Ukrainian drones overnight, causing power outages

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Industrial facilities in the city of Syzran, in Russia’s Samara region, came ‌under Ukrainian drone attack overnight, and one person was killed ‌in a Ukrainian drone strike on ‌the ⁠regional capital, Samara, local authorities ⁠said on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). Syzran and Samara, located on the Volga River, host three major oil refineries. According ​to unverified ‌reports on social media, at least two of them, the Syzran and Kuibyshev oil refineries, were attacked. Reuters could ‌not independently verify that. Samara’s regional governor, ​Vyacheslav Fedorishchev, said on social media that local air defence ⁠forces had downed 145 Ukrainian drones overnight, causing power outages. “There are consequences ‘on the ‌ground’ that you yourselves can see. But let me remind you that you must not play into the enemy’s hands. Do not publish any photos or videos showing the aftermath ‌of the attack,” he wrote on VKontakte, ​Russia’s Facebook equivalent. Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries subsided somewhat after U.S. ⁠President Donald Trump’s mid-October declaration of an ⁠energy ceasefire. But they have picked up again sharply since the ‌end of last month.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Russian President Vladimir Putin pledged retaliation for ​the Ukrainian strikes on Tuesday (November 24).

articles.title: Kremlin rejects ex-U.K. PM Johnson's call for a token Western force in Ukraine as unacceptable

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Russian officials have repeatedly warned that any Western troops ​deployed to Ukraine would be legitimate targets for Russian forces

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Kremlin on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) rejected former British ​Prime Minister Boris Johnson for a token Western force to ‌be deployed to Ukraine as unacceptable. "What I'm talking about is a token as a symbol of our support," said Mr. Johnson. "The reason that matters ‌is that this whole war is basically about whether [Russian President] Putin can get Ukraine back into ‌the Russian sphere of influence, and what you ‌would ⁠be saying by having even a ⁠token Western presence of the Coalition of the Willing in Ukraine, backfilling, doing logistical stuff miles and miles from the frontline, would ​be, 'Look, Vladimir Putin it's ‌up to the Ukrainians to decide which countries they invite to send their troops to Ukraine.' The Kremlin, which alleges Mr. Johnson sabotaged Ukraine peace talks in ‌2022 - something he denies - accused him of ​destructive behaviour. "This is something that is absolutely unacceptable and intolerable to the Russian side – the ⁠deployment of any foreign contingents on Ukrainian territory. This has been stated repeatedly at various levels, including by ‌President Putin," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters. "And we also know that, much to our regret, there have been repeated statements from European capitals and from Brussels regarding plans to deploy military contingents. I can repeat once again: this is something that is ‌absolutely unacceptable to Moscow."

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Russian officials have repeatedly warned that any Western troops ​deployed to Ukraine would be legitimate targets for Russian forces. Dmitry Medvedev, a former ⁠president who is deputy chairman of Russia's Security Council, on ⁠Wednesday (November 25, 2026) called Johnson a dangerous provocateur in a post on Telegram and said it was a ‌reasonable question to wonder whether a troop deployment of the kind he was suggesting would lead ​to a war between Russia and NATO.
