🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #20 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Kremlin rejects ex-U.K. PM Johnson's call for a token Western force in Ukraine as unacceptable

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 11:39:14 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Russian officials have repeatedly warned that any Western troops ​deployed to Ukraine would be legitimate targets for Russian forces

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Kremlin on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) rejected former British ​Prime Minister Boris Johnson for a token Western force to ‌be deployed to Ukraine as unacceptable. "What I'm talking about is a token as a symbol of our support," said Mr. Johnson. "The reason that matters ‌is that this whole war is basically about whether [Russian President] Putin can get Ukraine back into ‌the Russian sphere of influence, and what you ‌would ⁠be saying by having even a ⁠token Western presence of the Coalition of the Willing in Ukraine, backfilling, doing logistical stuff miles and miles from the frontline, would ​be, 'Look, Vladimir Putin it's ‌up to the Ukrainians to decide which countries they invite to send their troops to Ukraine.' The Kremlin, which alleges Mr. Johnson sabotaged Ukraine peace talks in ‌2022 - something he denies - accused him of ​destructive behaviour. "This is something that is absolutely unacceptable and intolerable to the Russian side – the ⁠deployment of any foreign contingents on Ukrainian territory. This has been stated repeatedly at various levels, including by ‌President Putin," Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters. "And we also know that, much to our regret, there have been repeated statements from European capitals and from Brussels regarding plans to deploy military contingents. I can repeat once again: this is something that is ‌absolutely unacceptable to Moscow."

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Russian officials have repeatedly warned that any Western troops ​deployed to Ukraine would be legitimate targets for Russian forces. Dmitry Medvedev, a former ⁠president who is deputy chairman of Russia's Security Council, on ⁠Wednesday (November 25, 2026) called Johnson a dangerous provocateur in a post on Telegram and said it was a ‌reasonable question to wonder whether a troop deployment of the kind he was suggesting would lead ​to a war between Russia and NATO.

articles.title: MEA separates Sheikh Hasina’s plans to return to Bangladesh from issue of extradition
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: ‘The case of a citizen willing to return voluntarily to her country on a travel document is a matter separate from the extradition request,’ MEA’s official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The return of the deposed former Prime Minister of Bangladesh Sheikh Hasina, using a “travel document” to her country and the process of her extradition from India to Bangladesh were two separate issues, India’s Ministry of External Affairs said on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). Speaking at the bi-weekly press briefing, the MEA’s official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal made the distinction, while expressing concern over the prevailing law and order situation in Bangladesh. Bangladesh’s request for Ms. Hasina’s extradition, made during the tenure of the interim government under Prof. Mohammed Yunus, is “being examined in line with our established processes”, Mr. Jaiswal said. Dhaka, in recent weeks, has talked about getting Ms. Hasina through an “acceptable prisoner exchange process”. Ms. Hasina had earlier this month requested the High Commission of Bangladesh, through a U.K.-based law firm, to issue her a fresh Bangladesh passport so that she could return home. Mr. Jaiswal said her plans to return to her country were separate from India extraditing her to Bangladesh. “The case of a citizen willing to return voluntarily to her country on a travel document is a matter separate from the extradition request,” Mr. Jaiswal said, adding that the issue of her return was a matter “between the former Prime Minister and the Bangladesh government”.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ms. Hasina’s supporters from the Awami League have been agitating in her party’s strongholds in places, including Gopalganj and Narail, where the party’s workers have been targeted by law enforcement authorities. “We understandably are concerned at the incidents of violence against minorities in Bangladesh. We urge the government of Bangladesh to thoroughly investigate these incidents and bring the perpetrators to justice,” Mr. Jaiswal said.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #21 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 MEA separates Sheikh Hasina’s plans to return to Bangladesh from issue of extradition

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 11:31:32 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: ‘The case of a citizen willing to return voluntarily to her country on a travel document is a matter separate from the extradition request,’ MEA’s official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The return of the deposed former Prime Minister of Bangladesh Sheikh Hasina, using a “travel document” to her country and the process of her extradition from India to Bangladesh were two separate issues, India’s Ministry of External Affairs said on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). Speaking at the bi-weekly press briefing, the MEA’s official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal made the distinction, while expressing concern over the prevailing law and order situation in Bangladesh. Bangladesh’s request for Ms. Hasina’s extradition, made during the tenure of the interim government under Prof. Mohammed Yunus, is “being examined in line with our established processes”, Mr. Jaiswal said. Dhaka, in recent weeks, has talked about getting Ms. Hasina through an “acceptable prisoner exchange process”. Ms. Hasina had earlier this month requested the High Commission of Bangladesh, through a U.K.-based law firm, to issue her a fresh Bangladesh passport so that she could return home. Mr. Jaiswal said her plans to return to her country were separate from India extraditing her to Bangladesh. “The case of a citizen willing to return voluntarily to her country on a travel document is a matter separate from the extradition request,” Mr. Jaiswal said, adding that the issue of her return was a matter “between the former Prime Minister and the Bangladesh government”.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ms. Hasina’s supporters from the Awami League have been agitating in her party’s strongholds in places, including Gopalganj and Narail, where the party’s workers have been targeted by law enforcement authorities. “We understandably are concerned at the incidents of violence against minorities in Bangladesh. We urge the government of Bangladesh to thoroughly investigate these incidents and bring the perpetrators to justice,” Mr. Jaiswal said.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Israeli military confirmed it had killed Abuelouf, whom it described as a significant figure who "served as ‌a key source of expertise in efforts to restrict the IDF’s counterterrorism operations in the ‌Gaza ⁠Strip"

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Israel's military killed a senior Hamas security ‌official as well as his wife and two children with an airstrike on ​their Gaza Strip apartment early on Wednesday (November 25, 2026), Gaza's Hamas-run Interior Ministry ⁠and medics said. The airstrike that killed Mohammad Abuelouf, a Hamas colonel who headed the militants' internal security service in northern Gaza, and his family was the second Israeli attack to kill a senior Hamas ‌security official in the past 24 hours. The Israeli military confirmed it had killed Abuelouf, whom it described as a significant figure who "served as ‌a key source of expertise in efforts to restrict the IDF’s counterterrorism operations in the ‌Gaza ⁠Strip". Despite a year-old ceasefire, Israel has continued to carry out attacks that ⁠it says target Hamas but have also killed many civilians. The broader ceasefire plan, backed by U.S. President Donald Trump, has not halted the violence or secured Hamas' disarmament. Medics said Wednesday's (November 25, 2026) airstrike had ripped through Abuelouf's apartment ​in the Beach refugee camp ‌in western Gaza City, near the coast. Later in the morning, another Israeli airstrike hit Gaza City's northern Karama neighbourhood, killing one person, medics said. The Israeli military said Abuelouf had helped, during the war and more recently, ‌to advance attacks against Israeli forces and civilians and had worked to restore ​the capabilities of Hamas in violation of the 2025 ceasefire deal. In a statement, Hamas accused Israel of trying to cause chaos by killing ⁠officials responsible for maintaining law and order in the Gaza Strip. On Tuesday (November 24, 2026), after the military killed Naeem Abu Nahel, Hamas' head of internal security for all Gaza, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin ‌Netanyahu said there was no escape for Hamas from his country's "long reach". Hamas' internal security service, which Abu Nahel ran and in which Abuelouf was a senior official, counters Palestinians suspected of collaboration with Israel's secret service and gathers information about its plans.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: At least 1,600 Palestinians and 5 Israeli soldiers have been killed since the ceasefire was struck in October 2025, according to respective Palestinian and Israeli tallies.

Later in the morning, another Israeli airstrike hit Gaza City's northern Karama neighbourhood, killing one person, medics said. The Israeli military said Abuelouf had helped, during the war and more recently, ‌to advance attacks against Israeli forces and civilians and had worked to restore ​the capabilities of Hamas in violation of the 2025 ceasefire deal. In a statement, Hamas accused Israel of trying to cause chaos by killing ⁠officials responsible for maintaining law and order in the Gaza Strip. articles.title: IAPEN summit adopts national declaration on muscle loss and sarcopenia
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Indian Association of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (IAPEN), Chennai Chapter, adopted the Sarcopenia Declaration at Beyond Calories 2026, its national gastrointestinal nutrition summit organised in association with SIMS Hospitals in Chennai on November 25.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The declaration calls for early screening for sarcopenia, setting protein intake targets, regular strength exercise and early mobilisation and rehabilitation after illness, including post-intensive care follow-up. It also emphasises professional education, India-specific research and the development of diagnostic cut-offs suited to Indian populations. It urges policymakers to include sarcopenia in national healthy-ageing and non-communicable disease programmes, particularly focusing on rural and low-income communities. Sarcopenia is the progressive loss of muscle mass, strength and function. It can occur with ageing and is accelerated by inadequate nutrition, physical inactivity and chronic diseases. It increases the risk of falls, fractures, disability, delayed recovery from illness or surgery and loss of independence. Doctors at the summit cited data showing that 43.6% of Indians aged 60 and above have sarcopenia, with 19.4% having its severe form. They noted that the condition also affects younger people, particularly those with chronic illnesses, poor nutrition and sedentary lifestyles.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The summit featured talks by specialists in surgical gastroenterology, critical care and nutrition.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #25 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 IAPEN summit adopts national declaration on muscle loss and sarcopenia

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 12:09:46 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Indian Association of Parenteral and Enteral Nutrition (IAPEN), Chennai Chapter, adopted the Sarcopenia Declaration at Beyond Calories 2026, its national gastrointestinal nutrition summit organised in association with SIMS Hospitals in Chennai on November 25.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The declaration calls for early screening for sarcopenia, setting protein intake targets, regular strength exercise and early mobilisation and rehabilitation after illness, including post-intensive care follow-up. It also emphasises professional education, India-specific research and the development of diagnostic cut-offs suited to Indian populations. It urges policymakers to include sarcopenia in national healthy-ageing and non-communicable disease programmes, particularly focusing on rural and low-income communities. Sarcopenia is the progressive loss of muscle mass, strength and function. It can occur with ageing and is accelerated by inadequate nutrition, physical inactivity and chronic diseases. It increases the risk of falls, fractures, disability, delayed recovery from illness or surgery and loss of independence. Doctors at the summit cited data showing that 43.6% of Indians aged 60 and above have sarcopenia, with 19.4% having its severe form. They noted that the condition also affects younger people, particularly those with chronic illnesses, poor nutrition and sedentary lifestyles.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The summit featured talks by specialists in surgical gastroenterology, critical care and nutrition.

articles.title: Great Nicobar Island project: Final Calcutta High Court hearing deferred as Centre seeks to file affidavit, objections
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Centre argues that the FRA is not implemented in the A&NI, objects to some petitions claiming that they should be heard by the NGT or SC; next hearing posted for January 13, 2027; court to hear Attorney General of India on January 22

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Calcutta High Court’s final hearing in a batch of petitions alleging forest rights violations in diverting forest land for the Union government’s ₹92,000 crore Great Nicobar Island (GNI) project was deferred again on Wednesday (November 25, 2026), after the Centre sought time to file another affidavit and some documents on the question of tribal rights. The Centre argued that the Forest Rights Act (FRA), 2006, is not implemented in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands (A&NI), which the petitioners rebutted by noting that the Islands administration has already issued a certificate claiming that FRA rights have been settled, which is what is being challenged. The High Court Bench, led by Chief Justice Ravindra Vithalrao Ghuge, has now posted the hearing for the batch of petitions on January 13, 2027, when the court is also expected to begin hearing a petition that specifically challenged the A&NI administration’s orders claiming that all provisions of the FRA had been complied with in diverting 121 sq.km. for the GNI project. This comes after the Centre told the Supreme Court in October this year that it would be best if the “High Court is requested to consider and decide all such cases at the earliest”. On Wednesday, when the Calcutta High Court was about to start the final hearing in these petitions as per the orders of the Supreme Court, Additional Solicitor General (ASG) of India Vikramjit Banerjee submitted that the Centre wished to once again raise preliminary objections on the maintainability of some of the petitions. Further, on the question of tribal rights, the ASG said the Centre wished to submit one more affidavit with some additional documents. Attorney General for India, R. Venkatramani, also appeared before the High Court on Wednesday. Profile: The Great Nicobar project | Between the sea and the state The Centre’s lawyers argued that on the question of the FRA, the law that is alleged to have been violated, it has been the historical stand of the Union government, across administrations, that the FRA need not be pursued in A&NI because the Protection of Aboriginal Tribes Regulations, 1956, was already operational there. In response, the petitioner’s counsel pointed out that the A&NI administration had explicitly issued a certificate saying that the rights of local tribespeople had been settled under the FRA and that this certificate is what has been challenged. Further, the Centre submitted that it would like to continue arguing on the maintainability of two more petitions tagged as part of the same issue, noting that these two petitions dealt with matters that should be brought either before the National Green Tribunal or the Supreme Court.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The petitioner’s counsel objected to this and clarified that these two petitions specifically deal with orders that reduce the buffer zones for two specific National Parks on Great Nicobar Island.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #26 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Great Nicobar Island project: Final Calcutta High Court hearing deferred as Centre seeks to file affidavit, objections

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 11:44:58 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Centre argues that the FRA is not implemented in the A&NI, objects to some petitions claiming that they should be heard by the NGT or SC; next hearing posted for January 13, 2027; court to hear Attorney General of India on January 22

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Calcutta High Court’s final hearing in a batch of petitions alleging forest rights violations in diverting forest land for the Union government’s ₹92,000 crore Great Nicobar Island (GNI) project was deferred again on Wednesday (November 25, 2026), after the Centre sought time to file another affidavit and some documents on the question of tribal rights. The Centre argued that the Forest Rights Act (FRA), 2006, is not implemented in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands (A&NI), which the petitioners rebutted by noting that the Islands administration has already issued a certificate claiming that FRA rights have been settled, which is what is being challenged. The High Court Bench, led by Chief Justice Ravindra Vithalrao Ghuge, has now posted the hearing for the batch of petitions on January 13, 2027, when the court is also expected to begin hearing a petition that specifically challenged the A&NI administration’s orders claiming that all provisions of the FRA had been complied with in diverting 121 sq.km. for the GNI project. This comes after the Centre told the Supreme Court in October this year that it would be best if the “High Court is requested to consider and decide all such cases at the earliest”. On Wednesday, when the Calcutta High Court was about to start the final hearing in these petitions as per the orders of the Supreme Court, Additional Solicitor General (ASG) of India Vikramjit Banerjee submitted that the Centre wished to once again raise preliminary objections on the maintainability of some of the petitions. Further, on the question of tribal rights, the ASG said the Centre wished to submit one more affidavit with some additional documents. Attorney General for India, R. Venkatramani, also appeared before the High Court on Wednesday. Profile: The Great Nicobar project | Between the sea and the state The Centre’s lawyers argued that on the question of the FRA, the law that is alleged to have been violated, it has been the historical stand of the Union government, across administrations, that the FRA need not be pursued in A&NI because the Protection of Aboriginal Tribes Regulations, 1956, was already operational there. In response, the petitioner’s counsel pointed out that the A&NI administration had explicitly issued a certificate saying that the rights of local tribespeople had been settled under the FRA and that this certificate is what has been challenged. Further, the Centre submitted that it would like to continue arguing on the maintainability of two more petitions tagged as part of the same issue, noting that these two petitions dealt with matters that should be brought either before the National Green Tribunal or the Supreme Court.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The petitioner’s counsel objected to this and clarified that these two petitions specifically deal with orders that reduce the buffer zones for two specific National Parks on Great Nicobar Island.

क्रियान्वयन / ज़मीनी स्तर पर लागू करना — किसी योजना या फैसले को असलियत में पूरा करना।
✓ Syn: Execution, Enforcement, Fulfillment  |  ✖ Ant: Abandonment, Neglect, Cancellation
Maintainability (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Maintainability' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Administration (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Administration' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Operational (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Operational' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "Great Nicobar Island project: Final Calcutta High Court hearing deferred as Centre seeks to file affidavit, objections", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Centre argues that the FRA is not implemented in the A&NI, objects to some petitions claiming that they should be heard by the NGT or SC; next...
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Great Nicobar Island project: Final Calcutta Hig' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Great Nicobar Island project: Final Calcutta ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Great Nicobar Island project: Final Calcutta ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Centre argues that the FRA is not implemented in the A&NI, objects to some petitions claiming that they should be heard by the NGT or SC; next..."
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Great Nicobar Island project: Final Calcutta High Court hearing deferred as Centre seeks to file affidavit, objections"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The petitioner’s counsel objected to this and clarified that these two petitions specifically deal with orders that reduce the buffer zones for two...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The petitioner’s counsel objected to this and clarified that these two petitions specifically deal with orders that reduce the buffer zones for two..."

articles.title: India’s satellite supply chain ‘highly dependent on imports’, says space body
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: India’s space economy is currently valued at nearly $9 billion and is set to grow to $40-45 billion in less than a decade

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India’s satellite supply chain is “highly dependent” on imports for critical components and the private sector’s contribution is limited to “structural assemblies” and “propulsion components” largely supplied by established public sector firms and vintage private firms, said a report by IN-SPACe, India’s regulatory-cum-promotional body for the private space sector. While pointing out the potential of India’s private space companies, the autonomous body under the Department of Space underlined the challenges ahead. Science Minister Jitendra Singh earlier this week said that India’s space economy is currently valued at nearly $9 billion and is set to increase to $40-45 billion in less than a decade, with the private sector set to grow from a a few startups “to nearly 400-500 companies in just a few years”. The Supply Chain Landscape of Satellite Manufacturing in India report, which was made public on Wednesday, says that nearly 60% of satellite costs were attributed to electronic, electrical and electromechanical components, and specialised materials, many of which are imported. India also has limited testing and certification facilities, which weakened prospects for acceptance in global markets. Many companies largely operated on a “project-based manufacturing model”, which disincentivised long-term investment in automation and production capacity, the report noted. Critical components often took a long time to procure – frequently 12-16 months – which led to project delays and hobbled responsiveness to market opportunities. There was also a shortage of trained and skilled personnel in satellite systems engineering, quality assurance, testing and qualification, besides limited private-sector research and development and technology transfer. The report was prepared by Brijesh Kumar Sol and Yudhishthir J. of IN-SPACe and “approved” by Pawan Goenka, IN-SPACe chairman.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The report isn’t a statistical survey, but paints a descriptive map of India’s satellite manufacturing supply chain.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #27 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 India’s satellite supply chain ‘highly dependent on imports’, says space body

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 11:39:18 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: India’s space economy is currently valued at nearly $9 billion and is set to grow to $40-45 billion in less than a decade

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: India’s satellite supply chain is “highly dependent” on imports for critical components and the private sector’s contribution is limited to “structural assemblies” and “propulsion components” largely supplied by established public sector firms and vintage private firms, said a report by IN-SPACe, India’s regulatory-cum-promotional body for the private space sector. While pointing out the potential of India’s private space companies, the autonomous body under the Department of Space underlined the challenges ahead. Science Minister Jitendra Singh earlier this week said that India’s space economy is currently valued at nearly $9 billion and is set to increase to $40-45 billion in less than a decade, with the private sector set to grow from a a few startups “to nearly 400-500 companies in just a few years”. The Supply Chain Landscape of Satellite Manufacturing in India report, which was made public on Wednesday, says that nearly 60% of satellite costs were attributed to electronic, electrical and electromechanical components, and specialised materials, many of which are imported. India also has limited testing and certification facilities, which weakened prospects for acceptance in global markets. Many companies largely operated on a “project-based manufacturing model”, which disincentivised long-term investment in automation and production capacity, the report noted. Critical components often took a long time to procure – frequently 12-16 months – which led to project delays and hobbled responsiveness to market opportunities. There was also a shortage of trained and skilled personnel in satellite systems engineering, quality assurance, testing and qualification, besides limited private-sector research and development and technology transfer. The report was prepared by Brijesh Kumar Sol and Yudhishthir J. of IN-SPACe and “approved” by Pawan Goenka, IN-SPACe chairman.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The report isn’t a statistical survey, but paints a descriptive map of India’s satellite manufacturing supply chain.

D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.

articles.title: Air pollution accelerates dementia by reprogramming brain's immune cells: study
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The analysis found that people living in the most polluted third of areas are 25% more likely to develop Alzheimer's disease or a related form of dementia than those in the least polluted third

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Air pollution helps cause dementia by changing the genes that are switched on in microglia, the brain's immune cells, in ways that disrupt their normal functions, a new study has found. The study, published in the Journal of Neuroinflammation , combined health records from nearly half a million people from the UK Biobank with experiments in mouse models. "By recreating in mice what happens when people breath polluted air, we found that pollution causes major changes in which genes are active in the brain's immune cells," senior author Sanjay Rajagopalan, professor of medicine and director of the Cardiovascular Research Institute at the Case Western Reserve University's school of medicine, said. "These cells normally keep the brain healthy by clearing away debris and fighting infection. Seeing how pollution disrupts them helps explain how a stress that affects much of the world's population harms the brain, and it points us toward a way to treat it," Rajagopalan said. Mice were exposed to outdoor Cleveland (US) air for five months. The fine particles in the air, known as particulate matter 2.5 (PM2.5), were concentrated to levels similar to those found in the world's most polluted cities. Otherwise healthy mice developed memory problems, a leaky blood-brain barrier and brain inflammation. Their brains also showed a lower chemical balance reflecting its energy status and ability to withstand injury and disease. The mice's brains also showed an increased death of newborn neurons in the hippocampus, the brain's centre for learning and memory. The analysis found that people living in the most polluted third of areas are 25% more likely to develop Alzheimer's disease or a related form of dementia than those in the least polluted third. Further, in mice genetically prone to Alzheimer's, air pollution caused the same harm and also sped up amyloid plaque buildup -- a hallmark of the neurodegenerative disease.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The authors wrote: "These population-scale data in humans and experimental data in mice​ support PM2.5 as an environmental neurotoxicant and define microglial regulatory programs through which genetic background shapes the biological response to a common and modifiable exposure."

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #28 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Air pollution accelerates dementia by reprogramming brain's immune cells: study

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 09:11:01 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The analysis found that people living in the most polluted third of areas are 25% more likely to develop Alzheimer's disease or a related form of dementia than those in the least polluted third

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Air pollution helps cause dementia by changing the genes that are switched on in microglia, the brain's immune cells, in ways that disrupt their normal functions, a new study has found. The study, published in the Journal of Neuroinflammation , combined health records from nearly half a million people from the UK Biobank with experiments in mouse models. "By recreating in mice what happens when people breath polluted air, we found that pollution causes major changes in which genes are active in the brain's immune cells," senior author Sanjay Rajagopalan, professor of medicine and director of the Cardiovascular Research Institute at the Case Western Reserve University's school of medicine, said. "These cells normally keep the brain healthy by clearing away debris and fighting infection. Seeing how pollution disrupts them helps explain how a stress that affects much of the world's population harms the brain, and it points us toward a way to treat it," Rajagopalan said. Mice were exposed to outdoor Cleveland (US) air for five months. The fine particles in the air, known as particulate matter 2.5 (PM2.5), were concentrated to levels similar to those found in the world's most polluted cities. Otherwise healthy mice developed memory problems, a leaky blood-brain barrier and brain inflammation. Their brains also showed a lower chemical balance reflecting its energy status and ability to withstand injury and disease. The mice's brains also showed an increased death of newborn neurons in the hippocampus, the brain's centre for learning and memory. The analysis found that people living in the most polluted third of areas are 25% more likely to develop Alzheimer's disease or a related form of dementia than those in the least polluted third. Further, in mice genetically prone to Alzheimer's, air pollution caused the same harm and also sped up amyloid plaque buildup -- a hallmark of the neurodegenerative disease.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The authors wrote: "These population-scale data in humans and experimental data in mice​ support PM2.5 as an environmental neurotoxicant and define microglial regulatory programs through which genetic background shapes the biological response to a common and modifiable exposure."

पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।

Institutional (Adjective)
संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।
✓ Syn: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional  |  ✖ Ant: Individual, Informal, Unorganized
Neuroinflammation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Neuroinflammation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Neurodegenerative (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Neurodegenerative' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

articles.title: Meet the little stint: The tiny Siberian traveller visiting India’s wetlands
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Little Stint travels thousands of kilometres between its Arctic breeding grounds and Indian wetlands. But as shrinking mudflats and changing landscapes threaten its feeding and resting habitats, this tiny shorebird tells an important story about conserving wetlands

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The little stint, a 25-gram shorebird, comes in lakhs from the Arctic to the shores of India, particularly to Point Calimere. “It’s an unforgettable sight,” says S Sivakumar, who has been involved in monitoring shorebirds in the Gulf of Mannar for over a decade. The birds remain through the winter months and depart between March and April, sometimes later in May. “In the 1980s, the little stint could be seen in several lakhs at any point of time. Even now, the numbers are still over a lakh as the Point Calimere Wetland Complex covers over 300 kilometres across coastal Tamil Nadu ,” says Sivakumar, assistant director at the Bombay Natural History Society’s Bird Migration Study Centre at Point Calimere, adding that such long-term observations help scientists understand how bird populations and their habitats are changing. The birds remain through the winter months and depart between March and April, sometimes later in May | Photo Credit: S Sivakumar The tiny bird’s annual migration journey, a feat of endurance, involves multiple stopovers across different landscapes, each of which must provide sufficient food and safe resting grounds. As shrinking mudflats and changing landscapes threaten its feeding and resting habitats, this tiny shorebird tells an important story about conserving wetlands. Ashvin Viswanathan, scientist at Bird Count India , places the little stints as the most visible representatives of a special group of shorebirds that breed in the Arctic. “ This group is declining rapidly due to climate change and loss of habitat. Little stints too are declining in India according to SoIB,” he says, referring to the State of India’s Birds assessment. Their widespread presence, he adds, indicates the health of wetland ecosystems in India as well as conditions in the Arctic. The fact that the little stint is still a fairly common bird does not mean that it is beyond risk. It’s numbers and distribution can help draw attention to changes taking place across the habitats it depends on. The numbers are still over a lakh at Point Calimere wetlands | Photo Credit: S Sivakumar The bird’s preparation for migration is as fascinating as the journey itself. “Before setting off, they enter a phase of intense feeding called hyperphagia. They feed voraciously to build up fat reserves that act as fuel during its journey. This can add 50 to 75 percent to the bird’s body weight. There are also physiological changes, some organs shrink in size as the bird prepares for the demands of sustained flight,” explains Sivakumar adding that India is an important destination along the Central Asian Flyway that connects the bird with wintering habitats further South. The birds can be found along several coastal wetlands, including Point Calimere, Pulicat, parts of Puducherry and Kanyakumari, the Sundarbans, and the mudflats of Gujarat and Maharashtra. Across Tamil Nadu, the species is familiar to birders. “You can spot them at wetlands such as Kurichi and Ukkadam in Coimbatore,” says birder K Selvaganesh adding that the flock plays an important part of the food chain as prey for raptors, including the Western marsh marrier and the brahminy kite. Goa-based Rakesh Dhareshwar, a wildlife photographer says Goa and the wider west coast are reliable places to find them each season. “This year, I was delighted to see them inland too, at Bhigwan in Maharashtra, during a mid-Novemeber trip. However, shorebirds worldwide are in decline. Loss of coastal and inland wetlands, reclamation of mudflats, and pollution threaten stopover and wintering sites these birds depend on. The good news is that we can fix this. Protecting wetlands, salt pans and estuaries, and sharing spaces thoughtfully with people can make a real difference.” Shorebirds worldwide are in decline | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In his new book, Little Stint: A Migrant’s Tale (Neythal Pathipakam), author Byju H explores the bird’s remarkable journey through a blend of science and unconventional storytelling allowing the bird to narrate its own life, beginning with emerging from an egg in the Arctic tundra. “I wanted readers to travel with the bird,” he says adding that the book also highlights the fact that the bird’s ability to navigate vast distances depends on the availability of suitable wetlands along its migratory route.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Meet the little stint: The tiny Siberian traveller visiting India’s wetlands

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 04:46:39 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Little Stint travels thousands of kilometres between its Arctic breeding grounds and Indian wetlands. But as shrinking mudflats and changing landscapes threaten its feeding and resting habitats, this tiny shorebird tells an important story about conserving wetlands

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The little stint, a 25-gram shorebird, comes in lakhs from the Arctic to the shores of India, particularly to Point Calimere. “It’s an unforgettable sight,” says S Sivakumar, who has been involved in monitoring shorebirds in the Gulf of Mannar for over a decade. The birds remain through the winter months and depart between March and April, sometimes later in May. “In the 1980s, the little stint could be seen in several lakhs at any point of time. Even now, the numbers are still over a lakh as the Point Calimere Wetland Complex covers over 300 kilometres across coastal Tamil Nadu ,” says Sivakumar, assistant director at the Bombay Natural History Society’s Bird Migration Study Centre at Point Calimere, adding that such long-term observations help scientists understand how bird populations and their habitats are changing. The birds remain through the winter months and depart between March and April, sometimes later in May | Photo Credit: S Sivakumar The tiny bird’s annual migration journey, a feat of endurance, involves multiple stopovers across different landscapes, each of which must provide sufficient food and safe resting grounds. As shrinking mudflats and changing landscapes threaten its feeding and resting habitats, this tiny shorebird tells an important story about conserving wetlands. Ashvin Viswanathan, scientist at Bird Count India , places the little stints as the most visible representatives of a special group of shorebirds that breed in the Arctic. “ This group is declining rapidly due to climate change and loss of habitat. Little stints too are declining in India according to SoIB,” he says, referring to the State of India’s Birds assessment. Their widespread presence, he adds, indicates the health of wetland ecosystems in India as well as conditions in the Arctic. The fact that the little stint is still a fairly common bird does not mean that it is beyond risk. It’s numbers and distribution can help draw attention to changes taking place across the habitats it depends on. The numbers are still over a lakh at Point Calimere wetlands | Photo Credit: S Sivakumar The bird’s preparation for migration is as fascinating as the journey itself. “Before setting off, they enter a phase of intense feeding called hyperphagia. They feed voraciously to build up fat reserves that act as fuel during its journey. This can add 50 to 75 percent to the bird’s body weight. There are also physiological changes, some organs shrink in size as the bird prepares for the demands of sustained flight,” explains Sivakumar adding that India is an important destination along the Central Asian Flyway that connects the bird with wintering habitats further South. The birds can be found along several coastal wetlands, including Point Calimere, Pulicat, parts of Puducherry and Kanyakumari, the Sundarbans, and the mudflats of Gujarat and Maharashtra. Across Tamil Nadu, the species is familiar to birders. “You can spot them at wetlands such as Kurichi and Ukkadam in Coimbatore,” says birder K Selvaganesh adding that the flock plays an important part of the food chain as prey for raptors, including the Western marsh marrier and the brahminy kite. Goa-based Rakesh Dhareshwar, a wildlife photographer says Goa and the wider west coast are reliable places to find them each season. “This year, I was delighted to see them inland too, at Bhigwan in Maharashtra, during a mid-Novemeber trip. However, shorebirds worldwide are in decline. Loss of coastal and inland wetlands, reclamation of mudflats, and pollution threaten stopover and wintering sites these birds depend on. The good news is that we can fix this. Protecting wetlands, salt pans and estuaries, and sharing spaces thoughtfully with people can make a real difference.” Shorebirds worldwide are in decline | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In his new book, Little Stint: A Migrant’s Tale (Neythal Pathipakam), author Byju H explores the bird’s remarkable journey through a blend of science and unconventional storytelling allowing the bird to narrate its own life, beginning with emerging from an egg in the Arctic tundra. “I wanted readers to travel with the bird,” he says adding that the book also highlights the fact that the bird’s ability to navigate vast distances depends on the availability of suitable wetlands along its migratory route.

Ashvin Viswanathan, scientist at Bird Count India , places the little stints as the most visible representatives of a special group of shorebirds that breed in the Arctic. “ This group is declining rapidly due to climate change and loss of habitat. Little stints too are declining in India according to SoIB,” he says, referring to the State of India’s Birds assessment. Their widespread presence, he adds, indicates the health of wetland ecosystems in India as well as conditions in the Arctic. The fact that the little stint is still a fairly common bird does not mean that it is beyond risk. It’s numbers and distribution can help draw attention to changes taking place across the habitats it depends on. The numbers are still over a lakh at Point Calimere wetlands | Photo Credit: S Sivakumar The bird’s preparation for migration is as fascinating as the journey itself. “Before setting off, they enter a phase of intense feeding called hyperphagia. They feed voraciously to build up fat reserves that act as fuel during its journey. This can add 50 to 75 percent to the bird’s body weight. There are also physiological changes, some organs shrink in size as the bird prepares for the demands of sustained flight,” explains Sivakumar adding that India is an important destination along the Central Asian Flyway that connects the bird with wintering habitats further South. The birds can be found along several coastal wetlands, including Point Calimere, Pulicat, parts of Puducherry and Kanyakumari, the Sundarbans, and the mudflats of Gujarat and Maharashtra. Across Tamil Nadu, the species is familiar to birders. “You can spot them at wetlands such as Kurichi and Ukkadam in Coimbatore,” says birder K Selvaganesh adding that the flock plays an important part of the food chain as prey for raptors, including the Western marsh marrier and the brahminy kite. Goa-based Rakesh Dhareshwar, a wildlife photographer says Goa and the wider west coast are reliable places to find them each season. “This year, I was delighted to see them inland too, at Bhigwan in Maharashtra, during a mid-Novemeber trip. However, shorebirds worldwide are in decline. Loss of coastal and inland wetlands, reclamation of mudflats, and pollution threaten stopover and wintering sites these birds depend on. The good news is that we can fix this. Protecting wetlands, salt pans and estuaries, and sharing spaces thoughtfully with people can make a real difference.” Shorebirds worldwide are in decline | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In his new book, Little Stint: A Migrant’s Tale (Neythal Pathipakam), author Byju H explores the bird’s remarkable journey through a blend of science and unconventional storytelling allowing the bird to narrate its own life, beginning with emerging from an egg in the Arctic tundra. “I wanted readers to travel with the bird,” he says adding that the book also highlights the fact that the bird’s ability to navigate vast distances depends on the availability of suitable wetlands along its migratory route.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Skywatchers were treated to a dazzling view as the Beaver Supermoon lit up the night skies on Tuesday (November 24, 2026). The November full moon, known as the Beaver Moon, appears larger and brighter than usual due to its proximity to Earth. Here is more about the celestial display and when you can watch the next supermoon The moon revolves around the Earth in an oval-shaped path (elliptical orbit). A supermoon occurs when the moon rises near perigee (the point in its orbit closest to earth), appearing larger and brighter than usual. This year’s full moon (November 24) is known as the Beaver Supermoon because this is when beavers prepare for the winter and also the time of year to set beaver traps before the swamps and rivers froze. Supermoon appears 14 per cent bigger and 30 per cent brighter than a micromoon, which occurs when a full moon coincides with the moon being near its apogee — the farthest point from Earth in its orbit. The “Beaver moon” is a moniker for November’s full moon adopted by the Old Farmer’s Almanac , supposedly from Algonquian languages once spoken by Native Americans in the New England territory. Though not a rare occurrence, supermoons only happen three to four times a year and always appear consecutively. Because the Moon is in its closest point to Earth, it can cause higher tides than usual, according to NASA. Supermoon is visible to the naked eye wherever skies are clear and no special equipment is required. The next supermoon will be on December 24, 2026. The last supermoon of the year, it will be the largest full moon. The first supermoon of 2027 will be on January 22, also known as the Wolf Supermoon. ‘Wolf moon’ is a traditional name for the first full moon that happens in January. Many full moons have old seasonal names, often popularised in folklore, that helped people keep track of the time of the year before the advent of modern calendars.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Beaver Moon is seen rising in Chandigarh on November 24, 2026. | Photo Credit: SHASHI SHEKHAR KASHYAP

• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Skywatchers were treated to a dazzling view as the Beaver Supermoon lit up the night skies on Tuesday (November 24, 2026). The November full moon, known as the Beaver Moon, appears larger and brighter than usual due to its proximity to Earth. Here is more about the celestial display and when you can watch the next supermoon The moon revolves around the Earth in an oval-shaped path (elliptical orbit). A supermoon occurs when the moon rises near perigee (the point in its orbit closest to earth), appearing larger and brighter than usual. This year’s full moon (November 24) is known as the Beaver Supermoon because this is when beavers prepare for the winter and also the time of year to set beaver traps before the swamps and rivers froze. Supermoon appears 14 per cent bigger and 30 per cent brighter than a micromoon, which occurs when a full moon coincides with the moon being near its apogee — the farthest point from Earth in its orbit. The “Beaver moon” is a moniker for November’s full moon adopted by the Old Farmer’s Almanac , supposedly from Algonquian languages once spoken by Native Americans in the New England territory. Though not a rare occurrence, supermoons only happen three to four times a year and always appear consecutively. Because the Moon is in its closest point to Earth, it can cause higher tides than usual, according to NASA. Supermoon is visible to the naked eye wherever skies are clear and no special equipment is required. The next supermoon will be on December 24, 2026. The last supermoon of the year, it will be the largest full moon. The first supermoon of 2027 will be on January 22, also known as the Wolf Supermoon. ‘Wolf moon’ is a traditional name for the first full moon that happens in January. Many full moons have old seasonal names, often popularised in folklore, that helped people keep track of the time of the year before the advent of modern calendars.

articles.title: All to play for: On the World chess championship in Geneva
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Chess is one sport where both the young and the old can excel

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The World chess championship opened in Geneva with a game worthy of the occasion. Both the defending champion, D. Gukesh, and his challenger, Javokhir Sindarov, produced chess of top quality, and the draw was a just result . Given that the Indian was playing with black pieces and that he had gone into the match as the less favoured of the two, Gukesh could be a little happier with the game than his Uzbek rival. The Chennai Grandmaster was in considerable time trouble on multiple occasions, but managed to solve his problems and found proper answers to the questions posed to him on the board by the confident Sindarov. The match has only begun, and there is plenty of chess left. It is a long match of 14 games, played in the classical time control, and the man who reaches 7.5 points will be the champion. The well-contested opening game would have given Gukesh, and his team comprising his coach and ‘seconds’, enough confidence, after several disappointing performances since he became the youngest World champion in history , at 18, by defeating China’s Ding Liren in Singapore two years ago. That match too had gone down the wire, with Gukesh winning the last of the 14 games, thanks to a terrible mistake towards the end by his rival. Sindarov is just six months older than Gukesh, making the Geneva match the youngest in the 140-year-old history of the World championship: both players are 20. It is remarkable that Gukesh has already seen the highs and lows of life at such a young age. For his opponent, the last one year has been better than a dream: from World No. 26 he has risen to No. 4. Chess is getting younger. The next World championship could also very well have two young contenders. Grandmasters are usually said to peak when they are around 30 and chess is one game that even older players have continued to excel in. Viswanathan Anand was 48 when he won the World rapid chess championship . The match between Gukesh and Sindarov has attracted considerable interest from across the sporting world. After the 1972 match between Boris Spassky and Bobby Fischer — the defining moment of world chess — the World championship has earned a reputation as one of the planet’s most important sporting events. No battle between two of the world’s most talented men in chess has ever disappointed.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: chess / World Chess Championship 2026 / India / Singapore / history

articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Chess is one sport where both the young and the old can excel
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The World chess championship opened in Geneva with a game worthy of the occasion. Both the defending champion, D. Gukesh, and his challenger, Javokhir Sindarov, produced chess of top quality, and the draw was a just result . Given that the Indian was playing with black pieces and that he had gone into the match as the less favoured of the two, Gukesh could be a little happier with the game than his Uzbek rival. The Chennai Grandmaster was in considerable time trouble on multiple occasions, but managed to solve his problems and found proper answers to the questions posed to him on the board by the confident Sindarov. The match has only begun, and there is plenty of chess left. It is a long match of 14 games, played in the classical time control, and the man who reaches 7.5 points will be the champion. The well-contested opening game would have given Gukesh, and his team comprising his coach and ‘seconds’, enough confidence, after several disappointing performances since he became the youngest World champion in history , at 18, by defeating China’s Ding Liren in Singapore two years ago. That match too had gone down the wire, with Gukesh winning the last of the 14 games, thanks to a terrible mistake towards the end by his rival. Sindarov is just six months older than Gukesh, making the Geneva match the youngest in the 140-year-old history of the World championship: both players are 20. It is remarkable that Gukesh has already seen the highs and lows of life at such a young age. For his opponent, the last one year has been better than a dream: from World No. 26 he has risen to No. 4. Chess is getting younger. The next World championship could also very well have two young contenders. Grandmasters are usually said to peak when they are around 30 and chess is one game that even older players have continued to excel in. Viswanathan Anand was 48 when he won the World rapid chess championship . The match between Gukesh and Sindarov has attracted considerable interest from across the sporting world. After the 1972 match between Boris Spassky and Bobby Fischer — the defining moment of world chess — the World championship has earned a reputation as one of the planet’s most important sporting events. No battle between two of the world’s most talented men in chess has ever disappointed.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: chess / World Chess Championship 2026 / India / Singapore / history

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The eligibility criteria and procedures to be followed for CAS will be implemented ‘in strict adherence’ to guidelines issued through a G.O. of January 11, 2021.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Keeping up with its announcement made during the demand for grant on August 24, the Tamil Nadu Higher Education Department issued a Government Order (G.O.) on Tuesday, awarding Career Advancement Scheme (CAS) monetary benefits to teachers of government-aided Arts and Science colleges. According to the G.O., the government has sanctioned ₹11.75 crore as recurring monthly expenditure for awarding CAS to eligible teachers, with effect from September 1. A total of 6,116 teachers will benefit from the scheme. According to the G.O., the eligibility criteria and procedures to be followed for CAS will be implemented “in strict adherence” to guidelines issued through a G.O. of January 11, 2021. The scheme would be implemented only after proper verification of the eligibility of each teacher. A screening and selection committee will scrutinise promotion requests and applications, and the Regional Joint Director will forward the minutes and recommendations to the Director of Collegiate Education. After being vetted, the files would be sent back to the Regional Joint Director who would forward the same, along with service records, to audit teams nominated by the Director-General of Audit. After receiving the observations from the audit teams, the Regional Joint Director would issue relevant CAS orders.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The G.O. warns that the responsibility of any miscalculation or error would fall squarely on the officer who issues the CAS order. The excess amount paid will be recovered from the teacher, while action will be initiated against erring officials.

• 1. Core Context & Background: The eligibility criteria and procedures to be followed for CAS will be implemented ‘in strict adherence’ to guidelines issued through a G.O. of January 11, 2021.
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Keeping up with its announcement made during the demand for grant on August 24, the Tamil Nadu Higher Education Department issued a Government Order (G.O.) on Tuesday, awarding Career Advancement Scheme (CAS) monetary benefits to teachers of government-aided Arts and Science colleges. According to the G.O., the government has sanctioned ₹11.75 crore as recurring monthly expenditure for awarding CAS to eligible teachers, with effect from September 1. A total of 6,116 teachers will benefit from the scheme. According to the G.O., the eligibility criteria and procedures to be followed for CAS will be implemented “in strict adherence” to guidelines issued through a G.O. of January 11, 2021. The scheme would be implemented only after proper verification of the eligibility of each teacher. A screening and selection committee will scrutinise promotion requests and applications, and the Regional Joint Director will forward the minutes and recommendations to the Director of Collegiate Education. After being vetted, the files would be sent back to the Regional Joint Director who would forward the same, along with service records, to audit teams nominated by the Director-General of Audit. After receiving the observations from the audit teams, the Regional Joint Director would issue relevant CAS orders.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The G.O. warns that the responsibility of any miscalculation or error would fall squarely on the officer who issues the CAS order. The excess amount paid will be recovered from the teacher, while action will be initiated against erring officials.

articles.title: Man arrested for murdering his wife over family dispute
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: A 31-year-old man was arrested by the Sathuvachari police in Vellore on Wednesday for killing his wife over a family dispute.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Police identified the arrested person as K. Hariprasad. Initial inquiry revealed that Hariprasad was married to Krithika nearly a decade ago. The couple has two children. Police said that Hariprasad was working as a driver. The couple reportedly fought repeatedly over poor income to maintain the family. In recent months, police said that Hariprasad was also irregular at work, forcing Krithika to meet the entire needs of the family on her own. Police said that Krithika left her husband and stayed in her parents house with her children. Hariprasad repeatedly requested her live with him but she refused. Police said on Wednesday, Hariprasad met her again and asked to come along with him to his house. As she refused, enraged Hariprasad stabbed Krithika, who collapsed in a pool of blood, police said.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Based on an alert from neighbours, the Sathuvachari police rushed to the spot and arrested Hariprasad. A case was registered and further probe is under way.

1. Core Context & Background: A 31-year-old man was arrested by the Sathuvachari police in Vellore on Wednesday for killing his wife over a family dispute.

In recent months, police said that Hariprasad was also irregular at work, forcing Krithika to meet the entire needs of the family on her own. Police said that Krithika left her husband and stayed in her parents house with her children. Hariprasad repeatedly requested her live with him but she refused. Police said on Wednesday, Hariprasad met her again and asked to come along with him to his house. As she refused, enraged Hariprasad stabbed Krithika, who collapsed in a pool of blood, police said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Based on an alert from neighbours, the Sathuvachari police rushed to the spot and arrested Hariprasad. A case was registered and further probe is under way.

articles.title: Burglars decamp with 15 sovereigns of gold, cash from house near Jolarpet
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Burglars decamped with 15 sovereigns of gold jewellery, and around ₹1.2 lakh in cash from the house of a tribal family near Jolarpet town in Tirupattur on Wednesday.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Police identified the victim as R. Siva, who belongs to the Irular community. He was living with his wife and son on the outskirts of the town. Siva went to Tiruvannamalai town for Maha Deepam day as part of Karthigai Deepam festival. When he returned home around 2 a.m., Siva opened the main entrance of the house and found cupboards in the living room and the bedroom door were broken. Police said that gold ornaments and cash kept in the cupboards were missing. The rear door of the house was damaged to gain access to the house. Based on the alert, the Jolarpet police inspected the spot.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Police said sniffer dogs and fingerprint experts were roped. Footage from CCTV cameras in the house and on the route were taken to identify suspects. A case was registered and special teams were formed to nab the suspects. Further probe is under way.

articles.title: Over 600 tonnes of waste generated on Maha Deepam day removed in Tiruvannamalai
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Most of the collected wastes would be dumped at the 15 acre-landfill site near the Girivalam path

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: More than 2,400 sanitary workers removed over 600 tonnes of garbage that was generated on Maha Deepam day. Officials of Tiruvannamalai Corporation said that apart from the civic body, sanitary workers of District Rural Development Agency (DRDA) were also roped in for the mammoth exercise, which was started on Monday, a day before Maha Deepam as the town witnessed steady flow of pilgrims. “Rain also delayed removal of garbage on streets and the Girivalam Path. Nonetheless, sanitary workers worked round-the-clock, in shifts, to keep the town clean of wastes,” K. Balasubramanian, Corporation Commissioner, told The Hindu. Apart from sanitary staff from Tiruvannamalai Corporation, civic workers from big municipalities such as Ambur, Arcot, Arani, Arakkonam, Polur, Vandavasi, Vaniyambadi, and Gudiyatham were also roped in for the purpose. Along with Corporation Commissioner Mr. Balasubramanian, Collector Vandhana Garg inspected the work and interacted with sanitary workers. Corporation officials said that waste generated on Maha Deepam day this year was the highest (600 metric tonnes) as against that generated in 2025 (450 metric tonnes), 2024 (350 metric tonnes), and 2023 (210 metric tonnes), due to increase in footfall. Around 45 lakh devotees visited the town on Maha Deepam day. Disposable food plates formed the majority of waste, followed by those of sugarcane and sweet corn. District administration has allowed 250 individuals and organisations for annadhanam (free food). Many volunteers and groups were also provided free food on the day.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Most of the collected wastes would be dumped at the 15 acre-landfill site of the civic body near the Girivalam path. Food and other organic wastes would be recycled to make manure for farming and terrace gardens in Tiruvannamalai.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (26 NOV)

📰 Over 600 tonnes of waste generated on Maha Deepam day removed in Tiruvannamalai

📌 Published: 26 Nov 2026, 12:32:59 AM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Most of the collected wastes would be dumped at the 15 acre-landfill site near the Girivalam path

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: More than 2,400 sanitary workers removed over 600 tonnes of garbage that was generated on Maha Deepam day. Officials of Tiruvannamalai Corporation said that apart from the civic body, sanitary workers of District Rural Development Agency (DRDA) were also roped in for the mammoth exercise, which was started on Monday, a day before Maha Deepam as the town witnessed steady flow of pilgrims. “Rain also delayed removal of garbage on streets and the Girivalam Path. Nonetheless, sanitary workers worked round-the-clock, in shifts, to keep the town clean of wastes,” K. Balasubramanian, Corporation Commissioner, told The Hindu. Apart from sanitary staff from Tiruvannamalai Corporation, civic workers from big municipalities such as Ambur, Arcot, Arani, Arakkonam, Polur, Vandavasi, Vaniyambadi, and Gudiyatham were also roped in for the purpose. Along with Corporation Commissioner Mr. Balasubramanian, Collector Vandhana Garg inspected the work and interacted with sanitary workers. Corporation officials said that waste generated on Maha Deepam day this year was the highest (600 metric tonnes) as against that generated in 2025 (450 metric tonnes), 2024 (350 metric tonnes), and 2023 (210 metric tonnes), due to increase in footfall. Around 45 lakh devotees visited the town on Maha Deepam day. Disposable food plates formed the majority of waste, followed by those of sugarcane and sweet corn. District administration has allowed 250 individuals and organisations for annadhanam (free food). Many volunteers and groups were also provided free food on the day.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Most of the collected wastes would be dumped at the 15 acre-landfill site of the civic body near the Girivalam path. Food and other organic wastes would be recycled to make manure for farming and terrace gardens in Tiruvannamalai.

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Over 600 tonnes of waste generated on Maha Deepam day removed in Tiruvannamalai", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Most of the collected wastes would be dumped at the 15 acre-landfill site near the Girivalam path.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Over 600 tonnes of waste generated on Maha Deepa' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.

✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Most of the collected wastes would be dumped at the 15 acre-landfill site near the Girivalam path."

articles.title: Large-sized pancreatic stones removed via keyhole surgery
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: A 41-year-old male patient got relief from debilitating pain after large-sized pancreatic stones measuring up to 3 cm were removed through laparoscopic surgery at a city hospital. The patient, who was diagnosed with acute-on-chronic calcific pancreatitis accompanied by pancreatic diabetes, had severely atrophic pancreas.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A team of surgeons led by surgical gastroenterologist and director at GEM Hospital P. Senthilnathan extracted the calculi with zero abdominal scars or stitches. The patient was discharged just four days after the surgery. Speaking to presspersons on Wednesday, he said that in chronic calcific pancreatitis, stones accumulate in the central duct and cause severe blockages, excruciating pain, and secondary diabetes. “If left untreated, chronic inflammation can even increase the risk of pancreatic cancer. While smaller stones can be managed medically or endoscopically, large stones require surgery.“ The pancreas was choked with dozens of stones, including giant calculi measuring 3 cm x 1 cm lodged across the head, neck, and tail of the main pancreatic duct, and stones up to 2 cm x 2 cm trapped inside the minor duct, he added.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: As these stones sit dangerously close to major blood vessels, they must be extracted without fracturing or damaging the surrounding tissue, which is why such cases are almost universally managed through traditional open surgery, Dr. Senthilnathan added.

Core Context & Background: A 41-year-old male patient got relief from debilitating pain after large-sized pancreatic stones measuring up to 3 cm were removed through laparoscopic surgery at a city hospital. The patient, who was diagnosed with acute-on-chronic calcific pancreatitis accompanied by pancreatic diabetes, had severely atrophic pancreas.
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A team of surgeons led by surgical gastroenterologist and director at GEM Hospital P. Senthilnathan extracted the calculi with zero abdominal scars or stitches. The patient was discharged just four days after the surgery. Speaking to presspersons on Wednesday, he said that in chronic calcific pancreatitis, stones accumulate in the central duct and cause severe blockages, excruciating pain, and secondary diabetes. “If left untreated, chronic inflammation can even increase the risk of pancreatic cancer. While smaller stones can be managed medically or endoscopically, large stones require surgery.“ The pancreas was choked with dozens of stones, including giant calculi measuring 3 cm x 1 cm lodged across the head, neck, and tail of the main pancreatic duct, and stones up to 2 cm x 2 cm trapped inside the minor duct, he added.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: As these stones sit dangerously close to major blood vessels, they must be extracted without fracturing or damaging the surrounding tissue, which is why such cases are almost universally managed through traditional open surgery, Dr. Senthilnathan added.

fullParagraphs: 1. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The declaration calls for early screening for sarcopenia, setting protein intake targets, regular strength exercise and early mobilisation and rehabilitation after illness, including post-intensive care follow-up. It also emphasises professional education, India-specific research and the development of diagnostic cut-offs suited to Indian populations. It urges policymakers to include sarcopenia in national healthy-ageing and non-communicable disease programmes, particularly focusing on rural and low-income communities. Sarcopenia is the progressive loss of muscle mass, strength and function. It can occur with ageing and is accelerated by inadequate nutrition, physical inactivity and chronic diseases. It increases the risk of falls, fractures, disability, delayed recovery from illness or surgery and loss of independence. Doctors at the summit cited data showing that 43.6% of Indians aged 60 and above have sarcopenia, with 19.4% having its severe form. They noted that the condition also affects younger people, particularly those with chronic illnesses, poor nutrition and sedentary lifestyles.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The summit featured talks by specialists in surgical gastroenterology, critical care and nutrition.

articles.title: Spinning wheels: on urban mobility in Karnataka
articles.examRelevance: UPSC, State PSC, SSC & Banking Mains: Deep Analytical Core Summary, Policy Critique, 4 Hinglish Vocab & 2 Analytical Questions
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Karnataka needs a coherent policy on urban mobility

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: While Karnataka has spent years disputing motorcycle owners’ right to carry paying passengers, Bengaluru — with the dubious distinction of having one of the world’s highest travel times per unit distance — struggles with inadequate public transport capacity and lacklustre intermediate options. The Supreme Court ruling on November 20 to dismiss Karnataka’s appeal was thus straightforward, allowing motorcycles to be registered as transport vehicles. The State has often called bike taxis unsafe, yet has not improved the prospects of safer options. Earlier this year, the Centre for Science and Environment estimated the number of buses in urban centres nationwide to be 70% short of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs benchmark and that 400 cities with populations between a lakh and 10 lakh altogether lacked organised bus services. In March, the BMTC reported a fleet of around 7,000 buses in Bengaluru, versus the 13,000 by 2025 envisaged by the Comprehensive Mobility Plan. Expanding the number of Metro stations also creates more demand for travel to and from stations, but the operating costs of the public transport corporation expected to serve that demand are not covered by the resulting increase in rail ridership. Overall, Karnataka has struggled to set up a consistent transport policy. An expert committee recommended against bike taxis in Bengaluru for first- and last-mile connectivity and in favour of better walking infrastructure and bicycle rentals in 2019, only for the State to launch the electric bike-taxi scheme in 2021, then rescind it in 2024 over safety concerns and drivers’ disputes. The market for short booked journeys is also dysfunctional. But while allowing bike taxis could temper autorickshaw fares, the State must investigate drivers’ operating costs, the difference between the paid and the received amounts, and prevent large platforms from exploiting the market. Finally, while the Union Road Transport Ministry has reported that 46.2% of all road deaths involved two-wheeler users, two-wheelers’ safety relative to autorickshaws and cabs, by the number and distance of journeys, is unclear. The State should require aggregators to report injuries and fatalities and investigate the consequences of drivers’ earnings being linked to the number of trips undertaken. The Union government’s 2025 Motor Vehicle Aggregator Guidelines already address passenger security, fares, and insurance while allowing States to authorise privately registered motorcycles through aggregators. Karnataka should exercise this additional power. A large national programme is required to address funding for public transport, which is necessary even when it is not immediately profitable.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Karnataka / scooters and motorbikes / public transport / court / population / urban planning / Bengaluru Metro / Electric vehicles / road accident / road transport / insurance
