महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'International' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Impartiality (Adjective / Verb)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Impartiality' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Consecutive (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Consecutive' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Devotees barred from Tirupparankundram hill for the second consecutive day and heavy security deployed."

articles.title: CMRL-Exalogic payoff case: Kerala HC extends stay on probe against Pinarayi Vijayan, kin
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Court was considering appeals by Vijayan, daughter T. Veena and son-in-law and former Public Works Minister P.A. Mohamed Riyas against a Single Bench order, directing registration of FIR

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Kerala High Court has extended the stay on the investigation and the First Information Report (FIR) registered against Keralam Leader of Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan and kin in the CMRL-Exalogic payoff case. A Division Bench of Justices Devan Ramachandran and V.M. Syam Kumar extended the interim stay granted earlier and adjourned the matter to December 15. Previously, the court had stayed the FIR and the investigation, stating that the matter required a detailed hearing. The court was considering the appeals filed by Mr. Vijayan, daughter T. Veena and son-in-law and former Public Works Minister P.A. Mohamed Riyas against a Single Bench order, directing the registration of an FIR in the pay-off case. The Single Bench had observed that an offence was prima facie made out in the letter given by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to the State Police Chief, which allegedly contained details of a predicate offence under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 against the accused. The ED was investigating the payoff case under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002. The accused argued that a cognisable offence could not be derived from the information passed on by the ED. They quoted the letter, which stated that “the transactions stopped at Ms. Veena” and that “it could be either Mr. Vijayan or Mr. Riyas” who was involved. They argued that there could be no “either or” in criminal law, and that the State could not launch a preliminary enquiry, if there was no credible information.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: ALSO WATCH ED seeks fresh FIR against Pinarayi Vijayan, family in Exalogic-CMRL case

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 CMRL-Exalogic payoff case: Kerala HC extends stay on probe against Pinarayi Vijayan, kin

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 03:18:11 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Court was considering appeals by Vijayan, daughter T. Veena and son-in-law and former Public Works Minister P.A. Mohamed Riyas against a Single Bench order, directing registration of FIR

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Kerala High Court has extended the stay on the investigation and the First Information Report (FIR) registered against Keralam Leader of Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan and kin in the CMRL-Exalogic payoff case. A Division Bench of Justices Devan Ramachandran and V.M. Syam Kumar extended the interim stay granted earlier and adjourned the matter to December 15. Previously, the court had stayed the FIR and the investigation, stating that the matter required a detailed hearing. The court was considering the appeals filed by Mr. Vijayan, daughter T. Veena and son-in-law and former Public Works Minister P.A. Mohamed Riyas against a Single Bench order, directing the registration of an FIR in the pay-off case. The Single Bench had observed that an offence was prima facie made out in the letter given by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) to the State Police Chief, which allegedly contained details of a predicate offence under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 against the accused. The ED was investigating the payoff case under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002. The accused argued that a cognisable offence could not be derived from the information passed on by the ED. They quoted the letter, which stated that “the transactions stopped at Ms. Veena” and that “it could be either Mr. Vijayan or Mr. Riyas” who was involved. They argued that there could be no “either or” in criminal law, and that the State could not launch a preliminary enquiry, if there was no credible information.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: ALSO WATCH ED seeks fresh FIR against Pinarayi Vijayan, family in Exalogic-CMRL case

✓ Syn: Foreseeably, Expectedly, Inevitably  |  ✖ Ant: Unexpectedly, Surprisingly, Abruptly

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Investigation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Registration (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Registration' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

"We aren't begging", Congress Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee chief Masood said after the Samajwadi Party announced candidates for five seats.

articles.title: Keralam CM Satheesan says he too is victim of online attacks, alleges ‘important individual’ behind fake news campaign
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: On the internal conflicts within the Congress involving MPs Rajmohan Unnithan and Shafi Parambil, Satheesan said he did not wish to comment on “organisational matters”

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) said that he himself was a victim of online attacks, and that an “important individual” was behind the dissemination of such fake news. At a post-Cabinet press briefing, Mr. Satheesan was responding to questions on the online attacks on Congress party leaders and members of the late former Chief Minister Oommen Chandy ’s family. Mr. Satheesan also displayed copies of social media cards with his photograph which purportedly claim that the government had decided to discontinue the welfare pensions and another attributed to Chandy Oommen that Mr. Satheesan was among the individuals who had caused anguish to his father and Oommen Chandy. “Many such fake news were are being spread in the name of mainstream media organisations,” he said. “All this comes from one centre, led by an important individual,” he said, but declined to name the person. On the internal conflicts within the Congress involving MPs Rajmohan Unnithan and Shafi Parambil, Mr. Satheesan said he did not wish to comment on “organisational matters.” Such questions should be posed to KPCC president Sunny Joseph, he said. Mr. Satheesan said the discussions regarding appointments to the top posts of boards and corporations under the State government were in the final stages. Mr. Satheesan’s response came amid criticism from within the Congress party and UDF constituents such as the Revolutionary Socialist Party (RSP) that the appointments were not finalised even after the UDF government had completed six months in power. Mr. Satheesan said the appointments would be made soon and the talks were in the final stages. On Monday, after a State secretariat meeting of the RSP, its leader N.K. Premachandran had sharply criticised the delay and also the “absence” of regular meetings of the UDF. The RSP also wanted the appointments to be completed, if possible, this month itself.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: On his part, Mr. Satheesan sought to play down the RSP leader’s remarks, saying that it was not criticism as such, and that the party merely wanted the board, corporation division completed quickly.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #11 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Keralam CM Satheesan says he too is victim of online attacks, alleges ‘important individual’ behind fake news campaign

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 03:16:31 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: On the internal conflicts within the Congress involving MPs Rajmohan Unnithan and Shafi Parambil, Satheesan said he did not wish to comment on “organisational matters”

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) said that he himself was a victim of online attacks, and that an “important individual” was behind the dissemination of such fake news. At a post-Cabinet press briefing, Mr. Satheesan was responding to questions on the online attacks on Congress party leaders and members of the late former Chief Minister Oommen Chandy ’s family. Mr. Satheesan also displayed copies of social media cards with his photograph which purportedly claim that the government had decided to discontinue the welfare pensions and another attributed to Chandy Oommen that Mr. Satheesan was among the individuals who had caused anguish to his father and Oommen Chandy. “Many such fake news were are being spread in the name of mainstream media organisations,” he said. “All this comes from one centre, led by an important individual,” he said, but declined to name the person. On the internal conflicts within the Congress involving MPs Rajmohan Unnithan and Shafi Parambil, Mr. Satheesan said he did not wish to comment on “organisational matters.” Such questions should be posed to KPCC president Sunny Joseph, he said. Mr. Satheesan said the discussions regarding appointments to the top posts of boards and corporations under the State government were in the final stages. Mr. Satheesan’s response came amid criticism from within the Congress party and UDF constituents such as the Revolutionary Socialist Party (RSP) that the appointments were not finalised even after the UDF government had completed six months in power. Mr. Satheesan said the appointments would be made soon and the talks were in the final stages. On Monday, after a State secretariat meeting of the RSP, its leader N.K. Premachandran had sharply criticised the delay and also the “absence” of regular meetings of the UDF. The RSP also wanted the appointments to be completed, if possible, this month itself.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: On his part, Mr. Satheesan sought to play down the RSP leader’s remarks, saying that it was not criticism as such, and that the party merely wanted the board, corporation division completed quickly.

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Dissemination' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
Corporation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Corporation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

Q1. ✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. articles.title: Missing patient at Thrissur MCH found dead in washroom 36 hours later
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The body of a patient who had gone missing from a ward at Thrissur Medical College Hospital was found inside a washroom nearly 36 hours later.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The deceased was identified as Makutti Ravuthar, 79, a native of Nenmara in Palakkad. He went missing from ward 11 on November 19 around 9 p.m. Though the ward staff alerted the hospital authorities and lodged a complaint with the Medical College police, he could not be traced. Eventually, his body was found in the washroom on the morning of November 21. Sanitation workers grew suspicious after noticing that a washroom had remained shut from inside for an unusually long period, following which they alerted the security staff, who forced open the door. A post-mortem examination report attributed the death to a heart attack that had occurred around 36 hours earlier. He had been admitted on November 16 with a respiratory illness and had no bystanders. A thorough investigation has been sought into the matter, with the Medical College police also registering a case.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Former Health Minister K.K. Shailaja described the incident as a case of negligence and demanded stern action.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Missing patient at Thrissur MCH found dead in washroom 36 hours later

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 03:10:10 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The body of a patient who had gone missing from a ward at Thrissur Medical College Hospital was found inside a washroom nearly 36 hours later.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The deceased was identified as Makutti Ravuthar, 79, a native of Nenmara in Palakkad. He went missing from ward 11 on November 19 around 9 p.m. Though the ward staff alerted the hospital authorities and lodged a complaint with the Medical College police, he could not be traced. Eventually, his body was found in the washroom on the morning of November 21. Sanitation workers grew suspicious after noticing that a washroom had remained shut from inside for an unusually long period, following which they alerted the security staff, who forced open the door. A post-mortem examination report attributed the death to a heart attack that had occurred around 36 hours earlier. He had been admitted on November 16 with a respiratory illness and had no bystanders. A thorough investigation has been sought into the matter, with the Medical College police also registering a case.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Former Health Minister K.K. Shailaja described the incident as a case of negligence and demanded stern action.

articles.title: Air passenger services see 35% inflation in Q2; banking, securities transaction witness deflation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Commerce and Industry Ministry released the provisional Service Producer Price Indices (PPI) for the second quarter of 2026-27

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Air passenger services recorded 35.52% inflation in the July-September quarter, recording the highest rate of price rise among the seven major services for which the inflation data was released on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). Securities transaction services and banking services, however, recorded a deflation of 6.93% and 3.96% respectively, the provisional Service Producer Price Indices (PPI) for the second quarter of 2026-27 released by the Commerce and Industry Ministry showed. The PPI has inflation data for seven major services — Banking, Securities Transaction, Insurance, Management of Pension Funds, Railways, Air (Passenger), and Telecom — with base year 2022-23. Service PPI measures the change in the average prices received by producers on production of a service. As per the data, inflation in Air (Passenger) Services rose 35.52% YoY in the second quarter, compared to 31.94% in the first quarter. Annual inflation in the railway passenger service price index rose 2.17% during the September quarter, lower than 3.50% in the June quarter. Inflation in 'Banking Service Contribution' was 3.86% in Q2 of FY27, higher than 2.62% in Q1. The 'Banking Service Price' witnessed 3.96% deflation in Q2, vis-a-vis 4.98% deflation in Q1. Securities Transaction Service Prices saw a deflation of 6.93% in Q2, compared to 1.32% deflation in June quarter. Pension fund management, insurance and telecom services recorded an inflation of 1.01%, 0.49% and 0.54%, respectively in September quarter, compared to 5.48%, 0.98% and 0.72%, respectively in the June quarter.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The government would eventually include more services in the Service PPI data.

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #16 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Air passenger services see 35% inflation in Q2; banking, securities transaction witness deflation

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 03:21:19 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Commerce and Industry Ministry released the provisional Service Producer Price Indices (PPI) for the second quarter of 2026-27

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Air passenger services recorded 35.52% inflation in the July-September quarter, recording the highest rate of price rise among the seven major services for which the inflation data was released on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). Securities transaction services and banking services, however, recorded a deflation of 6.93% and 3.96% respectively, the provisional Service Producer Price Indices (PPI) for the second quarter of 2026-27 released by the Commerce and Industry Ministry showed. The PPI has inflation data for seven major services — Banking, Securities Transaction, Insurance, Management of Pension Funds, Railways, Air (Passenger), and Telecom — with base year 2022-23. Service PPI measures the change in the average prices received by producers on production of a service. As per the data, inflation in Air (Passenger) Services rose 35.52% YoY in the second quarter, compared to 31.94% in the first quarter. Annual inflation in the railway passenger service price index rose 2.17% during the September quarter, lower than 3.50% in the June quarter. Inflation in 'Banking Service Contribution' was 3.86% in Q2 of FY27, higher than 2.62% in Q1. The 'Banking Service Price' witnessed 3.96% deflation in Q2, vis-a-vis 4.98% deflation in Q1. Securities Transaction Service Prices saw a deflation of 6.93% in Q2, compared to 1.32% deflation in June quarter. Pension fund management, insurance and telecom services recorded an inflation of 1.01%, 0.49% and 0.54%, respectively in September quarter, compared to 5.48%, 0.98% and 0.72%, respectively in the June quarter.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The government would eventually include more services in the Service PPI data.

महंगाई (मुद्रास्फीति) — जब बाज़ार में वस्तुओं के दाम बढ़ें और रुपये की खरीद शक्ति कम हो जाए।
✓ Syn: Price-escalation, Hyperinflation, Dearness  |  ✖ Ant: Deflation, Disinflation, Recession

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Contribution' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Provisional (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Provisional' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Transaction (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Transaction' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 📈 Economic, Banking & Finance passage on "Air passenger services see 35% inflation in Q2; banking, securities transaction witness deflation", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The Commerce and Industry Ministry released the provisional Service Producer Price Indices (PPI) for the second quarter of 2026-27.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Air passenger services see 35% inflation in Q2; ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Air passenger services see 35% inflation in Q' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Air passenger services see 35% inflation in Q' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The Commerce and Industry Ministry released the provisional Service Producer Price Indices (PPI) for the second quarter of 2026-27."
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Air passenger services see 35% inflation in Q2; banking, securities transaction witness deflation"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The government would eventually include more services in the Service PPI data.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The government would eventually include more services in the Service PPI data."

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: PCD is a rare genetic disorder that affects the cilia, which help move mucus and other particles out of the respiratory tract. Mucus is therefore not cleared effectively and builds up in the respiratory tract, increasing the risk of recurrent infections

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a rare inherited disorder that affects tiny, hair-like structures in the body called cilia. When these structures fail to move properly, mucus and bacteria accumulate in the airways, increasing the risk of recurrent respiratory infections and long-term lung damage.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: While there is currently no cure, early diagnosis and regular treatment can help manage symptoms and preserve lung function. Recent research into the genetic causes of PCD is also offering new insights into the disease and its diagnosis.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #29 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 All you need to know about: Primary ciliary dyskinesia

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 03:52:27 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: PCD is a rare genetic disorder that affects the cilia, which help move mucus and other particles out of the respiratory tract. Mucus is therefore not cleared effectively and builds up in the respiratory tract, increasing the risk of recurrent infections

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is a rare inherited disorder that affects tiny, hair-like structures in the body called cilia. When these structures fail to move properly, mucus and bacteria accumulate in the airways, increasing the risk of recurrent respiratory infections and long-term lung damage.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: While there is currently no cure, early diagnosis and regular treatment can help manage symptoms and preserve lung function. Recent research into the genetic causes of PCD is also offering new insights into the disease and its diagnosis.

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The November full moon, known as the Beaver Moon, appears larger and brighter than usual due to its proximity to Earth

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Skywatchers were treated to a dazzling view as the Beaver Supermoon lit up the night skies on Tuesday (November 24, 2026). The November full moon, known as the Beaver Moon, appears larger and brighter than usual due to its proximity to Earth. Here is more about the celestial display and when you can watch the next supermoon The moon revolves around the Earth in an oval-shaped path (elliptical orbit). A supermoon occurs when the moon rises near perigee (the point in its orbit closest to earth), appearing larger and brighter than usual. This year’s full moon (November 24) is known as the Beaver Supermoon because this is when beavers prepare for the winter and also the time of year to set beaver traps before the swamps and rivers froze. Supermoon appears 14 per cent bigger and 30 per cent brighter than a micromoon, which occurs when a full moon coincides with the moon being near its apogee — the farthest point from Earth in its orbit. The “Beaver moon” is a moniker for November’s full moon adopted by the Old Farmer’s Almanac , supposedly from Algonquian languages once spoken by Native Americans in the New England territory. Though not a rare occurrence, supermoons only happen three to four times a year and always appear consecutively. Because the Moon is in its closest point to Earth, it can cause higher tides than usual, according to NASA. Supermoon is visible to the naked eye wherever skies are clear and no special equipment is required. The next supermoon will be on December 24, 2026. The last supermoon of the year, it will be the largest full moon. The first supermoon of 2027 will be on January 22, also known as the Wolf Supermoon. ‘Wolf moon’ is a traditional name for the first full moon that happens in January. Many full moons have old seasonal names, often popularised in folklore, that helped people keep track of the time of the year before the advent of modern calendars.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Beaver Moon is seen rising in Chandigarh on November 24, 2026. | Photo Credit: SHASHI SHEKHAR KASHYAP

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 What is Beaver Supermoon, when is the next supermoon and more

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 04:06:07 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The November full moon, known as the Beaver Moon, appears larger and brighter than usual due to its proximity to Earth

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Skywatchers were treated to a dazzling view as the Beaver Supermoon lit up the night skies on Tuesday (November 24, 2026). The November full moon, known as the Beaver Moon, appears larger and brighter than usual due to its proximity to Earth. Here is more about the celestial display and when you can watch the next supermoon The moon revolves around the Earth in an oval-shaped path (elliptical orbit). A supermoon occurs when the moon rises near perigee (the point in its orbit closest to earth), appearing larger and brighter than usual. This year’s full moon (November 24) is known as the Beaver Supermoon because this is when beavers prepare for the winter and also the time of year to set beaver traps before the swamps and rivers froze. Supermoon appears 14 per cent bigger and 30 per cent brighter than a micromoon, which occurs when a full moon coincides with the moon being near its apogee — the farthest point from Earth in its orbit. The “Beaver moon” is a moniker for November’s full moon adopted by the Old Farmer’s Almanac , supposedly from Algonquian languages once spoken by Native Americans in the New England territory. Though not a rare occurrence, supermoons only happen three to four times a year and always appear consecutively. Because the Moon is in its closest point to Earth, it can cause higher tides than usual, according to NASA. Supermoon is visible to the naked eye wherever skies are clear and no special equipment is required. The next supermoon will be on December 24, 2026. The last supermoon of the year, it will be the largest full moon. The first supermoon of 2027 will be on January 22, also known as the Wolf Supermoon. ‘Wolf moon’ is a traditional name for the first full moon that happens in January. Many full moons have old seasonal names, often popularised in folklore, that helped people keep track of the time of the year before the advent of modern calendars.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Beaver Moon is seen rising in Chandigarh on November 24, 2026. | Photo Credit: SHASHI SHEKHAR KASHYAP

articles.title: Karnataka CM in Japan: Kawasaki to invest up to ₹800 crore in State over 10 years
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Expansion of Harohalli plant to create 600 jobs; Chief Minister-led delegation also holds talks with Panasonic Automotive

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Japanese industrial major Kawasaki Heavy Industries has committed to invest up to ₹800 crore over 10 years to expand Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery Pvt. Ltd. at Harohalli Industrial Area in Karnataka. The expansion is expected to generate around 600 manufacturing jobs. A memorandum of understanding (MoU) was signed in Tokyo in the presence of Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Minister for Large and Medium Industries and Infrastructure Development M.B. Patil. The agreement was exchanged by Principal Secretary, Commerce and Industries Department, S. Selvakumar, Kawasaki Heavy Industries representative Kenji Matsushita and Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery CEO Minoru Hatsuda. The proposed facility will manufacture hydraulic pumps, swing motors and related components for the construction equipment industry. The investment will be taken up in two phases. Established in Bengaluru in 2012, Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery has become a major player in India’s excavator hydraulic pump market. The expansion is expected to strengthen Karnataka’s construction equipment and capital goods ecosystem. The State government has assured the company of assistance with land allotment, approvals, clearances and applicable incentives. The Chief MInister and Mr. Patil also invited Kawasaki’s leadership to participate in the Global Investors Meet — Invest Karnataka 2027, scheduled to be held in Bengaluru from April 20 to 22. Karnataka has attracted 101 Japanese greenfield projects since 2016, with more than 525 Japanese establishments currently operating in the State, according to an official release. The Chief Minister and Mr. Patil also met the leadership of Panasonic Automotive in Japan, led by its president and CEO, Mike Nagayasu. The discussions focused on Karnataka’s strengths in advanced manufacturing and Global Capability Centres (GCCs), and the possibility of the company expanding its operations in the State. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Minister M.B. Patil with Mike Nagayasu, president and CEO of Panasonic Automotive in Japan, on November 25, 2026. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The delegation invited the company to participate in the Global Investors Meet 2027.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Karnataka CM in Japan: Kawasaki to invest up to ₹800 crore in State over 10 years

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 04:17:14 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Expansion of Harohalli plant to create 600 jobs; Chief Minister-led delegation also holds talks with Panasonic Automotive

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Japanese industrial major Kawasaki Heavy Industries has committed to invest up to ₹800 crore over 10 years to expand Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery Pvt. Ltd. at Harohalli Industrial Area in Karnataka. The expansion is expected to generate around 600 manufacturing jobs. A memorandum of understanding (MoU) was signed in Tokyo in the presence of Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Minister for Large and Medium Industries and Infrastructure Development M.B. Patil. The agreement was exchanged by Principal Secretary, Commerce and Industries Department, S. Selvakumar, Kawasaki Heavy Industries representative Kenji Matsushita and Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery CEO Minoru Hatsuda. The proposed facility will manufacture hydraulic pumps, swing motors and related components for the construction equipment industry. The investment will be taken up in two phases. Established in Bengaluru in 2012, Wipro Kawasaki Precision Machinery has become a major player in India’s excavator hydraulic pump market. The expansion is expected to strengthen Karnataka’s construction equipment and capital goods ecosystem. The State government has assured the company of assistance with land allotment, approvals, clearances and applicable incentives. The Chief MInister and Mr. Patil also invited Kawasaki’s leadership to participate in the Global Investors Meet — Invest Karnataka 2027, scheduled to be held in Bengaluru from April 20 to 22. Karnataka has attracted 101 Japanese greenfield projects since 2016, with more than 525 Japanese establishments currently operating in the State, according to an official release. The Chief Minister and Mr. Patil also met the leadership of Panasonic Automotive in Japan, led by its president and CEO, Mike Nagayasu. The discussions focused on Karnataka’s strengths in advanced manufacturing and Global Capability Centres (GCCs), and the possibility of the company expanding its operations in the State. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Minister M.B. Patil with Mike Nagayasu, president and CEO of Panasonic Automotive in Japan, on November 25, 2026. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The delegation invited the company to participate in the Global Investors Meet 2027.

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Karnataka CM in Japan: Kawasaki to invest up to ₹800 crore in State over 10 years", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Expansion of Harohalli plant to create 600 jobs; Chief Minister-led delegation also holds talks with Panasonic Automotive.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Karnataka CM in Japan: Kawasaki to invest up to ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Karnataka CM in Japan: Kawasaki to invest up ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Karnataka CM in Japan: Kawasaki to invest up ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Expansion of Harohalli plant to create 600 jobs; Chief Minister-led delegation also holds talks with Panasonic Automotive."
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Karnataka CM in Japan: Kawasaki to invest up to ₹800 crore in State over 10 years"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. The delegation invited the company to participate in the Global Investors Meet 2027.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "The delegation invited the company to participate in the Global Investors Meet 2027."

articles.title: FSSAI’s pan-India enforcement drive on packaged drinking water, lab test to take 1-2 months: CEO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The regulator has widened the scope of its scrutiny after a sample of Bisleri packaged drinking water failed the lab test

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: FSSAI CEO Rajit Punhani on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) said the food regulator is collecting samples of packaged drinking water from across the country and lab testing will be complete in around two months. He also announced that FSSAI would soon start inspection of 'packaging materials' used for food items, saying those should be 'food grade'. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has widened the scope of its scrutiny after a sample of Bisleri packaged drinking water failed the lab test. The regulator has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International. When asked about its enforcement drive against packaged drinking water, Mr. Punhani said, "We are in the process. The process has started. We are doing all over the country." On the timeline for results, he said, "It's a very big country. So I think it will take at least a month or two." The CEO said the drive on packaged drinking water is not for any particular reason but part of the FSSAI efforts to safeguard consumers' interest by ensuring safe food. "There is no particular reason. If you notice, in the last year, we have taken up, one by one, a lot of things. We have done dairy, meat, eggs, cereals, energy drinks, and sugary drinks. Water is also part of that process," he told reporters on the sidelines of a CII event. Mr. Punhani highlighted that FSSAI has taken action against misleading advertisements as well as claims on the labelling of food products.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Asked about when the regulator will start the legal process against Bisleri International, Mr. Punhani said it is a "normal routine thing and it will happen".

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 FSSAI’s pan-India enforcement drive on packaged drinking water, lab test to take 1-2 months: CEO

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 04:15:01 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The regulator has widened the scope of its scrutiny after a sample of Bisleri packaged drinking water failed the lab test

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: FSSAI CEO Rajit Punhani on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) said the food regulator is collecting samples of packaged drinking water from across the country and lab testing will be complete in around two months. He also announced that FSSAI would soon start inspection of 'packaging materials' used for food items, saying those should be 'food grade'. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has widened the scope of its scrutiny after a sample of Bisleri packaged drinking water failed the lab test. The regulator has sanctioned prosecution against Bisleri International. When asked about its enforcement drive against packaged drinking water, Mr. Punhani said, "We are in the process. The process has started. We are doing all over the country." On the timeline for results, he said, "It's a very big country. So I think it will take at least a month or two." The CEO said the drive on packaged drinking water is not for any particular reason but part of the FSSAI efforts to safeguard consumers' interest by ensuring safe food. "There is no particular reason. If you notice, in the last year, we have taken up, one by one, a lot of things. We have done dairy, meat, eggs, cereals, energy drinks, and sugary drinks. Water is also part of that process," he told reporters on the sidelines of a CII event. Mr. Punhani highlighted that FSSAI has taken action against misleading advertisements as well as claims on the labelling of food products.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Asked about when the regulator will start the legal process against Bisleri International, Mr. Punhani said it is a "normal routine thing and it will happen".

Enforcement (Noun)
सख्ती से कानून लागू करना — किसी नियम या आदेश का ज़मीनी स्तर पर पालन करवाना।
✓ Syn: Implementation, Execution, Administration  |  ✖ Ant: Neglect, Abandonment, Waiver
International (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'International' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Prosecution (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Prosecution' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Inspection (Adjective / Verb)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Inspection' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "FSSAI’s pan-India enforcement drive on packaged drinking water, lab test to take 1-2 months: CEO", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The regulator has widened the scope of its scrutiny after a sample of Bisleri packaged drinking water failed the lab test.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'FSSAI’s pan-India enforcement drive on packaged ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'FSSAI’s pan-India enforcement drive on packag' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'FSSAI’s pan-India enforcement drive on packag' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The regulator has widened the scope of its scrutiny after a sample of Bisleri packaged drinking water failed the lab test."

A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Punhani said it is a "normal routine thing and it will happen".
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Punhani said it is a "normal routine thing and it will happen"."

articles.title: T.N. Chief Secretary did not receive complaint from woman IAS officer over Kallakurichi TVK MLA’s alleged misbehaviour, Madras HC told
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan asks State Public Prosecutor R. John Sathyan to take instructions from the woman officer, too, and report to the court by November 24, 2026

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: State Public Prosecutor (SPP) R. John Sathyan on Monday (November 23, 2026) asserted before the Madras High Court that neither Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar nor the police had received any representation/complaint from a woman IAS officer accusing Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh of misbehaving with her , as widely reported in the media over the past few days. Appearing before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, the SPP gave an emphatic “no” in response to questions raised by the judge as to whether the police or the Chief Secretary had received any complaint/representation from the woman officer. Thereafter, the judge asked the SPP to also obtain instructions from the officer and report to the court by Tuesday (November 24, 2026). The submissions were made during the hearing of a writ petition (criminal) filed by advocate R. Thrishuli, seeking a direction to the State police to register a criminal case against the MLA on the basis of the petitioner’s complaint that he had trespassed into the IAS officer’s bungalow in an inebriated state and threatened the officials there, besides sending obscene messages to the officer. When the judge wanted to know how the petitioner knew about the alleged obscene messages, her counsel S. Jeyakumar replied that the woman officer had complained to the Chief Secretary. On being asked to place the complaint before the court, the counsel said: “It is not available with me, I agree.” He, however, accused the official respondents of suppressing the facts of the case. “Everything is available with them but they are suppressing all those things. They are sailing with the accused and not at all taking care of the law. All higher officers are protecting the accused. In these circumstances, what will the ... (woman IAS officer) do MiLord?” the counsel said. Surprised at his answer, the judge asked: “You mean to say that an IAS officer does not know to protect herself?” The judge also referred to the 2021 sexual harassment complaint lodged by a woman IPS officer against the then special DGP and said: “Last time when a similar incident happened, it was the woman officer who gave the complaint. Where is the complaint in the present instance? Are you and I going to do something that an IAS officer does not know to do? She is the head of a district, I say.” On being told by the petitioner’s counsel that the National Commission for Women (NCW) had taken suo motu cognisance of the issue on the basis of newspaper reports and called for a report from the DGP, the judge said: “They can act based on newspaper reports, I cannot. Give me some tangible material to show that the MLA had indeed sent obscene messages and I will issue a (writ of) mandamus.” Stating that the petitioner before the court appeared to be trying to fish in troubled waters, Justice Lakshminarayanan also said: “If the officer concerned has not made any complaint, where is the question of police taking action? Do you want them (the police) to take action on the basis of newspaper reports? If there is no complaint by the woman, I will not interfere.” DMK urges Tamil Nadu DGP to act against TVK MLA for sending ‘obscene messages’ to Kallakurichi Collector
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Kallakurichi TVK MLA-Collector row: Tamil Nadu Minister Vanni Arasu says VCK will stand by victims

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 T.N. Chief Secretary did not receive complaint from woman IAS officer over Kallakurichi TVK MLA’s alleged misbehaviour, Madras HC told

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 04:10:54 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Justice V. Lakshminarayanan asks State Public Prosecutor R. John Sathyan to take instructions from the woman officer, too, and report to the court by November 24, 2026

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: State Public Prosecutor (SPP) R. John Sathyan on Monday (November 23, 2026) asserted before the Madras High Court that neither Chief Secretary M. Sai Kumar nor the police had received any representation/complaint from a woman IAS officer accusing Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh of misbehaving with her , as widely reported in the media over the past few days. Appearing before Justice V. Lakshminarayanan, the SPP gave an emphatic “no” in response to questions raised by the judge as to whether the police or the Chief Secretary had received any complaint/representation from the woman officer. Thereafter, the judge asked the SPP to also obtain instructions from the officer and report to the court by Tuesday (November 24, 2026). The submissions were made during the hearing of a writ petition (criminal) filed by advocate R. Thrishuli, seeking a direction to the State police to register a criminal case against the MLA on the basis of the petitioner’s complaint that he had trespassed into the IAS officer’s bungalow in an inebriated state and threatened the officials there, besides sending obscene messages to the officer. When the judge wanted to know how the petitioner knew about the alleged obscene messages, her counsel S. Jeyakumar replied that the woman officer had complained to the Chief Secretary. On being asked to place the complaint before the court, the counsel said: “It is not available with me, I agree.” He, however, accused the official respondents of suppressing the facts of the case. “Everything is available with them but they are suppressing all those things. They are sailing with the accused and not at all taking care of the law. All higher officers are protecting the accused. In these circumstances, what will the ... (woman IAS officer) do MiLord?” the counsel said. Surprised at his answer, the judge asked: “You mean to say that an IAS officer does not know to protect herself?” The judge also referred to the 2021 sexual harassment complaint lodged by a woman IPS officer against the then special DGP and said: “Last time when a similar incident happened, it was the woman officer who gave the complaint. Where is the complaint in the present instance? Are you and I going to do something that an IAS officer does not know to do? She is the head of a district, I say.” On being told by the petitioner’s counsel that the National Commission for Women (NCW) had taken suo motu cognisance of the issue on the basis of newspaper reports and called for a report from the DGP, the judge said: “They can act based on newspaper reports, I cannot. Give me some tangible material to show that the MLA had indeed sent obscene messages and I will issue a (writ of) mandamus.” Stating that the petitioner before the court appeared to be trying to fish in troubled waters, Justice Lakshminarayanan also said: “If the officer concerned has not made any complaint, where is the question of police taking action? Do you want them (the police) to take action on the basis of newspaper reports? If there is no complaint by the woman, I will not interfere.” DMK urges Tamil Nadu DGP to act against TVK MLA for sending ‘obscene messages’ to Kallakurichi Collector

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Kallakurichi TVK MLA-Collector row: Tamil Nadu Minister Vanni Arasu says VCK will stand by victims

Representation (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Representation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Commission (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Commission' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Cognisance (Noun)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Cognisance' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "T.N. Chief Secretary did not receive complaint from woman IAS officer over Kallakurichi TVK MLA’s alleged misbehaviour, Madras HC told", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Lakshminarayanan asks State Public Prosecutor R.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'T.N. Chief Secretary did not receive complaint f' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'T.N. Chief Secretary did not receive complain' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'T.N. Chief Secretary did not receive complain' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Lakshminarayanan asks State Public Prosecutor R."
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "T.N. Chief Secretary did not receive complaint from woman IAS officer over Kallakurichi TVK MLA’s alleged misbehaviour, Madras HC told"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Kallakurichi TVK MLA-Collector row: Tamil Nadu Minister Vanni Arasu says VCK will stand by victims.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Kallakurichi TVK MLA-Collector row: Tamil Nadu Minister Vanni Arasu says VCK will stand by victims."

articles.title: Cabinet clears construction of new airport at Silchar for ₹2,014 crore
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The existing Silchar airport, owned by the Indian Air Force and the Airports Authority of India (AAI), operates a civil enclave spread over 70 acres

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) approved a proposal to construct a new airport at Doloo in Silchar, Assam, with an estimated cost of ₹2,014 crore. The existing Silchar airport, owned by the Indian Air Force and the Airports Authority of India (AAI), operates a civil enclave spread over 70 acres. Briefing the media after Cabinet meeting, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the airport will have the capacity to handle 800 passengers during peak hours and the annual passenger handling capacity will be 1.01 million. The project is estimated to cost ₹2,014 crore and will be fully funded by AAI through its own internal resources. Mr. Vaishnaw said the airport will provide connectivity to Barak Valley and the adjoining northeastern region and help promote tourism.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The project was approved by the Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Cabinet clears construction of new airport at Silchar for ₹2,014 crore

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 04:01:29 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The existing Silchar airport, owned by the Indian Air Force and the Airports Authority of India (AAI), operates a civil enclave spread over 70 acres

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Union Cabinet on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) approved a proposal to construct a new airport at Doloo in Silchar, Assam, with an estimated cost of ₹2,014 crore. The existing Silchar airport, owned by the Indian Air Force and the Airports Authority of India (AAI), operates a civil enclave spread over 70 acres. Briefing the media after Cabinet meeting, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said the airport will have the capacity to handle 800 passengers during peak hours and the annual passenger handling capacity will be 1.01 million. The project is estimated to cost ₹2,014 crore and will be fully funded by AAI through its own internal resources. Mr. Vaishnaw said the airport will provide connectivity to Barak Valley and the adjoining northeastern region and help promote tourism.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The project was approved by the Cabinet chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

articles.title: Wildlife, forests, and culture in Gudalur: Sculptures, stories, and interactive workshops
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Into the Forest, an ongoing exhibition in Gudalur explores the relationship between forests, wildlife and people through sculptures, stories, workshops for children and creative artefacts made using invasive plant species

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: What if the plants choking the forests of the Nilgiris could be given a second life as works of art?An ongoing exhibition in Gudalur hopes to tell that story, bringing together conservation, craftsmanship and narratives of the intimate relationship between people and the natural world. “For all of us, sharing space with wildlife is part of everyday life,” says Rhea Antony, who takes care of storytelling and design at The Elephant People, a social enterprise based in Gudalur in the Nilgiris Biosphere Reserve that makes hand-carved wildlife sculptures, masks, and everyday objects from invasive plant species like Lantana camara and Senna spectabilis. Handcrafted objects made using invasive species vegetation | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement The exhibition is an attempt to draw attention to the changing landscapes of the Nilgiris Biosphere Reserve, where the invasive species have spread across native habitats. These fast-growing plants suppress native vegetation, particularly grasses, affecting the food sources of wildlife and sometimes pushing animals towards human settlements. ALSO WATCH Watch: How communities are rebuilding the Nilgiris ecosystem The Elephant People collective works with Forest Departments of Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka in clearing these invasive species. Instead of treating the recovered vegetation as waste, they transform the wood into handcrafted objects and sculptures inspired by the region’s wildlife, people, and landscapes. The team includes over 50 makers across carving, painting, design, production, and operations | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Titled Into the Forest, the first exhibition by The Elephant People features stories of wildlife, people, shared landscapes, and practices connected to the land. “These stories are brought to life through art and craft, with sculptures and installations created by a team of makers from the Nilgiris, for whom sharing space with wildlife is part of everyday life,” says Rhea. The exhibition features large-scale sculptures, smaller carved pieces, and interactive storytelling experiences. For children, there will be facilitated painting and story-building workshops, alongside interactive art installations that let them explore the forest through play. These installations offer opportunities to learn about different species, their habitats, and the sounds they make. ALSO WATCH Watch: A ride on the quaint Ooty toy train “Over the last three years, we’ve been exploring the stories of the Nilgiris and finding ways to bring them to life through art and craft. The region has been central to this journey. It’s wildlife, landscapes, people and the many relationships between them have shaped the stories we are drawn to and the work we create ,” says Rhea. While discovering stories of different species, they also learnt about encounters between people and wildlife, traditional practices, food cultures and ways of living that keep the forest at the centre. Some came from conversations with people, others from naturalists and researchers, and many from simply observing the fascinating relationships that exist within these landscapes.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: ALSO WATCH Watch: A day at Baralikadu: Coracles, tribal food and community-led tourism

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — क्या होगा यदि नीलगिरी के जंगलों का गला घोंटने वाले पौधों को कला के कार्यों के रूप में दूसरा जीवन दिया जा सके? गुडलूर में चल रही एक प्रदर्शनी उस कहानी को बताने की उम्मीद करती है, जो लोगों और प्राकृतिक दुनिया के बीच घनिष्ठ संबंधों के संरक्षण, शिल्प कौशल और आख्यानों को एक साथ लाती है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Conservation' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: संरक्षण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Conservation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Significant, Substantial, Strategic और Antonyms हैं: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial।

hinglishTracks.en: “For all of us, sharing space with wildlife is part of everyday life,” says Rhea Antony, who takes care of storytelling and design at The Elephant People, a social enterprise based in Gudalur in the Nilgiris Biosphere Reserve that makes hand-carved wildlife sculptures, masks, and everyday objects from invasive plant species like Lantana camara and Senna spectabilis.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — "हम सभी के लिए, वन्यजीवों के साथ जगह साझा करना रोजमर्रा की जिंदगी का हिस्सा है," रिया एंटनी कहती हैं, जो नीलगिरी बायोस्फीयर रिजर्व में गुडलूर में स्थित एक सामाजिक उद्यम द एलीफेंट पीपल में कहानी कहने और डिजाइन की देखभाल करती हैं, जो लैंटाना कैमारा और सेन्ना स्पेक्टाबिलिस जैसी आक्रामक पौधों की प्रजातियों से हाथ से नक्काशीदार वन्यजीव मूर्तियां, मुखौटे और रोजमर्रा की वस्तुएं बनाती है।।

hinglishTracks.en: Handcrafted objects made using invasive species vegetation | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — आक्रामक प्रजाति की वनस्पति का उपयोग करके बनाई गई हस्तनिर्मित वस्तुएं | फोटो साभार: विशेष व्यवस्था। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Arrangement' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: व्यवस्था — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Arrangement' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

hinglishTracks.en: The exhibition is an attempt to draw attention to the changing landscapes of the Nilgiris Biosphere Reserve, where the invasive species have spread across native habitats.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — प्रदर्शनी नीलगिरी बायोस्फीयर रिजर्व के बदलते परिदृश्यों पर ध्यान आकर्षित करने का एक प्रयास है, जहां आक्रामक प्रजातियां मूल निवास स्थानों में फैल गई हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: These fast-growing plants suppress native vegetation, particularly grasses, affecting the food sources of wildlife and sometimes pushing animals towards human settlements.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — ये तेजी से बढ़ने वाले पौधे देशी वनस्पति, विशेषकर घास को दबा देते हैं, वन्यजीवों के भोजन स्रोतों को प्रभावित करते हैं और कभी-कभी जानवरों को मानव बस्तियों की ओर धकेल देते हैं।।

📰 Wildlife, forests, and culture in Gudalur: Sculptures, stories, and interactive workshops

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 04:01:11 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Into the Forest, an ongoing exhibition in Gudalur explores the relationship between forests, wildlife and people through sculptures, stories, workshops for children and creative artefacts made using invasive plant species

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: What if the plants choking the forests of the Nilgiris could be given a second life as works of art?An ongoing exhibition in Gudalur hopes to tell that story, bringing together conservation, craftsmanship and narratives of the intimate relationship between people and the natural world. “For all of us, sharing space with wildlife is part of everyday life,” says Rhea Antony, who takes care of storytelling and design at The Elephant People, a social enterprise based in Gudalur in the Nilgiris Biosphere Reserve that makes hand-carved wildlife sculptures, masks, and everyday objects from invasive plant species like Lantana camara and Senna spectabilis. Handcrafted objects made using invasive species vegetation | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement The exhibition is an attempt to draw attention to the changing landscapes of the Nilgiris Biosphere Reserve, where the invasive species have spread across native habitats. These fast-growing plants suppress native vegetation, particularly grasses, affecting the food sources of wildlife and sometimes pushing animals towards human settlements. ALSO WATCH Watch: How communities are rebuilding the Nilgiris ecosystem The Elephant People collective works with Forest Departments of Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka in clearing these invasive species. Instead of treating the recovered vegetation as waste, they transform the wood into handcrafted objects and sculptures inspired by the region’s wildlife, people, and landscapes. The team includes over 50 makers across carving, painting, design, production, and operations | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Titled Into the Forest, the first exhibition by The Elephant People features stories of wildlife, people, shared landscapes, and practices connected to the land. “These stories are brought to life through art and craft, with sculptures and installations created by a team of makers from the Nilgiris, for whom sharing space with wildlife is part of everyday life,” says Rhea. The exhibition features large-scale sculptures, smaller carved pieces, and interactive storytelling experiences. For children, there will be facilitated painting and story-building workshops, alongside interactive art installations that let them explore the forest through play. These installations offer opportunities to learn about different species, their habitats, and the sounds they make. ALSO WATCH Watch: A ride on the quaint Ooty toy train “Over the last three years, we’ve been exploring the stories of the Nilgiris and finding ways to bring them to life through art and craft. The region has been central to this journey. It’s wildlife, landscapes, people and the many relationships between them have shaped the stories we are drawn to and the work we create ,” says Rhea. While discovering stories of different species, they also learnt about encounters between people and wildlife, traditional practices, food cultures and ways of living that keep the forest at the centre. Some came from conversations with people, others from naturalists and researchers, and many from simply observing the fascinating relationships that exist within these landscapes.

articles.summary: 1. Core Context & Background: Into the Forest, an ongoing exhibition in Gudalur explores the relationship between forests, wildlife and people through sculptures, stories, workshops for children and creative artefacts made using invasive plant species
articles.keyPoints:
• 1. Core Context & Background: Into the Forest, an ongoing exhibition in Gudalur explores the relationship between forests, wildlife and people through sculptures, stories, workshops for children and creative artefacts made using invasive plant species
• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: What if the plants choking the forests of the Nilgiris could be given a second life as works of art?An ongoing exhibition in Gudalur hopes to tell that story, bringing together conservation, craftsmanship and narratives of the intimate relationship between people and the natural world. “For all of us, sharing space with wildlife is part of everyday life,” says Rhea Antony, who takes care of storytelling and design at The Elephant People, a social enterprise based in Gudalur in the Nilgiris Biosphere Reserve that makes hand-carved wildlife sculptures, masks, and everyday objects from invasive plant species like Lantana camara and Senna spectabilis. Handcrafted objects made using invasive species vegetation | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement The exhibition is an attempt to draw attention to the changing landscapes of the Nilgiris Biosphere Reserve, where the invasive species have spread across native habitats. These fast-growing plants suppress native vegetation, particularly grasses, affecting the food sources of wildlife and sometimes pushing animals towards human settlements. ALSO WATCH Watch: How communities are rebuilding the Nilgiris ecosystem The Elephant People collective works with Forest Departments of Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka in clearing these invasive species. Instead of treating the recovered vegetation as waste, they transform the wood into handcrafted objects and sculptures inspired by the region’s wildlife, people, and landscapes. The team includes over 50 makers across carving, painting, design, production, and operations | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Titled Into the Forest, the first exhibition by The Elephant People features stories of wildlife, people, shared landscapes, and practices connected to the land. “These stories are brought to life through art and craft, with sculptures and installations created by a team of makers from the Nilgiris, for whom sharing space with wildlife is part of everyday life,” says Rhea. The exhibition features large-scale sculptures, smaller carved pieces, and interactive storytelling experiences. For children, there will be facilitated painting and story-building workshops, alongside interactive art installations that let them explore the forest through play. These installations offer opportunities to learn about different species, their habitats, and the sounds they make. ALSO WATCH Watch: A ride on the quaint Ooty toy train “Over the last three years, we’ve been exploring the stories of the Nilgiris and finding ways to bring them to life through art and craft. The region has been central to this journey. It’s wildlife, landscapes, people and the many relationships between them have shaped the stories we are drawn to and the work we create ,” says Rhea. While discovering stories of different species, they also learnt about encounters between people and wildlife, traditional practices, food cultures and ways of living that keep the forest at the centre. Some came from conversations with people, others from naturalists and researchers, and many from simply observing the fascinating relationships that exist within these landscapes.

articles.title: 30 missing terrorists from Reasi exfiltrated to Pakistan for arms training, disturb peace in India: DGP

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The police chief said Mahore Police Station received information through reliable sources that 30 terrorists hailing from Mahore and Chassana, missing since 1991 to 2003, had crossed over to Pakistan

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Thirty terrorists hailing from Reasi district, who had gone missing between 1991 and 2003, have exfiltrated to Pakistan and are working for a terror outfit, supplying arms, ammunition and money to revive terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir , Director General of Police Nalin Prabhat said on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). The police chief said Mahore Police Station received information through reliable sources that 30 terrorists hailing from Mahore and Chassana, missing since 1991 to 2003, had crossed over to Pakistan for weapons training for waging war against India. "These persons are now working for HM [Hizbul Mujahideen] in Pakistan and are supplying arms and ammunition, money, to promote terrorism in J&K, besides instigating and radicalising the youth for taking part in terror activities in the area," the DGP said on X. The 30 terrorists operating from Pakistan have been identified as Mohd Qayoom of Shadole, Mohd Sabdar of Shajroo, Ghulam Mohd and Ghulam Qadir, both sons of Samdoo and residents of Khour, Mushtaq Ahmad of Khour and Khushal Hussain, a resident of Dada. The list further names Abdul Majeed, Mohd Rafiq, alias Shabir, Shabir Ahmad and Manzoor Ahmad, all residents of Karmkatha, Makhna and Alaf Din, both residents of Shajroo, Abdul Majeed of Lar, Ghulam Mohd, alias Gamma, of Shajroo, and Mushtaq Ahmad of Sildhar. Others identified are Mohd Yousuf Khakmat, alias Bilal (callsign), of Shadool, Mohd Iqbal and Mohd Ashraf, both residents of Chakrass, Ghulam Mohd of Ladh, Abdul Hamid Najar, alias Mahamdoo, of Shibrass, Jamal Din of Sildhar, and Talib Hussain of Chiklass. The remaining names are Mohd Rafiq, Gami Gujjar, both residents of Larh, Mohd Rafiq of Tulli, Mohd Qasim of Kunderdhan, Abdul Hamid of Balmatkote, Shabir Ahmad of Bagodass, Mohd Rafiq of Kunderdhan, and Mohd Ali of Hassote. In 2024, Mahore police filed an FIR under sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Explosive and Im­provised Materials Control provisions and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) against these alleged terrorists. During the investigation, police recorded statements of witnesses and identified five alleged terrorists who also exfiltrated to Pakistan for arms and ammunition training and were actively involved in attempts to revive terrorist activities in the area from across the border by selling their lands to finance terrorism, the DGP said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: They have been identified as Mohd Qayoom, alias Abdul Qayoom, of Shadole in Mahore tehsil, Bashir Ahmad, alias Masoom, of Bidder, Shokat Ali of Hunder in Arnas tehsil, Manzoor Ahmad, alias Manzoor Hussain, of Khanti in Thuroo tehsil, and Imtyaz Ahmad of Thuroo.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 30 missing terrorists from Reasi exfiltrated to Pakistan for arms training, disturb peace in India: DGP

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 05:30:44 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The police chief said Mahore Police Station received information through reliable sources that 30 terrorists hailing from Mahore and Chassana, missing since 1991 to 2003, had crossed over to Pakistan

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Thirty terrorists hailing from Reasi district, who had gone missing between 1991 and 2003, have exfiltrated to Pakistan and are working for a terror outfit, supplying arms, ammunition and money to revive terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir , Director General of Police Nalin Prabhat said on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). The police chief said Mahore Police Station received information through reliable sources that 30 terrorists hailing from Mahore and Chassana, missing since 1991 to 2003, had crossed over to Pakistan for weapons training for waging war against India. "These persons are now working for HM [Hizbul Mujahideen] in Pakistan and are supplying arms and ammunition, money, to promote terrorism in J&K, besides instigating and radicalising the youth for taking part in terror activities in the area," the DGP said on X. The 30 terrorists operating from Pakistan have been identified as Mohd Qayoom of Shadole, Mohd Sabdar of Shajroo, Ghulam Mohd and Ghulam Qadir, both sons of Samdoo and residents of Khour, Mushtaq Ahmad of Khour and Khushal Hussain, a resident of Dada. The list further names Abdul Majeed, Mohd Rafiq, alias Shabir, Shabir Ahmad and Manzoor Ahmad, all residents of Karmkatha, Makhna and Alaf Din, both residents of Shajroo, Abdul Majeed of Lar, Ghulam Mohd, alias Gamma, of Shajroo, and Mushtaq Ahmad of Sildhar. Others identified are Mohd Yousuf Khakmat, alias Bilal (callsign), of Shadool, Mohd Iqbal and Mohd Ashraf, both residents of Chakrass, Ghulam Mohd of Ladh, Abdul Hamid Najar, alias Mahamdoo, of Shibrass, Jamal Din of Sildhar, and Talib Hussain of Chiklass. The remaining names are Mohd Rafiq, Gami Gujjar, both residents of Larh, Mohd Rafiq of Tulli, Mohd Qasim of Kunderdhan, Abdul Hamid of Balmatkote, Shabir Ahmad of Bagodass, Mohd Rafiq of Kunderdhan, and Mohd Ali of Hassote. In 2024, Mahore police filed an FIR under sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Explosive and Im­provised Materials Control provisions and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) against these alleged terrorists. During the investigation, police recorded statements of witnesses and identified five alleged terrorists who also exfiltrated to Pakistan for arms and ammunition training and were actively involved in attempts to revive terrorist activities in the area from across the border by selling their lands to finance terrorism, the DGP said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: They have been identified as Mohd Qayoom, alias Abdul Qayoom, of Shadole in Mahore tehsil, Bashir Ahmad, alias Masoom, of Bidder, Shokat Ali of Hunder in Arnas tehsil, Manzoor Ahmad, alias Manzoor Hussain, of Khanti in Thuroo tehsil, and Imtyaz Ahmad of Thuroo.

articles.title: Women’s Commission urges Telangana Governor to recommend special investigation into illegal oocyte racket
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Telangana State Women’s Commission urged Governor Shiv Pratap Shukla to recommend a special investigation to uncover the network behind the illegal oocyte (egg) collection racket — that was busted in Hyderabad a few weeks ago. A high-level committee to ensure a comprehensive and impartial investigation too was sought.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Commission’s Chairperson Nerella Sharada, along with its Member Uzma Shakeer, met the Governor at Lok Bhavan in the city on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) and apprised him of the racket involving alleged exploitation of poor and middle-class women. Malkajgiri Commissionerate Police in October last week said that they have busted an illegal human egg harvesting racket. The police arrested eight people, and 43 women from Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Maharashtra and other States were rescued from four premises in Hyderabad. The Chairperson apprised the Governor on the findings of the inquiry conducted by the Women’s Commission, information gathered from officials concerned, police investigation and legal developments. Ms. Sharada explained that women from different States were allegedly brought to Hyderabad on the pretext of employment and subsequently lured them into illegal retrieval of oocytes, exploiting their financial vulnerabilities. Considering the inter-State connection and wider ramifications of the racket, the Commission urged for the special investigation. Highlighting “loopholes and shortcomings” in the implementation of the Assisted Reproductive Technology (ART) Act, it has urged the Governor to recommend necessary amendments to strengthen the legislation and ensure better protection of women’s rights, health and safety. The Governor responded positively to the representations made by the Commission and sought detailed information about the matter, as per a press note.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The Commission has earlier issued notices to eight ART centres and egg banks over suspected irregularities . Around 10 days ago, the Police sought documents from 14 fertility centres, including consent forms, and electronic records pertaining to egg donation procedures to find the number of women who were approached, how frequently they underwent the procedure and whether required consent was obtained.
