कानूनी अनुमति या स्वीकार्यता — किसी कार्य को करने की वैध छूट।

क्रियान्वयन / ज़मीनी स्तर पर लागू करना — किसी योजना या फैसले को असलियत में पूरा करना।
✓ Syn: Execution, Enforcement, Fulfillment  |  ✖ Ant: Abandonment, Neglect, Cancellation
Constitutional (Adjective)
संवैधानिक — देश के संविधान (Constitution) के दायरे और मौलिक अधिकारों के अनुरूप।
✓ Syn: Statutory, Legitimate, Lawful  |  ✖ Ant: Unconstitutional, Illegal, Arbitrary
Administration (Noun)
प्रशासन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Administration' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

articles.title: The Hindu’s coffee table book on exploration of the Western Ghats released
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The book titled, ‘Mountains of Our Destiny: The Western Ghats, A Journey Through The Southern Monsoon Mountains by Vrinda Ramanan and J. Ramanan is a sequel to ‘Mountains of our Destiny: An Expedition to the Indian Himalaya’, also by the same authors.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Hindu launched a coffee table book titled, ‘Mountains of Our Destiny: The Western Ghats, A Journey Through The Southern Monsoon Mountains’, on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). Authored by Vrinda Ramanan and J. Ramanan, mountaineers, writers and photographers, the book was launched by Tamil Nadu Forests Minister R.V. Ranjith Kumar. The first copies were received by Rohit Ramesh, Director, Suresh Nambath, Editor, and L.V. Navaneeth, CEO, The Hindu . The book is a sequel to ‘Mountains of our Destiny: An Expedition to the Indian Himalaya’, also by the same authors. Speaking on the occasion, the Minister noted the importance of the forests, rivers and mountains to sustaining agriculture, livelihoods and ecological balance. He highlighted the need to ensure forest conservation, spoke of the measures taken by the government to improve upon work being done, such as AI technology to prevent elephant deaths on railway tracks and in the control of forest fires, and congratulated the authors on their work. Author J. Ramanan explained that the two mountain ranges: the Himalayas and the Western Ghats formed the bedrock of India’s existence. Without them, he said, we would not have had our rivers. The 1,500 km Western Ghats in particular, recognised as a biodiversity hotspot, was one of the richest ecological resources in the country, sustaining thousands of lives. The monsoon in India, Mr. Ramanan said, is shaped by the Western Ghats and the Himalayas. The book was an attempt to create awareness about, and educate people on the importance of maintaining ecological balance through their preservation. Through more than 400 photographs, field experiences and narratives, the book explores the geology, wildlife, plants, indigenous communities and the intricate web of life that sustains these mountains. It also examines the growing pressures of plantations, invasive species, tourism, dams and other human interventions, highlighting the urgent need for conservation.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The book is available at The Hindu ’s online bookstore: https://publications.thehindugroup.com/ . The cover price of the book is ₹2,999. At present, the book is available at a special launch offer price of ₹2,249 for a limited period of time. Those interested can also scan the QR code to buy a copy.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 The Hindu’s coffee table book on exploration of the Western Ghats released

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 07:22:40 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The book titled, ‘Mountains of Our Destiny: The Western Ghats, A Journey Through The Southern Monsoon Mountains by Vrinda Ramanan and J. Ramanan is a sequel to ‘Mountains of our Destiny: An Expedition to the Indian Himalaya’, also by the same authors.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The Hindu launched a coffee table book titled, ‘Mountains of Our Destiny: The Western Ghats, A Journey Through The Southern Monsoon Mountains’, on Wednesday (November 25, 2026). Authored by Vrinda Ramanan and J. Ramanan, mountaineers, writers and photographers, the book was launched by Tamil Nadu Forests Minister R.V. Ranjith Kumar. The first copies were received by Rohit Ramesh, Director, Suresh Nambath, Editor, and L.V. Navaneeth, CEO, The Hindu . The book is a sequel to ‘Mountains of our Destiny: An Expedition to the Indian Himalaya’, also by the same authors. Speaking on the occasion, the Minister noted the importance of the forests, rivers and mountains to sustaining agriculture, livelihoods and ecological balance. He highlighted the need to ensure forest conservation, spoke of the measures taken by the government to improve upon work being done, such as AI technology to prevent elephant deaths on railway tracks and in the control of forest fires, and congratulated the authors on their work. Author J. Ramanan explained that the two mountain ranges: the Himalayas and the Western Ghats formed the bedrock of India’s existence. Without them, he said, we would not have had our rivers. The 1,500 km Western Ghats in particular, recognised as a biodiversity hotspot, was one of the richest ecological resources in the country, sustaining thousands of lives. The monsoon in India, Mr. Ramanan said, is shaped by the Western Ghats and the Himalayas. The book was an attempt to create awareness about, and educate people on the importance of maintaining ecological balance through their preservation. Through more than 400 photographs, field experiences and narratives, the book explores the geology, wildlife, plants, indigenous communities and the intricate web of life that sustains these mountains. It also examines the growing pressures of plantations, invasive species, tourism, dams and other human interventions, highlighting the urgent need for conservation.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The book is available at The Hindu ’s online bookstore: https://publications.thehindugroup.com/ . The cover price of the book is ₹2,999. At present, the book is available at a special launch offer price of ₹2,249 for a limited period of time. Those interested can also scan the QR code to buy a copy.

Indigenous (Adjective)
स्वदेशी — अपने ही देश (भारत) के वैज्ञानिकों और इंजीनियरों द्वारा देश में विकसित किया गया।
✓ Syn: Domestic, Home-grown, Native  |  ✖ Ant: Imported, Foreign, Exotic
Sustainability (Noun)
सतत विकास — पर्यावरण और भविष्य की पीढ़ियों को नुकसान पहुँचाए बिना लंबे समय तक चलने वाला विकास।
✓ Syn: Viability, Eco-balance, Durability  |  ✖ Ant: Depletion, Unsustainability, Destruction
Conservation (Noun)
संरक्षण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Conservation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Biodiversity (Noun)
जैव विविधता — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Biodiversity' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "The Hindu’s coffee table book on exploration of the Western Ghats released", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. The book titled, ‘Mountains of Our Destiny: The Western Ghats, A Journey Through The Southern Monsoon Mountains by Vrinda Ramanan and J.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'The Hindu’s coffee table book on exploration of ' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'The Hindu’s coffee table book on exploration ' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'The Hindu’s coffee table book on exploration ' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "The book titled, ‘Mountains of Our Destiny: The Western Ghats, A Journey Through The Southern Monsoon Mountains by Vrinda Ramanan and J." (Hinglish Arth: वृंदा रामानन और जे. द्वारा लिखित पुस्तक का शीर्षक है, 'माउंटेन ऑफ अवर डेस्टिनी: द वेस्टर्न घाट्स, ए जर्नी थ्रू द सदर्न मॉनसून माउंटेन्स।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "The Hindu’s coffee table book on exploration of the Western Ghats released"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Those interested can also scan the QR code to buy a copy.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Those interested can also scan the QR code to buy a copy." (Hinglish Arth: इच्छुक लोग कॉपी खरीदने के लिए क्यूआर कोड को स्कैन भी कर सकते हैं।)

articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: According to Agriculture Department data, groundnut sowing this year stood at 1.59 lakh hectares against the target of 2.54 lakh hectares. Of the area sown, crop failure has been recorded across 1.49 lakh hectares, accounting for 93.71% of the total sown area

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: As Bengaluru gears up for the historic Kadlekai Parishe, celebrated in Basavanagudi and Malleshwaram, the arrival of groundnuts in Karnataka’s markets has been delayed this year due to drought conditions, with farmers reporting reduced sowing and poor yields across major groundnut-growing districts. Groundnut farmers in Kolar, Chitradurga, Dharwad, Haveri, Mandya, Mysuru and Tumakuru districts said sowing had declined this year due to inadequate rainfall and drying borewells. Groundnut is predominantly cultivated during the kharif season in these districts, while Vijayapura, Yadgir, Kalaburagi and Raichur districts also cultivate the crop during the summer season. According to data from the Department of Agriculture, groundnut sowing this year stood at 1.59 lakh hectares against the target of 2.54 lakh hectares. Of the area sown, crop failure has been recorded across 1.49 lakh hectares, accounting for 93.71% of the total sown area. Agriculture Department officials attributed the extensive crop failure primarily to deficient rainfall, pointing out that groundnut cultivation in Karnataka is largely rain-dependent. Of the 2.54 lakh hectares targeted for cultivation, around 2.38 lakh hectares are rainfed, while only approximately 0.17 lakh hectares are under irrigation. Although groundnut is not widely cultivated during the rabi season, the department’s data showed that sowing had been completed across 0.58 lakh hectares as of November 13, against a target of 1.33 lakh hectares. Speaking to The Hindu , a senior Agriculture Department official said that the farmers who cultivate groundnut during the rabi season generally have access to better irrigation facilities. “Farmers who cultivate during the rabi season have good water facilities through borewells, or their fields are usually located in command areas,” the official said. Pointing to the delayed market arrivals, K.P. Bhoothaiah, senior vice-president of the Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha, Chitradurga, said even farmers who had managed to cultivate groundnut were reporting poor yields. “Even where farmers have cultivated groundnut, the yield is low and the seeds are smaller in size,” he said. Abhilash Reddy, a farmer from Kolar district, said that he had not cultivated groundnut this year due to drought, drying borewells and a shortage of agricultural labourers.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “Groundnut cultivation is labour-intensive. The crop has to be harvested, dried under the sun and shelled. With the borewells drying up and labour becoming difficult to find, I decided not to cultivate it this year,” he said.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Drought affects groundnut cultivation in Karnataka; prices rise amid supply shortage

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 07:19:46 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: According to Agriculture Department data, groundnut sowing this year stood at 1.59 lakh hectares against the target of 2.54 lakh hectares. Of the area sown, crop failure has been recorded across 1.49 lakh hectares, accounting for 93.71% of the total sown area

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: As Bengaluru gears up for the historic Kadlekai Parishe, celebrated in Basavanagudi and Malleshwaram, the arrival of groundnuts in Karnataka’s markets has been delayed this year due to drought conditions, with farmers reporting reduced sowing and poor yields across major groundnut-growing districts. Groundnut farmers in Kolar, Chitradurga, Dharwad, Haveri, Mandya, Mysuru and Tumakuru districts said sowing had declined this year due to inadequate rainfall and drying borewells. Groundnut is predominantly cultivated during the kharif season in these districts, while Vijayapura, Yadgir, Kalaburagi and Raichur districts also cultivate the crop during the summer season. According to data from the Department of Agriculture, groundnut sowing this year stood at 1.59 lakh hectares against the target of 2.54 lakh hectares. Of the area sown, crop failure has been recorded across 1.49 lakh hectares, accounting for 93.71% of the total sown area. Agriculture Department officials attributed the extensive crop failure primarily to deficient rainfall, pointing out that groundnut cultivation in Karnataka is largely rain-dependent. Of the 2.54 lakh hectares targeted for cultivation, around 2.38 lakh hectares are rainfed, while only approximately 0.17 lakh hectares are under irrigation. Although groundnut is not widely cultivated during the rabi season, the department’s data showed that sowing had been completed across 0.58 lakh hectares as of November 13, against a target of 1.33 lakh hectares. Speaking to The Hindu , a senior Agriculture Department official said that the farmers who cultivate groundnut during the rabi season generally have access to better irrigation facilities. “Farmers who cultivate during the rabi season have good water facilities through borewells, or their fields are usually located in command areas,” the official said. Pointing to the delayed market arrivals, K.P. Bhoothaiah, senior vice-president of the Karnataka Rajya Raitha Sangha, Chitradurga, said even farmers who had managed to cultivate groundnut were reporting poor yields. “Even where farmers have cultivated groundnut, the yield is low and the seeds are smaller in size,” he said. Abhilash Reddy, a farmer from Kolar district, said that he had not cultivated groundnut this year due to drought, drying borewells and a shortage of agricultural labourers.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: “Groundnut cultivation is labour-intensive. The crop has to be harvested, dried under the sun and shelled. With the borewells drying up and labour becoming difficult to find, I decided not to cultivate it this year,” he said.

Department (Adjective)

A. According to Agriculture Department data, groundnut sowing this year stood at 1.59 lakh hectares against the target of 2.54 lakh hectares.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Drought affects groundnut cultivation in Karnata' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Drought affects groundnut cultivation in Karn' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Drought affects groundnut cultivation in Karn' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "According to Agriculture Department data, groundnut sowing this year stood at 1.59 lakh hectares against the target of 2.54 lakh hectares." D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.

articles.title: Operation Gaja in Karnataka: People protest in Mudigere, observe bandh
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The Operation Gaja was launched after two people were killed in separate elephant attacks in Belur taluk. The department plans to relocate about 56 elephants.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The bandh called in Mudigere on Wednesday against Operation Gaja, the Forest Department’s drive to push wild elephants from Belur in Hassan district towards the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary, evoked an impressive response. The operation was launched after two people were killed in elephant attacks in Belur taluk. The bandh was called by various political parties and organisations, including farmers’ groups. Shops and hotels remained shut from 6 a.m. Autorickshaw associations backed the call, and auto stands stayed empty through the day. Most private schools and colleges had declared a holiday a day earlier. Government schools and colleges opened in the morning and were closed later, leaving students from rural areas inconvenienced. Lawyers stayed away from court and took out a march from the court premises to Lions Circle. KSRTC buses operated but ran almost empty, and several rural routes were cancelled. Heavy police deployment was seen in Mudigere town, Hand Post, Banakal, Kottigehara, Jannapura and Gonibeedu. Western Range IGP Shashikumar and Superintendent of Police Jitendra Kumar Dayama camped in the town. Protesters from across the taluk blocked the Kadur–Mangaluru National Highway for over an hour. They raised slogans against the government and Hassan district in-charge Minister K.M. Shivalinge Gowda, and burned his photograph. They placed coffee and arecanut plants damaged by elephants in Makonahalli, Gowthalli, Pura and Karabail on the road. They refused to move until the Deputy Conservator of Forests (DCF) met them. After police persuaded them to end the blockade, they marched to the Forest Department’s sub-division office, staged a dharna and raised slogans against the State government, the department and elected representatives. DCF K.T. Boraiah received a memorandum from the protesters. He said a meeting of Ministers, MLAs and senior officials would be held in Bengaluru. Former MLC M.K. Pranesh said the people of the taluk had shown patience and that it should not be tested. He said compensation was not what they wanted and demanded that the elephants be driven to Nagarahole or Bandipur. He accused Mudigere MLA Nayana Motamma of seeking sympathy through her offer to resign and said the ruling party’s legislators should have used their influence in government to find a lasting solution. Former town panchayat president P.G. Anukumar said farmers were leaving their land fallow because of wild animals. He demanded that the elephants be sent back to Belur and warned of a hunger strike from Thursday if this was not done.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The protesters took exception to Mudigere MLA Nayana Motamma for offering to resign. “The MLA should have joined the protest if she were genuinely concerned about the plight of farmers, instead of submitting the resignation," the proesters said.

They placed coffee and arecanut plants damaged by elephants in Makonahalli, Gowthalli, Pura and Karabail on the road. They refused to move until the Deputy Conservator of Forests (DCF) met them. After police persuaded them to end the blockade, they marched to the Forest Department’s sub-division office, staged a dharna and raised slogans against the State government, the department and elected representatives. DCF K.T. Boraiah received a memorandum from the protesters. He said a meeting of Ministers, MLAs and senior officials would be held in Bengaluru. Former MLC M.K. Pranesh said the people of the taluk had shown patience and that it should not be tested. He said compensation was not what they wanted and demanded that the elephants be driven to Nagarahole or Bandipur. He accused Mudigere MLA Nayana Motamma of seeking sympathy through her offer to resign and said the ruling party’s legislators should have used their influence in government to find a lasting solution. Former town panchayat president P.G. Anukumar said farmers were leaving their land fallow because of wild animals. He demanded that the elephants be sent back to Belur and warned of a hunger strike from Thursday if this was not done.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The protesters took exception to Mudigere MLA Nayana Motamma for offering to resign. “The MLA should have joined the protest if she were genuinely concerned about the plight of farmers, instead of submitting the resignation," the proesters said.

📰 Operation Gaja in Karnataka: People protest in Mudigere, observe bandh

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 07:19:44 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The Operation Gaja was launched after two people were killed in separate elephant attacks in Belur taluk. The department plans to relocate about 56 elephants.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The bandh called in Mudigere on Wednesday against Operation Gaja, the Forest Department’s drive to push wild elephants from Belur in Hassan district towards the Bhadra Wildlife Sanctuary, evoked an impressive response. The operation was launched after two people were killed in elephant attacks in Belur taluk. The bandh was called by various political parties and organisations, including farmers’ groups. Shops and hotels remained shut from 6 a.m. Autorickshaw associations backed the call, and auto stands stayed empty through the day. Most private schools and colleges had declared a holiday a day earlier. Government schools and colleges opened in the morning and were closed later, leaving students from rural areas inconvenienced. Lawyers stayed away from court and took out a march from the court premises to Lions Circle. KSRTC buses operated but ran almost empty, and several rural routes were cancelled. Heavy police deployment was seen in Mudigere town, Hand Post, Banakal, Kottigehara, Jannapura and Gonibeedu. Western Range IGP Shashikumar and Superintendent of Police Jitendra Kumar Dayama camped in the town. Protesters from across the taluk blocked the Kadur–Mangaluru National Highway for over an hour. They raised slogans against the government and Hassan district in-charge Minister K.M. Shivalinge Gowda, and burned his photograph. They placed coffee and arecanut plants damaged by elephants in Makonahalli, Gowthalli, Pura and Karabail on the road. They refused to move until the Deputy Conservator of Forests (DCF) met them. After police persuaded them to end the blockade, they marched to the Forest Department’s sub-division office, staged a dharna and raised slogans against the State government, the department and elected representatives. DCF K.T. Boraiah received a memorandum from the protesters. He said a meeting of Ministers, MLAs and senior officials would be held in Bengaluru. Former MLC M.K. Pranesh said the people of the taluk had shown patience and that it should not be tested. He said compensation was not what they wanted and demanded that the elephants be driven to Nagarahole or Bandipur. He accused Mudigere MLA Nayana Motamma of seeking sympathy through her offer to resign and said the ruling party’s legislators should have used their influence in government to find a lasting solution. Former town panchayat president P.G. Anukumar said farmers were leaving their land fallow because of wild animals. He demanded that the elephants be sent back to Belur and warned of a hunger strike from Thursday if this was not done.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The protesters took exception to Mudigere MLA Nayana Motamma for offering to resign. “The MLA should have joined the protest if she were genuinely concerned about the plight of farmers, instead of submitting the resignation," the proesters said.

articles.title: IIT Dharwad scientist helps unravel structure of protein linked to heart disease
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The finding by an international team of researchers led by Badri Nath Dubey can help advance research into potential drug targets

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: An international team of researchers led by Badri Nath Dubey of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Dharwad has uncovered the structural organisation of a protein associated with several cardiovascular disorders, a finding that can help advance research into potential drug targets. The study on Rho-associated coiled-coil-containing protein kinase (ROCK) authored by 15 researchers, including Mr. Dubey, was published in Communications Chemistry, a Nature Portfolio journal, on November 4. The research was conducted in collaboration with scientists from Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf, the Max Planck Institute of Molecular Physiology, the European Molecular Biology Laboratory in Hamburg and other institutions. ROCK plays a role in regulating cell contraction and movement, including processes involved in the functioning of blood vessels. Its abnormal activity has been linked to conditions such as high blood pressure and pulmonary hypertension. While scientists have previously characterised certain regions of the protein, its central region remained poorly understood. Using X-ray crystallography, electron microscopy and other structural analysis techniques, the researchers examined the central coiled-coil region of ROCK. They found that two long protein helices twist around each other to form an elongated structure. By combining the findings with existing structural information, the researchers modelled the protein as an extended molecular rod. Their analysis also indicated that the structure can exhibit flexibility and form different molecular assemblies, including dimers and tetramers.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to the researchers, the findings provide a better understanding of ROCK’s structural organisation. They can help investigate how the protein functions and is regulated within cells.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 IIT Dharwad scientist helps unravel structure of protein linked to heart disease

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 07:18:28 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The finding by an international team of researchers led by Badri Nath Dubey can help advance research into potential drug targets

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: An international team of researchers led by Badri Nath Dubey of the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Dharwad has uncovered the structural organisation of a protein associated with several cardiovascular disorders, a finding that can help advance research into potential drug targets. The study on Rho-associated coiled-coil-containing protein kinase (ROCK) authored by 15 researchers, including Mr. Dubey, was published in Communications Chemistry, a Nature Portfolio journal, on November 4. The research was conducted in collaboration with scientists from Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf, the Max Planck Institute of Molecular Physiology, the European Molecular Biology Laboratory in Hamburg and other institutions. ROCK plays a role in regulating cell contraction and movement, including processes involved in the functioning of blood vessels. Its abnormal activity has been linked to conditions such as high blood pressure and pulmonary hypertension. While scientists have previously characterised certain regions of the protein, its central region remained poorly understood. Using X-ray crystallography, electron microscopy and other structural analysis techniques, the researchers examined the central coiled-coil region of ROCK. They found that two long protein helices twist around each other to form an elongated structure. By combining the findings with existing structural information, the researchers modelled the protein as an extended molecular rod. Their analysis also indicated that the structure can exhibit flexibility and form different molecular assemblies, including dimers and tetramers.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to the researchers, the findings provide a better understanding of ROCK’s structural organisation. They can help investigate how the protein functions and is regulated within cells.

संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ।

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Collaboration (Noun)
सहयोग — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Collaboration' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Organisation (Noun)
संगठन — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Organisation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial

D. The author contends that 'IIT Dharwad scientist helps unravel structure' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. B. They can help investigate how the protein functions and is regulated within cells.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "They can help investigate how the protein functions and is regulated within cells." articles.title: Net FDI fell to more than 5.5-year low in September 2026, as outflows jumped 40%
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Despite September’s performance, net FDI in the first half of the financial year was more than 20% higher than in the same period last year

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Net foreign direct investment (FDI) into India in September 2026 fell to its lowest level in at least 5.5 years, with outflows exceeding inflows by nearly $5 billion, data released by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) shows. This was driven by a simultaneous slump in gross inflows and a jump in outflows. However, net FDI in the first half of the financial year (April-September 2026) was more than 20% higher than in the same period of the previous year. September’s net FDI figure of -$4.95 billion was the lowest since at least March 2021, the earliest month for which data is accessible. Direct investment refers to the inflows that give the investor substantial control over an asset or means of production, as opposed to portfolio investments, which are typically more in the nature of speculative purchases of minor shareholding. Gross inflows, or the total amount of direct investment entering the country, fell to $5.9 billion in September 2026, 46.6% lower than in August, and 17.6% lower than in September of last year. According to the RBI, around two-thirds of the gross inflows were channelled into manufacturing, communication, and computer services sectors, with Singapore and the U.S. as the major source countries. Total outflows climbed to $10.8 billion in September 2026, nearly 40% higher than in August, and 15% higher than in September last year. Within this, repatriation of profits by foreign companies in India grew to $6.4 billion, nearly 37% higher than in the same month last year, and the highest since at least March 2021. Outward investments made by Indian companies grew to a five-month high of $4.4 billion in September 2026. The RBI says that of the outward investments, manufacturing, and financial, insurance and business services sectors accounted for about four-fifths of the amount that flowed out of India, with The Netherlands, Singapore and the U.S. serving as the major destinations.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: economy (general) / foreign investment / economic indicator

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #14 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Net FDI fell to more than 5.5-year low in September 2026, as outflows jumped 40%

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 09:11:09 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Despite September’s performance, net FDI in the first half of the financial year was more than 20% higher than in the same period last year

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Net foreign direct investment (FDI) into India in September 2026 fell to its lowest level in at least 5.5 years, with outflows exceeding inflows by nearly $5 billion, data released by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) shows. This was driven by a simultaneous slump in gross inflows and a jump in outflows. However, net FDI in the first half of the financial year (April-September 2026) was more than 20% higher than in the same period of the previous year. September’s net FDI figure of -$4.95 billion was the lowest since at least March 2021, the earliest month for which data is accessible. Direct investment refers to the inflows that give the investor substantial control over an asset or means of production, as opposed to portfolio investments, which are typically more in the nature of speculative purchases of minor shareholding. Gross inflows, or the total amount of direct investment entering the country, fell to $5.9 billion in September 2026, 46.6% lower than in August, and 17.6% lower than in September of last year. According to the RBI, around two-thirds of the gross inflows were channelled into manufacturing, communication, and computer services sectors, with Singapore and the U.S. as the major source countries. Total outflows climbed to $10.8 billion in September 2026, nearly 40% higher than in August, and 15% higher than in September last year. Within this, repatriation of profits by foreign companies in India grew to $6.4 billion, nearly 37% higher than in the same month last year, and the highest since at least March 2021. Outward investments made by Indian companies grew to a five-month high of $4.4 billion in September 2026. The RBI says that of the outward investments, manufacturing, and financial, insurance and business services sectors accounted for about four-fifths of the amount that flowed out of India, with The Netherlands, Singapore and the U.S. serving as the major destinations.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: economy (general) / foreign investment / economic indicator

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Repatriation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 📈 Economic, Banking & Finance passage on "Net FDI fell to more than 5.5-year low in September 2026, as outflows jumped 40%", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Despite September’s performance, net FDI in the first half of the financial year was more than 20% higher than in the same period last year.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Net FDI fell to more than 5.5-year low in Septem' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Net FDI fell to more than 5.5-year low in Sep' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Net FDI fell to more than 5.5-year low in Sep' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Despite September’s performance, net FDI in the first half of the financial year was more than 20% higher than in the same period last year."
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Net FDI fell to more than 5.5-year low in September 2026, as outflows jumped 40%"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. economy (general) / foreign investment / economic indicator.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "economy (general) / foreign investment / economic indicator."

articles.title: Duty-free raw sugar imports up to 10 lakh tonnes allowed till March 2027
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & IBPS/SBI/RBI/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP Growth, Inflation, Fiscal Deficit & Trade Balance
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The industry expects more imports in the coming days and this will ensure supply of adequate quantity of sugar in the domestic market throughout the sugar season.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Duty-free imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar will be permitted until the end of March 2027, according to a notification issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) on Wednesday. A notification issued on August 20 had allowed duty-free imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes of sugar under the Tariff Rate Quota (TRQ) scheme until December 31, 2026. Separately, the DGFT has allowed sugar mills time until September 30, 2027, to process the imported raw sugar and sell it in the domestic market. The Indian Sugar and Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association Director General Deepak Ballani told The Hindu that price parity had prevailed over the past, making it viable for Indian importers to source raw sugar from international markets, primarily Brazil. Some imports have already begun. The industry expects more imports in the coming days and this will ensure supply of adequate quantity of sugar in the domestic market throughout the sugar season. It will also keep the prices stable, he said.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Agriculture / imports / food / economy (general) / agriculture / farms / consumer goods

📈 Economic, Banking & Finance Paragraph #15 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Duty-free raw sugar imports up to 10 lakh tonnes allowed till March 2027

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 08:43:58 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The industry expects more imports in the coming days and this will ensure supply of adequate quantity of sugar in the domestic market throughout the sugar season.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Duty-free imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes of raw sugar will be permitted until the end of March 2027, according to a notification issued by the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) on Wednesday. A notification issued on August 20 had allowed duty-free imports of up to 10 lakh tonnes of sugar under the Tariff Rate Quota (TRQ) scheme until December 31, 2026. Separately, the DGFT has allowed sugar mills time until September 30, 2027, to process the imported raw sugar and sell it in the domestic market. The Indian Sugar and Bio-Energy Manufacturers Association Director General Deepak Ballani told The Hindu that price parity had prevailed over the past, making it viable for Indian importers to source raw sugar from international markets, primarily Brazil. Some imports have already begun. The industry expects more imports in the coming days and this will ensure supply of adequate quantity of sugar in the domestic market throughout the sugar season. It will also keep the prices stable, he said.

articles.title: Bangladesh tightens border security ahead of Hasina's planned return; deploys 108 BGB platoons
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The heightened security comes amid fears that Ms. Hasina's supporters could intensify violence and sabotage in the coming days. Awami League, whose activities have been banned, is promoting a lockdown programme for November 29 and 30 through online platforms, adding to concerns over a possible escalation of tensions

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bangladesh beefed up security across several districts, deploying 108 platoons of border paramilitary forces, including 56 in exiled former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's home district, Gopalganj, as political tensions mount over her planned return next month. There have been incidents of violence, including arson attacks targeting trains, buses and banks, across Bangladesh in the last many days surrounding the 79-year-old politician's possible return. Ms. Hasina has been staying in India since fleeing Dhaka in August 2024 following a student-led uprising that toppled her government. Police blamed activists of Awami League and its affiliated organisations for several of the incidents. The heightened security comes amid fears that Ms. Hasina's supporters could intensify violence and sabotage in the coming days. Awami League, whose activities have been banned, is promoting a lockdown programme for November 29 and 30 through online platforms, adding to concerns over a possible escalation of tensions. In a press statement on Wednesday (November 25, 2026), the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) announced the deployment of 108 platoons in seven districts "to maintain law and order, ensure public safety and deal with any untoward situation", news portal bdnews24.com reported. Of them, 56 platoons have been deployed in Gopalganj amid persistent unrest, the BGB said. Gopalganj, a stronghold of the Awami League, has witnessed incidents of violence, arson and vandalism in recent days. Around 2,000 police personnel and 10 BGB platoons, along with personnel of the Special Response Battalion (SRB), were deployed in the district last week. According to the BGB statement, 18 platoons have been deployed in Dhaka, six in Narayanganj, 18 in Gazipur, two in Mymensingh, three in Chattogram and one in Cox's Bazar districts. "In addition, four platoons of BGB members have been kept on alert for deployment," it said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The deployment has been made on the instructions of the Home Ministry, with BGB personnel coordinating with the respective district administrations and other law enforcement agencies, the Prothom Alo newspaper reported.

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #21 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Bangladesh tightens border security ahead of Hasina's planned return; deploys 108 BGB platoons

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 06:53:52 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: The heightened security comes amid fears that Ms. Hasina's supporters could intensify violence and sabotage in the coming days. Awami League, whose activities have been banned, is promoting a lockdown programme for November 29 and 30 through online platforms, adding to concerns over a possible escalation of tensions

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Bangladesh beefed up security across several districts, deploying 108 platoons of border paramilitary forces, including 56 in exiled former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's home district, Gopalganj, as political tensions mount over her planned return next month. There have been incidents of violence, including arson attacks targeting trains, buses and banks, across Bangladesh in the last many days surrounding the 79-year-old politician's possible return. Ms. Hasina has been staying in India since fleeing Dhaka in August 2024 following a student-led uprising that toppled her government. Police blamed activists of Awami League and its affiliated organisations for several of the incidents. The heightened security comes amid fears that Ms. Hasina's supporters could intensify violence and sabotage in the coming days. Awami League, whose activities have been banned, is promoting a lockdown programme for November 29 and 30 through online platforms, adding to concerns over a possible escalation of tensions. In a press statement on Wednesday (November 25, 2026), the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) announced the deployment of 108 platoons in seven districts "to maintain law and order, ensure public safety and deal with any untoward situation", news portal bdnews24.com reported. Of them, 56 platoons have been deployed in Gopalganj amid persistent unrest, the BGB said. Gopalganj, a stronghold of the Awami League, has witnessed incidents of violence, arson and vandalism in recent days. Around 2,000 police personnel and 10 BGB platoons, along with personnel of the Special Response Battalion (SRB), were deployed in the district last week. According to the BGB statement, 18 platoons have been deployed in Dhaka, six in Narayanganj, 18 in Gazipur, two in Mymensingh, three in Chattogram and one in Cox's Bazar districts. "In addition, four platoons of BGB members have been kept on alert for deployment," it said.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The deployment has been made on the instructions of the Home Ministry, with BGB personnel coordinating with the respective district administrations and other law enforcement agencies, the Prothom Alo newspaper reported.

articles.title: Execution of proclamation orders against Hafiz Saeed, five other 26/11 accused still awaited
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: A special court issued proclamation orders against the six absconding accused in July this year; the court is currently conducting the trial against handler Abu Jundal

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: While the trial in the 26/11 terror attacks is on against Zabiuddin Ansari alias Abu Jundal, the handler who taught the 10 Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists Hindi, steps to execute the proclamation orders against six other perpetrators, including Lashkar operatives Hafiz Saeed and Zaki-ur-Rehman Lakhvi, are yet to be taken. A special court issued proclamation orders against the six absconding accused in July this year. The court is currently conducting the trial against Jundal. In August and September this year, the prosecution told the court that it had requested the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) to serve the proclamation orders against the six absconding accused in the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks case. However, the MHA has not responded to the request yet. Special Public Prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam said that while there has been no development regarding the execution of the proclamation orders issued against the wanted accused, he assured that the perpetrators of the attacks would be punished in India. "The prosecution will ensure that all those persons who facilitated the dastardly attacks would be punished on Indian soil," Mr. Nikam told PTI . He said, as per procedure, non-bailable warrants and Interpol Red Corner notices were issued through diplomatic channels against the absconding accused, who are the main perpetrators and conspirators behind the attacks. "But I am sure that the Pakistan government will not respond as that country continues to be a haven for terrorists," Mr. Nikam said. The prosecution had in August and September told the court that the MHA was requested to take necessary steps to serve the proclamation orders, through Interpol, against the accused believed to be residing in Pakistan. Mr. Nikam had then told the court that amid the procedural compliance, the trial against the absconding accused would commence as Section 356 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 allows criminal trials in absentia for absconding proclaimed offenders, even where there is no immediate prospect of arrest.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The trial against Jundal, which had been on hold since 2018 pending a petition filed by government authorities over the furnishing of certain documents to the accused, commenced in November last year after clearance from the Bombay High Court.

articles.newspaperPrintHtml:
🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #20 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Execution of proclamation orders against Hafiz Saeed, five other 26/11 accused still awaited

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 08:35:31 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: A special court issued proclamation orders against the six absconding accused in July this year; the court is currently conducting the trial against handler Abu Jundal

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: While the trial in the 26/11 terror attacks is on against Zabiuddin Ansari alias Abu Jundal, the handler who taught the 10 Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists Hindi, steps to execute the proclamation orders against six other perpetrators, including Lashkar operatives Hafiz Saeed and Zaki-ur-Rehman Lakhvi, are yet to be taken. A special court issued proclamation orders against the six absconding accused in July this year. The court is currently conducting the trial against Jundal. In August and September this year, the prosecution told the court that it had requested the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) to serve the proclamation orders against the six absconding accused in the 2008 Mumbai terror attacks case. However, the MHA has not responded to the request yet. Special Public Prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam said that while there has been no development regarding the execution of the proclamation orders issued against the wanted accused, he assured that the perpetrators of the attacks would be punished in India. "The prosecution will ensure that all those persons who facilitated the dastardly attacks would be punished on Indian soil," Mr. Nikam told PTI . He said, as per procedure, non-bailable warrants and Interpol Red Corner notices were issued through diplomatic channels against the absconding accused, who are the main perpetrators and conspirators behind the attacks. "But I am sure that the Pakistan government will not respond as that country continues to be a haven for terrorists," Mr. Nikam said. articles.title: Air pollution accelerates dementia by reprogramming brain's immune cells: study
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: The analysis found that people living in the most polluted third of areas are 25% more likely to develop Alzheimer's disease or a related form of dementia than those in the least polluted third

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Air pollution helps cause dementia by changing the genes that are switched on in microglia, the brain's immune cells, in ways that disrupt their normal functions, a new study has found. The study, published in the Journal of Neuroinflammation , combined health records from nearly half a million people from the UK Biobank with experiments in mouse models. "By recreating in mice what happens when people breath polluted air, we found that pollution causes major changes in which genes are active in the brain's immune cells," senior author Sanjay Rajagopalan, professor of medicine and director of the Cardiovascular Research Institute at the Case Western Reserve University's school of medicine, said. "These cells normally keep the brain healthy by clearing away debris and fighting infection. Seeing how pollution disrupts them helps explain how a stress that affects much of the world's population harms the brain, and it points us toward a way to treat it," Rajagopalan said. Mice were exposed to outdoor Cleveland (US) air for five months. The fine particles in the air, known as particulate matter 2.5 (PM2.5), were concentrated to levels similar to those found in the world's most polluted cities. Otherwise healthy mice developed memory problems, a leaky blood-brain barrier and brain inflammation. Their brains also showed a lower chemical balance reflecting its energy status and ability to withstand injury and disease. The mice's brains also showed an increased death of newborn neurons in the hippocampus, the brain's centre for learning and memory. The analysis found that people living in the most polluted third of areas are 25% more likely to develop Alzheimer's disease or a related form of dementia than those in the least polluted third. Further, in mice genetically prone to Alzheimer's, air pollution caused the same harm and also sped up amyloid plaque buildup -- a hallmark of the neurodegenerative disease.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The authors wrote: "These population-scale data in humans and experimental data in mice​ support PM2.5 as an environmental neurotoxicant and define microglial regulatory programs through which genetic background shapes the biological response to a common and modifiable exposure."

• 2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Air pollution helps cause dementia by changing the genes that are switched on in microglia, the brain's immune cells, in ways that disrupt their normal functions, a new study has found. The study, published in the Journal of Neuroinflammation , combined health records from nearly half a million people from the UK Biobank with experiments in mouse models. "By recreating in mice what happens when people breath polluted air, we found that pollution causes major changes in which genes are active in the brain's immune cells," senior author Sanjay Rajagopalan, professor of medicine and director of the Cardiovascular Research Institute at the Case Western Reserve University's school of medicine, said. "These cells normally keep the brain healthy by clearing away debris and fighting infection. Seeing how pollution disrupts them helps explain how a stress that affects much of the world's population harms the brain, and it points us toward a way to treat it," Rajagopalan said. Mice were exposed to outdoor Cleveland (US) air for five months. The fine particles in the air, known as particulate matter 2.5 (PM2.5), were concentrated to levels similar to those found in the world's most polluted cities. Otherwise healthy mice developed memory problems, a leaky blood-brain barrier and brain inflammation. Their brains also showed a lower chemical balance reflecting its energy status and ability to withstand injury and disease. The mice's brains also showed an increased death of newborn neurons in the hippocampus, the brain's centre for learning and memory. The analysis found that people living in the most polluted third of areas are 25% more likely to develop Alzheimer's disease or a related form of dementia than those in the least polluted third. Further, in mice genetically prone to Alzheimer's, air pollution caused the same harm and also sped up amyloid plaque buildup -- a hallmark of the neurodegenerative disease.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The authors wrote: "These population-scale data in humans and experimental data in mice​ support PM2.5 as an environmental neurotoxicant and define microglial regulatory programs through which genetic background shapes the biological response to a common and modifiable exposure."

articles.title: ₹300-crore Bhadrachalam temple development works under way, structures designed to last 200 years: Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy said development works at the historic Sri Sitaramachandra Swamy temple in Bhadrachalam are being undertaken at a cost of ₹300 crore, with the structures designed to last for 200 years and be appreciated by future generations.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The works are part of the development of temples located along the Godavari riverbanks under the temple corridor from Basar to Bhadrachalam, in preparation for the Godavari Pushkaralu-2027, at an estimated cost of ₹1,100 crore, he said. The Minister reviewed the temple development works in Bhadrachalam on Wednesday. He inspected the concrete construction works being undertaken from Dammakka Annadana Satram to the stairway, as well as the works surrounding the main temple. He also held a review meeting with officials at the Sub-Collector’s office in the temple town. Later, speaking to reporters, he said the major development works would be completed by December 19, 2026, on the occasion of Mukkoti Ekadasi, ensuring that devotees would not face any inconvenience. Stating that the slab construction works had been completed, the Minister said the Cabinet sub-committee was reviewing the progress of the works once every fortnight. He said Bhadrachalam was expected to attract more than one crore pilgrims during the Godavari Pushkaralu-2027 and that all arrangements were being planned accordingly to ensure the smooth conduct of the mega religious event. The Minister also undertook an extensive tour of the Bhadrachalam Agency, inaugurating and laying foundation stones for various development works in Bhadrachalam, Charla and Dummugudem mandals. He laid the foundation stones for a Ground-Level Service Reservior (GLSR) at Ranganayakula Gutta and a tribal multi-purpose market on the premises of the Agriculture Market Yard in Bhadrachalam.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Later, he inaugurated additional classrooms at the Ashram School in Narayanaraopeta village and laid the foundation stone for an Overhead Service Reservoir (OHSR) at Parnashala Ghat in Dummugudem mandal.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 ₹300-crore Bhadrachalam temple development works under way, structures designed to last 200 years: Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 09:25:56 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Revenue Minister Ponguleti Srinivasa Reddy said development works at the historic Sri Sitaramachandra Swamy temple in Bhadrachalam are being undertaken at a cost of ₹300 crore, with the structures designed to last for 200 years and be appreciated by future generations.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The works are part of the development of temples located along the Godavari riverbanks under the temple corridor from Basar to Bhadrachalam, in preparation for the Godavari Pushkaralu-2027, at an estimated cost of ₹1,100 crore, he said. The Minister reviewed the temple development works in Bhadrachalam on Wednesday. He inspected the concrete construction works being undertaken from Dammakka Annadana Satram to the stairway, as well as the works surrounding the main temple. He also held a review meeting with officials at the Sub-Collector’s office in the temple town. Later, speaking to reporters, he said the major development works would be completed by December 19, 2026, on the occasion of Mukkoti Ekadasi, ensuring that devotees would not face any inconvenience. Stating that the slab construction works had been completed, the Minister said the Cabinet sub-committee was reviewing the progress of the works once every fortnight. He said Bhadrachalam was expected to attract more than one crore pilgrims during the Godavari Pushkaralu-2027 and that all arrangements were being planned accordingly to ensure the smooth conduct of the mega religious event. The Minister also undertook an extensive tour of the Bhadrachalam Agency, inaugurating and laying foundation stones for various development works in Bhadrachalam, Charla and Dummugudem mandals. He laid the foundation stones for a Ground-Level Service Reservior (GLSR) at Ranganayakula Gutta and a tribal multi-purpose market on the premises of the Agriculture Market Yard in Bhadrachalam.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Later, he inaugurated additional classrooms at the Ashram School in Narayanaraopeta village and laid the foundation stone for an Overhead Service Reservoir (OHSR) at Parnashala Ghat in Dummugudem mandal.

articles.title: Andhra CM calls for report on illegal sand mining, damage to drinking water pipeline in Kadapa
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Following the directive, District Collector informs CMO the action taken against those involved in the illegal activity and measures initiated to prevent recurrence of such incidents

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has sought a report on the alleged illegal sand mining in the Penna river in Proddatur mandal of Kadapa district and the damage caused to a drinking water pipeline during the activity. Taking note of media reports on the incident on Wednesday, Mr. Naidu directed the officials to immediately submit a comprehensive explanation. Following the instructions, the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) sought a report from the Kadapa district administration. The CMO said the government viewed the alleged illegal mining and damage to a public drinking water pipeline seriously. It directed the District Collector to ensure that those involved in illegal mining or causing damage to government property were not spared. In his report to the CMO, the Collector said the village panchayat secretary had alerted the police after detecting illegal sand mining near Somulavaripalli. Officials immediately intervened and stopped both the mining activity and transportation of sand, the Collector said. A police complaint was lodged, providing details of the tractors used for illegal transportation of sand, their owners and others allegedly involved in the offence. An FIR was registered and investigation was under way, the Collector said. Cases under stringent sections were registered against those responsible for damaging the drinking water pipeline and the tractor owners. Repairs to the damaged pipeline were completed on a war-footing and water supply was restored, he added. The Collector said the district administration had initiated measures to prevent recurrence of such incidents. Special check-posts were established along the Penna and Chitravathi rivers to curb illegal sand mining and transportation.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: District and mandal-level committees were also constituted to monitor mining activities. Village panchayat secretaries and tahsildars of the mandals concerned were instructed to coordinate and prevent illegal transportation through the check-posts, the Collector said, adding that continuous surveillance was arranged along the Penna river.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Andhra CM calls for report on illegal sand mining, damage to drinking water pipeline in Kadapa

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 09:25:30 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Following the directive, District Collector informs CMO the action taken against those involved in the illegal activity and measures initiated to prevent recurrence of such incidents

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has sought a report on the alleged illegal sand mining in the Penna river in Proddatur mandal of Kadapa district and the damage caused to a drinking water pipeline during the activity. Taking note of media reports on the incident on Wednesday, Mr. Naidu directed the officials to immediately submit a comprehensive explanation. Following the instructions, the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) sought a report from the Kadapa district administration. The CMO said the government viewed the alleged illegal mining and damage to a public drinking water pipeline seriously. It directed the District Collector to ensure that those involved in illegal mining or causing damage to government property were not spared. In his report to the CMO, the Collector said the village panchayat secretary had alerted the police after detecting illegal sand mining near Somulavaripalli. Officials immediately intervened and stopped both the mining activity and transportation of sand, the Collector said. A police complaint was lodged, providing details of the tractors used for illegal transportation of sand, their owners and others allegedly involved in the offence. An FIR was registered and investigation was under way, the Collector said. Cases under stringent sections were registered against those responsible for damaging the drinking water pipeline and the tractor owners. Repairs to the damaged pipeline were completed on a war-footing and water supply was restored, he added. The Collector said the district administration had initiated measures to prevent recurrence of such incidents. Special check-posts were established along the Penna and Chitravathi rivers to curb illegal sand mining and transportation.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: District and mandal-level committees were also constituted to monitor mining activities. Village panchayat secretaries and tahsildars of the mandals concerned were instructed to coordinate and prevent illegal transportation through the check-posts, the Collector said, adding that continuous surveillance was arranged along the Penna river.

Comprehensive (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Comprehensive' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

A. Following the directive, District Collector informs CMO the action taken against those involved in the illegal activity and measures initiated to...

✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. articles.title: Moderate rain likely for two days in State
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Trough brings rain to several parts of the State with highest of 45.3 mm recorded at Naidupeta in Tirupati district

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: South Coastal Andhra Pradesh recorded moderate showers on Wednesday due to a trough extending from the Gulf of Mannar to the southwest Bay of Bengal. As of 3 p.m., the highest rainfall of 45.3 mm was recorded at Naidupeta in Tirupati district, followed by 41.5 mm at Allampadu in Nellore district. Other areas that received rainfall included Gudur (32.7 mm), Vakadu in Tirupati district (32.5 mm), Vidavalur in Nellore district (32 mm), Pennepalle in Tirupati district (30 mm), Molakalapundla in Nellore district (28 mm), Nellore (23.2 mm) and Bhimavaram (22.7 mm). Light to moderate rainfall, accompanied by lightning, may continue for the next two days, according to the India Meteorological Department.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: On Thursday, light to moderate rainfall is likely at isolated places in Polavaram, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, East Godavari, Bapatla, Prakasam, Nellore, Kadapa, Annamayya, Chittoor and Tirupati districts. Scattered light rainfall is also expected in other districts.

hinglishTracks.en: South Coastal Andhra Pradesh recorded moderate showers on Wednesday due to a trough extending from the Gulf of Mannar to the southwest Bay of Bengal.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — मन्नार की खाड़ी से दक्षिण पश्चिम बंगाल की खाड़ी तक बनी एक ट्रफ रेखा के कारण दक्षिण तटीय आंध्र प्रदेश में बुधवार को मध्यम बारिश दर्ज की गई।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Coastal' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Coastal' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है। इसके Synonyms हैं: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive और Antonyms हैं: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile।

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #10 of 30 (25 NOV)

📰 Moderate rain likely for two days in State

📌 Published: 25 Nov 2026, 09:21:18 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Trough brings rain to several parts of the State with highest of 45.3 mm recorded at Naidupeta in Tirupati district

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: South Coastal Andhra Pradesh recorded moderate showers on Wednesday due to a trough extending from the Gulf of Mannar to the southwest Bay of Bengal. As of 3 p.m., the highest rainfall of 45.3 mm was recorded at Naidupeta in Tirupati district, followed by 41.5 mm at Allampadu in Nellore district. Other areas that received rainfall included Gudur (32.7 mm), Vakadu in Tirupati district (32.5 mm), Vidavalur in Nellore district (32 mm), Pennepalle in Tirupati district (30 mm), Molakalapundla in Nellore district (28 mm), Nellore (23.2 mm) and Bhimavaram (22.7 mm). Light to moderate rainfall, accompanied by lightning, may continue for the next two days, according to the India Meteorological Department.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: On Thursday, light to moderate rainfall is likely at isolated places in Polavaram, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Konaseema, East Godavari, Bapatla, Prakasam, Nellore, Kadapa, Annamayya, Chittoor and Tirupati districts. Scattered light rainfall is also expected in other districts.

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Moderate rain likely for two days in State", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Trough brings rain to several parts of the State with highest of 45.3 mm recorded at Naidupeta in Tirupati district.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Moderate rain likely for two days in State' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.

D. The author contends that 'Moderate rain likely for two days in State' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.

articles.title: Akbaruddin Owaisi questions low spending, high dropouts in minority schools
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) legislator Akbaruddin Owaisi on Wednesday flagged low utilisation of funds by the Minorities Welfare Department, shortfall in minority student enrolment in welfare schools and delays in processing overseas scholarship applications, even as he called for corrective measures to address the gaps.

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Raising these concerns at a meeting of the Joint Committee for Welfare of Minorities in the Legislative Assembly, Mr. Owaisi questioned why admissions of students from minority communities in schools run by the Telangana Minorities Residential Educational Institutions Society (TGMREIS) were falling short of the prescribed quota. The Society has reserved 75% of seats for students from minority communities and 25% for others. However, of the approximately 85,000 students enrolled, around 56,000 belonged to minority communities and 29,000 to non-minority communities, accounting for about 66% and 34%, respectively. He expressed concern over the shortfall in minority enrolment and the high dropout rate, and called for systematic measures to address the issue. To check dropouts, Mr. Owaisi suggested that the State government introduce its own pre-matric scholarship scheme, irrespective of the Centre’s decision to discontinue its scheme. He also proposed using data from the Unified District Information System for Education (UDISE) to analyse dropout rates and identify the reasons behind them. While welcoming the proposed constitution of a Sikh Minority Finance Corporation, a promise in the Congress’s Minority Declaration ahead of the Assembly elections, he pointed out that a Christian Minorities Finance Corporation was already in existence. He suggested renaming the State Minorities Finance Corporation as the Muslim Finance Corporation. On the Chief Minister’s Overseas Scholarship Scheme, Mr. Owaisi questioned the delay in verifying applications and sought clarity on the pending reimbursement of tuition fees and maintenance of tuition fees. The outstanding dues for the period from 2019-20 to 2025-26 stood at ₹1,273 crore. Asking who would bear the financial burden, he cautioned that students would ultimately suffer. He also expressed concern over the department’s low fund utilisation. Against a budgetary allocation of ₹3,768 crore, the Minorities Welfare Department had spent only around ₹1,013 crore, he said. The department and its allied agencies and institutions have a sanctioned strength of 6,986 employees, but only 4,028 posts were filled. Mr. Owaisi said the large number of vacancies could affect the department’s efficiency and delivery of services.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: He stated that the MWD and its allied agencies and institutions have a sanctioned cadre strength of 6,986, but pointed out that only 4,028 were working, and indicated that the yawning gap in vacancies was a matter of concern, especially as regards the efficiency of the department, and service delivery.

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — ऑल इंडिया मजलिस-ए-इत्तेहादुल मुस्लिमीन (एआईएमआईएम) विधायक अकबरुद्दीन ओवैसी ने बुधवार को अल्पसंख्यक कल्याण विभाग द्वारा धन के कम उपयोग, कल्याण स्कूलों में अल्पसंख्यक छात्रों के नामांकन में कमी और विदेशी छात्रवृत्ति आवेदनों को संसाधित करने में देरी को चिह्नित किया, यहां तक ​​​​कि उन्होंने कमियों को दूर करने के लिए सुधारात्मक उपायों का भी आह्वान किया।।

hinglishTracks.en: Raising these concerns at a meeting of the Joint Committee for Welfare of Minorities in the Legislative Assembly, Mr.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: ज़रा ध्यान दीजियेगा, यहाँ मुख्य बात यह है कि — विधानसभा में अल्पसंख्यक कल्याण के लिए संयुक्त समिति की बैठक में ये चिंताएं उठाते हुए श्री.।

hinglishTracks.en: Owaisi questioned why admissions of students from minority communities in schools run by the Telangana Minorities Residential Educational Institutions Society (TGMREIS) were falling short of the prescribed quota.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: आसान हिंग्लिश भाषा में इसे समझें तो — ओवैसी ने सवाल किया कि तेलंगाना माइनॉरिटीज रेजिडेंशियल एजुकेशनल इंस्टीट्यूशंस सोसाइटी (टीजीएमआरईआईएस) द्वारा संचालित स्कूलों में अल्पसंख्यक समुदाय के छात्रों का प्रवेश निर्धारित कोटा से कम क्यों हो रहा है।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Institutional' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: संस्थागत — देश की संवैधानिक या सरकारी संस्थाओं के नियमों और ढांचे से जुड़ा हुआ। इसके Synonyms हैं: Systemic, Organizational, Constitutional और Antonyms हैं: Individual, Informal, Unorganized।

hinglishTracks.en: The Society has reserved 75% of seats for students from minority communities and 25% for others.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये, एग्जाम के नज़रिये से यह पॉइंट बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है — सोसायटी ने अल्पसंख्यक समुदायों के छात्रों के लिए 75% सीटें और अन्य के लिए 25% सीटें आरक्षित की हैं।।

hinglishTracks.en: However, of the approximately 85,000 students enrolled, around 56,000 belonged to minority communities and 29,000 to non-minority communities, accounting for about 66% and 34%, respectively.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: चलिए, अब इस अगली लाइन का असली मतलब देखते हैं — हालाँकि, नामांकित लगभग 85,000 छात्रों में से लगभग 56,000 अल्पसंख्यक समुदायों से थे और 29,000 गैर-अल्पसंख्यक समुदायों से थे, जो क्रमशः लगभग 66% और 34% थे।। नोट कर लीजिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का वर्ड 'Accountability' एग्जाम के लिए बहुत महत्वपूर्ण है! इसका अर्थ है: जवाबदेही — अपने फैसलों और काम का जनता तथा संविधान को हिसाब देने की बाध्यता। इसके Synonyms हैं: Responsibility, Answerability, Liability और Antonyms हैं: Immunity, Exemption, Irresponsibility।

hinglishTracks.en: He expressed concern over the shortfall in minority enrolment and the high dropout rate, and called for systematic measures to address the issue.
hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — उन्होंने अल्पसंख्यक नामांकन में कमी और उच्च ड्रॉपआउट दर पर चिंता व्यक्त की और इस मुद्दे के समाधान के लिए व्यवस्थित उपायों का आह्वान किया।।

hinglishTracks.en: To check dropouts, Mr.

hinglishTracks.en: Owaisi suggested that the State government introduce its own pre-matric scholarship scheme, irrespective of the Centre’s decision to discontinue its scheme.

hinglishTracks.hiExplanation: देखिये दोस्तों, इस लाइन का सीधा सा मतलब समझिये — उन्होंने विभाग के कम फंड उपयोग पर भी चिंता व्यक्त की।।
