articles.title: Sheikh Hasina could only be brought back to Bangladesh in handcuffs: Humaiun Kobir
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: “She can only be brought back in handcuffs or under strict surveillance,” Bangladesh State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina could only be brought back to Bangladesh in handcuffs or under strict surveillance, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), according to a local media report. Ms. Hasina, 79, has been living in India since fleeing Bangladesh on August 5, 2024, following a student-led protest that toppled her government. Bangladesh has been seeking her extradition from India, while New Delhi has maintained that Dhaka's extradition request was being examined through a legal process. Ms. Hasina’s spokesman Syed Mozammel Ali, speaking to a news agency on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), said she would return on December 16, which Bangladesh celebrates as Victory Day to commemorate independence from Pakistan after the 1971 war. Ms. Hasina has urged Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to arrange her return on the national airline. “Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5th, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka,” the spokesman said. Responding to the news report, Mr. Kobir said, “She can only be brought back in handcuffs or under strict surveillance." "A distinction had to be drawn between what Hasina wanted and what could happen," he was quoted as saying by the state-run BSS news agency. The issue of Ms. Hasina's return has emerged as a major source of tension between Dhaka and New Delhi, with the latest wave of unrest in Bangladesh following the government's rejection of her request for a fresh passport and national identity card earlier this month.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ms. Hasina's lawyers had approached the Bangladesh mission in New Delhi seeking the documents to facilitate her planned return in December.

📰 Sheikh Hasina could only be brought back to Bangladesh in handcuffs: Humaiun Kobir

🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: “She can only be brought back in handcuffs or under strict surveillance,” Bangladesh State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina could only be brought back to Bangladesh in handcuffs or under strict surveillance, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), according to a local media report. Ms. Hasina, 79, has been living in India since fleeing Bangladesh on August 5, 2024, following a student-led protest that toppled her government. Bangladesh has been seeking her extradition from India, while New Delhi has maintained that Dhaka's extradition request was being examined through a legal process. Ms. Hasina’s spokesman Syed Mozammel Ali, speaking to a news agency on Tuesday (November 24, 2026), said she would return on December 16, which Bangladesh celebrates as Victory Day to commemorate independence from Pakistan after the 1971 war. Ms. Hasina has urged Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to arrange her return on the national airline. “Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5th, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka,” the spokesman said. Responding to the news report, Mr. Kobir said, “She can only be brought back in handcuffs or under strict surveillance." "A distinction had to be drawn between what Hasina wanted and what could happen," he was quoted as saying by the state-run BSS news agency. The issue of Ms. Hasina's return has emerged as a major source of tension between Dhaka and New Delhi, with the latest wave of unrest in Bangladesh following the government's rejection of her request for a fresh passport and national identity card earlier this month.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ms. Hasina's lawyers had approached the Bangladesh mission in New Delhi seeking the documents to facilitate her planned return in December.

प्रत्यर्पण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Extradition' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

"A distinction had to be drawn between what Hasina wanted and what could happen," he was quoted as saying by the state-run BSS news agency. The issue of Ms. Hasina's return has emerged as a major source of tension between Dhaka and New Delhi, with the latest wave of unrest in Bangladesh following the government's rejection of her request for a fresh passport and national identity card earlier this month.
• 3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Ms. Hasina's lawyers had approached the Bangladesh mission in New Delhi seeking the documents to facilitate her planned return in December.

articles.title: COP31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A standoff on a fossil fuel phase-out prevented countries at COP 31, the United Nations climate talks in Antalya, Turkiye, from achieving any consensus agreement on future climate action on Sunday (November 22, 2026), despite the conference running a record 48 hours into overtime. The European Union led objections to COP 31 President Murat Kurum’s consensus cover text that failed to include any explicit language about moving away from fossil fuels. The EU’s stance was reportedly supported by about 130 countries. On the other side of the divide, India is among the nations that supported the proposed cover text, as they want to keep using fossil fuels for the foreseeable future, with Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav stressing that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation.” “We express profound disappointment with the final draft COP31 cover decision or Antalya Pact. At a point where the world urgently needs action to avert disastrous levels of global warming, the draft cover decision falls well short,” Ireland’s Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien said, speaking on behalf of the EU. “We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science, that disregards the implementation gap, and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required to correct the overshoot and bring 1.5 degrees back to within reach… We will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” he added. A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome, it needs the consensus of all parties. Panama also formally objected to the text, saying that as a country battling droughts and other perilous impacts of climate change, the lack of any commitment to keep the rise in temperatures below 1.5 degrees C with firm action on phasing out fossil fuels was “a setback”. “Panama cannot support this decision. One, because it repeats previously agreed commitments without closing the gap between reality and what science demands. Two, because it weighs too much upon technologies such as CCUS [carbon capture utilisation and storage] instead of calling for deep changes, and three, because it weakens language agreed in previous decisions. This is a setback, a rollback,” said Ana Aguilar, Panama’s chief climate negotiator. On the other side, Saudi Arabia, China, and India are among the countries that are against language on prescriptive fossil fuel targets and didn’t oppose the way the cover text language was framed, while also expressing misgivings about the lack of clarity on adaptation finance. The countries are part of the Like Minded Developing Countries (LMDC) coalition, who are insistent on the use of fossil fuel in the foreseeable future to further their economies, but have also significantly deployed renewable energy.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Indian Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav said that India’s voice had shaped the draft COP 31 outcome, especially on food security, livelihoods, and cultural practices recognised in action on methane. However, in a post on X, he emphasised that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation. Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology and capacity-building for developing countries.”

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #23 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 COP31 talks fail as EU, others reject any climate deal without language on a fossil fuel phase-out

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 02:23:47 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India, China, Saudi Arabia are on the other side of the divide

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: A standoff on a fossil fuel phase-out prevented countries at COP 31, the United Nations climate talks in Antalya, Turkiye, from achieving any consensus agreement on future climate action on Sunday (November 22, 2026), despite the conference running a record 48 hours into overtime. The European Union led objections to COP 31 President Murat Kurum’s consensus cover text that failed to include any explicit language about moving away from fossil fuels. The EU’s stance was reportedly supported by about 130 countries. On the other side of the divide, India is among the nations that supported the proposed cover text, as they want to keep using fossil fuels for the foreseeable future, with Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav stressing that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation.” “We express profound disappointment with the final draft COP31 cover decision or Antalya Pact. At a point where the world urgently needs action to avert disastrous levels of global warming, the draft cover decision falls well short,” Ireland’s Climate Minister Darragh O’Brien said, speaking on behalf of the EU. “We will not endorse a decision that does not respond to the science, that disregards the implementation gap, and that actually risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required to correct the overshoot and bring 1.5 degrees back to within reach… We will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuel,” he added. A cover text is an overarching political decision that frames the outcome of a climate conference rather than settling any single agenda item. It is usually finalised last, and like every outcome, it needs the consensus of all parties. Panama also formally objected to the text, saying that as a country battling droughts and other perilous impacts of climate change, the lack of any commitment to keep the rise in temperatures below 1.5 degrees C with firm action on phasing out fossil fuels was “a setback”. “Panama cannot support this decision. One, because it repeats previously agreed commitments without closing the gap between reality and what science demands. Two, because it weighs too much upon technologies such as CCUS [carbon capture utilisation and storage] instead of calling for deep changes, and three, because it weakens language agreed in previous decisions. This is a setback, a rollback,” said Ana Aguilar, Panama’s chief climate negotiator. On the other side, Saudi Arabia, China, and India are among the countries that are against language on prescriptive fossil fuel targets and didn’t oppose the way the cover text language was framed, while also expressing misgivings about the lack of clarity on adaptation finance. The countries are part of the Like Minded Developing Countries (LMDC) coalition, who are insistent on the use of fossil fuel in the foreseeable future to further their economies, but have also significantly deployed renewable energy.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Indian Environment Minister Bhupendra Yadav said that India’s voice had shaped the draft COP 31 outcome, especially on food security, livelihoods, and cultural practices recognised in action on methane. However, in a post on X, he emphasised that “climate ambition must go hand in hand with means of implementation. Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology and capacity-building for developing countries.”

📚 TOP 4 HARD VOCABULARY WORDS EXTRACTED FROM THIS PARAGRAPH (TAP CARD FOR PICTURE & SYNONYMS):
Environmental (Adjective)
पर्यावरण, प्रकृति और हमारे पारिस्थितिकी तंत्र (Ecosystem) से संबंधित।
✓ Syn: Ecological, Biospheric, Natural  |  ✖ Ant: Industrial, Polluting, Synthetic
Implementation (Noun)
क्रियान्वयन / ज़मीनी स्तर पर लागू करना — किसी योजना या फैसले को असलियत में पूरा करना।
✓ Syn: Execution, Enforcement, Fulfillment  |  ✖ Ant: Abandonment, Neglect, Cancellation
Disappointment (Adjective)
निराशा — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Disappointment' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Prescriptive (Adjective)
नियम के अनुसार — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Prescriptive' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

A. EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India,...

D. The author contends that 'COP31 talks fail as EU, others reject any cli' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "EU, Panama among about 130 parties that refuse to accept COP President’s consensus cover text, alleges that it “greenwashes” fossil fuels; India,..." (Hinglish Arth: यूरोपीय संघ, पनामा सहित लगभग 130 पार्टियों ने सीओपी अध्यक्ष के सर्वसम्मति कवर पाठ को स्वीकार करने से इनकार कर दिया, उनका आरोप है कि यह जीवाश्म ईंधन को "ग्रीनवॉश" करता है; भारत, चीन, सऊदी अरब विभाजन के दूसरी तरफ हैं)

A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology and capacity-building for developing countries.”.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Energy transitions must be nationally determined, just and equitable, backed by finance, technology and capacity-building for developing countries.”." (Hinglish Arth: विकासशील देशों के लिए ऊर्जा परिवर्तन राष्ट्रीय स्तर पर निर्धारित, न्यायसंगत और वित्त, प्रौद्योगिकी और क्षमता-निर्माण द्वारा समर्थित होना चाहिए।)

articles.title: U.S. targets chip smuggling to China after Huang's return to scandal-hit Nvidia
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Jensen Huang resigned over extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, linked to Singapore-based company Megaspeed International, who is suspected of being a Chinese spy

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Singapore agreed on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) to cooperate with the United States after it added the company at the centre of the Nvidia scandal to a trade backlist, following CEO Jensen Huang's stunning return to the helm of the U.S. chip giant. Mr. Huang resigned over extramarital affairs , including with Alice Huang, linked to Singapore-based company Megaspeed International, who is suspected of being a Chinese spy. News of his return sent Nvidia shares soaring 31.5% and pulled the tech-heavy Nasdaq up more than 6%. The company said on Monday (November 23) that it had reinstated Huang as chief executive after receiving information from the U.S. government that he did not pose a national security risk. Following Mr. Huang's return, the U.S. added Megaspeed to a trade blacklist that bars it from purchasing advanced chips. The company, along with four affiliates in Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, was added to the U.S. Commerce Department's Entity List for "acting contrary to the national security or foreign policy interests of the United States" on Monday, the department said in a filing on the Federal Register. Singapore-based Apex Enterprise Solutions, a subsidiary of Chinese tech giant Alibaba, was also added to the list. The move prompted Malaysia to urge data centre operators to cut links with seven companies, including Megaspeed and two local firms on the blacklist. Singapore's Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said on Tuesday (November 24) the country was working with the U.S. to stop companies "exploiting Singapore's position to tranship and reroute chips through Singapore to other parts of Southeast Asia or to other countries".
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: U.S. President Donald Trump said Mr. Huang's return followed his own direct contacts with Nvidia's board, calling it a "correct and proper decision".

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #24 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 U.S. targets chip smuggling to China after Huang's return to scandal-hit Nvidia

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 02:21:30 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Jensen Huang resigned over extramarital affairs, including with Alice Huang, linked to Singapore-based company Megaspeed International, who is suspected of being a Chinese spy

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Singapore agreed on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) to cooperate with the United States after it added the company at the centre of the Nvidia scandal to a trade backlist, following CEO Jensen Huang's stunning return to the helm of the U.S. chip giant. Mr. Huang resigned over extramarital affairs , including with Alice Huang, linked to Singapore-based company Megaspeed International, who is suspected of being a Chinese spy. News of his return sent Nvidia shares soaring 31.5% and pulled the tech-heavy Nasdaq up more than 6%. The company said on Monday (November 23) that it had reinstated Huang as chief executive after receiving information from the U.S. government that he did not pose a national security risk. Following Mr. Huang's return, the U.S. added Megaspeed to a trade blacklist that bars it from purchasing advanced chips. The company, along with four affiliates in Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, was added to the U.S. Commerce Department's Entity List for "acting contrary to the national security or foreign policy interests of the United States" on Monday, the department said in a filing on the Federal Register. Singapore-based Apex Enterprise Solutions, a subsidiary of Chinese tech giant Alibaba, was also added to the list. The move prompted Malaysia to urge data centre operators to cut links with seven companies, including Megaspeed and two local firms on the blacklist. Singapore's Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said on Tuesday (November 24) the country was working with the U.S. to stop companies "exploiting Singapore's position to tranship and reroute chips through Singapore to other parts of Southeast Asia or to other countries".

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: U.S. President Donald Trump said Mr. Huang's return followed his own direct contacts with Nvidia's board, calling it a "correct and proper decision".

fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: ‘I would like to make an announcement today that I would like to set up an advisory group, as I have for the TSPs [telecom service providers], an advisory group for our startups and MSMEs that would meet with me regularly with your pain points so that we can resolve,’ says Mr. Scindia

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Telecom Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia has announced the setting up of an advisory panel to resolve issues related to startups and MSMEs in the sector. During the Telecom Startups and MSME conclave, several entities presented their readiness to provide advanced technologies required for self-reliance in the sector, and also flagged issues that are retarding their growth path. articles.title: NASA’s Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth on November 18: What does it mean?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: NASA’s Voyager 1, humanity’s farthest spacecraft, is about to reach one light-day from Earth, more than 16 billion miles away; Know what it means

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: NASA’s Voyager 1 is set to cross a historic threshold in space exploration as it is about to become humanity’s first object to reach one light-day from Earth. The iconic probe, which has travelled farther from Earth than any other human-made object since its launch in 1977, is expected to cross the landmark on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) at 5:16:07 a.m. EST (3:46:07 p.m. IST), according to NASA. Infographics: Voyager I’s 49-year journey into the void Having spent 49 years, two months and 11 days hurtling through the cosmos, Voyager 1 continues to push the boundaries of human space exploration. One light-day is a staggering measure of distance, rather than a measure of time. It represents the exact space that light, which travels at roughly 186,000 miles (300,000 kilometres) per second, covers in a full 24-hour period. For Voyager 1, this is equivalent to more than 16 billion miles away from Earth. When Voyager 1 reaches that incredible milestone on November 18, its radio signals will take precisely 24 hours travelling at the speed of light to reach Earth — in other words, one light-day. Sunlight takes just over eight minutes to reach Earth, and over four hours and 10 minutes to reach Neptune. From November 18, any radio command sent from NASA’s Deep Space Network to Voyager 1 will take a full 24 hours to arrive, requiring another 24 hours for the spacecraft’s response to return. Launched on September 2, 1977, Voyager 1 was originally designed for a four-year mission to study Jupiter and Saturn. Its trajectory eventually allowed it to overtake its twin, Voyager 2, which was launched 16 days earlier. According to NASA, Voyager 2 is expected to reach the one-light-day distance from Earth in November 2035. 🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: NASA’s Voyager 1, humanity’s farthest spacecraft, is about to reach one light-day from Earth, more than 16 billion miles away; Know what it means

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: NASA’s Voyager 1 is set to cross a historic threshold in space exploration as it is about to become humanity’s first object to reach one light-day from Earth. The iconic probe, which has travelled farther from Earth than any other human-made object since its launch in 1977, is expected to cross the landmark on Wednesday (November 18, 2026) at 5:16:07 a.m. EST (3:46:07 p.m. IST), according to NASA. Infographics: Voyager I’s 49-year journey into the void Having spent 49 years, two months and 11 days hurtling through the cosmos, Voyager 1 continues to push the boundaries of human space exploration. One light-day is a staggering measure of distance, rather than a measure of time. It represents the exact space that light, which travels at roughly 186,000 miles (300,000 kilometres) per second, covers in a full 24-hour period. For Voyager 1, this is equivalent to more than 16 billion miles away from Earth. When Voyager 1 reaches that incredible milestone on November 18, its radio signals will take precisely 24 hours travelling at the speed of light to reach Earth — in other words, one light-day. Sunlight takes just over eight minutes to reach Earth, and over four hours and 10 minutes to reach Neptune. From November 18, any radio command sent from NASA’s Deep Space Network to Voyager 1 will take a full 24 hours to arrive, requiring another 24 hours for the spacecraft’s response to return. Launched on September 2, 1977, Voyager 1 was originally designed for a four-year mission to study Jupiter and Saturn. Its trajectory eventually allowed it to overtake its twin, Voyager 2, which was launched 16 days earlier. According to NASA, Voyager 2 is expected to reach the one-light-day distance from Earth in November 2035. The two spacecrafts were launched to explore the outer planets, with Voyager 1 taking a trajectory that eventually carried it towards interstellar space. It became the first spacecraft that entered the interstellar space in August 2012 and has continued transmitting information from beyond the solar system. Today, it speeds onward at roughly 38,000 miles per hour.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: In 1990, Voyager 1 captured the most distant image of Earth, known as the iconic “Pale Blue Dot,” while venturing farther than any other human-made object beyond Neptune.

articles.title: BJP MLA Rekha Patra’s condition improves, legislator remains under observation
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Rekha Patra is now able to speak and communicate any physical discomfort to doctors, while the slurring in her speech has also reduced significantly

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The health condition of BJP MLA Rekha Patra has improved, with her slurred speech reducing considerably, but doctors have kept her in the intensive care unit (ICU) for close observation, hospital sources said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026). The Hingalganj MLA was taken off ventilator support on Monday (November 23, 2026) and has not required it since. She is now able to speak and communicate any physical discomfort to doctors, while the slurring in her speech has also reduced significantly, BJP leader Archana Das Majumdar said. However, the three-member medical team treating her is not willing to take any chances and has recommended that she remain in the ICU for continued monitoring. Hospital sources said she was still receiving supplemental oxygen due to low oxygen levels in her body. While other clinical parameters indicate a positive recovery, doctors remain concerned about possible complications arising from the poisoning. Following the suspected poisoning, excessive saliva had accumulated in Ms. Patra's mouth. As she was not fully conscious, some saliva entered her lungs, affecting oxygen supply to the body, an earlier CT scan had found. Doctors said the effects of impaired oxygen supply to the lungs may not become immediately apparent and could manifest after some delay. A repeat CT scan of her chest was scheduled for Tuesday (November 24, 2026) afternoon to assess the extent of any lung damage. Her further recovery would depend, among other factors, on the findings of the scan, they said. Meanwhile, doctors are yet to establish the exact composition of the suspected poison detected in her stomach.
3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to the medical team, the substance found in her stomach was described as a herbal larvicide (herbal pesticide), but its precise ingredients remain unknown.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #7 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 BJP MLA Rekha Patra’s condition improves, legislator remains under observation

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 05:14:24 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Rekha Patra is now able to speak and communicate any physical discomfort to doctors, while the slurring in her speech has also reduced significantly

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: The health condition of BJP MLA Rekha Patra has improved, with her slurred speech reducing considerably, but doctors have kept her in the intensive care unit (ICU) for close observation, hospital sources said on Tuesday (November 24, 2026). The Hingalganj MLA was taken off ventilator support on Monday (November 23, 2026) and has not required it since. She is now able to speak and communicate any physical discomfort to doctors, while the slurring in her speech has also reduced significantly, BJP leader Archana Das Majumdar said. However, the three-member medical team treating her is not willing to take any chances and has recommended that she remain in the ICU for continued monitoring. Hospital sources said she was still receiving supplemental oxygen due to low oxygen levels in her body. While other clinical parameters indicate a positive recovery, doctors remain concerned about possible complications arising from the poisoning. Following the suspected poisoning, excessive saliva had accumulated in Ms. Patra's mouth. As she was not fully conscious, some saliva entered her lungs, affecting oxygen supply to the body, an earlier CT scan had found. Doctors said the effects of impaired oxygen supply to the lungs may not become immediately apparent and could manifest after some delay. A repeat CT scan of her chest was scheduled for Tuesday (November 24, 2026) afternoon to assess the extent of any lung damage. Her further recovery would depend, among other factors, on the findings of the scan, they said. Meanwhile, doctors are yet to establish the exact composition of the suspected poison detected in her stomach.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: According to the medical team, the substance found in her stomach was described as a herbal larvicide (herbal pesticide), but its precise ingredients remain unknown.

articles.title: Rift within Congress: Rajmohan Unnithan challenges Shafi Parambil to public debate, warns ‘teacher and disciple will be exposed’
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Unnithan said he was ‘ready to end his political career' if Shafi Parambil could prove that his allegations were baseless

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Intensifying the internal conflict within the Congress in Keralam, Kasaragod MP Rajmohan Unnithan on Tuesday launched a sharp attack on fellow party leader Shafi Parambil, MP, alleging that a coordinated cyber campaign was being orchestrated against him and warning that he would expose those behind it if the attacks continued. Challenging Mr. Parambil to an open public debate, Mr Unnithan said he was “ready to end his political career” if Mr Parambil could prove that his allegations were baseless. He also claimed that he had recorded all relevant details in his personal diary and warned that the people involved, whom he described as “the teacher and the disciple”, would eventually be exposed. Mr Unnithan dismissed the claim that Mr. Parambil belonged to the ‘A’ group in the Congress, saying it would be “the eighth wonder of the world” to describe him as an A group leader. He clarified that he had not insulted Mr Parambil but had only stated that he did not belong to the group. Taking aim at those invoking the legacy of the late former Chief Minister Oommen Chandy, Mr Unnithan said many Congress leaders had stayed away when Chandy was being targeted, while others were concerned about protecting the public image. He questioned where those now speaking about the “Oommen Chandy school of politics” had been at the time. He also maintained that he had not received any personal benefits in Chandy’s name. Mr Unnithan alleged that the social media attacks against him were being conducted through fake accounts as part of a deliberate campaign rather than being spontaneous criticism. He claimed that the operation was being “controlled from Adoor and from a particular house.” Referring to a flat in Panampilly Nagar and a vehicle bearing the registration number 20-20, he hinted that he possessed information about those involved but declined to disclose further details immediately. “Everything is in my diary, the teacher and the disciple will both be trapped,” he warned, adding that he should not be unnecessarily provoked. He warned that if forced to reveal everything, “the respectable public image of certain people will be torn apart.” Mr Unnithan said he had always been “a lone fighter” within the party and had stood with former Congress leader K Karunakaran and Oommen Chandy “without expecting positions or personal gains.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Responding to allegations concerning his family, Mr Unnithan asserted that his son had never joined the BJP. Taking an apparent dig at Padmaja Venugopal, he said it was “the children of those who had secured everything” within the Congress who had crossed over to the BJP.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #8 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 Rift within Congress: Rajmohan Unnithan challenges Shafi Parambil to public debate, warns ‘teacher and disciple will be exposed’

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 05:13:49 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Unnithan said he was ‘ready to end his political career' if Shafi Parambil could prove that his allegations were baseless

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Intensifying the internal conflict within the Congress in Keralam, Kasaragod MP Rajmohan Unnithan on Tuesday launched a sharp attack on fellow party leader Shafi Parambil, MP, alleging that a coordinated cyber campaign was being orchestrated against him and warning that he would expose those behind it if the attacks continued. Challenging Mr. Parambil to an open public debate, Mr Unnithan said he was “ready to end his political career” if Mr Parambil could prove that his allegations were baseless. He also claimed that he had recorded all relevant details in his personal diary and warned that the people involved, whom he described as “the teacher and the disciple”, would eventually be exposed. Mr Unnithan dismissed the claim that Mr. Parambil belonged to the ‘A’ group in the Congress, saying it would be “the eighth wonder of the world” to describe him as an A group leader. He clarified that he had not insulted Mr Parambil but had only stated that he did not belong to the group. Taking aim at those invoking the legacy of the late former Chief Minister Oommen Chandy, Mr Unnithan said many Congress leaders had stayed away when Chandy was being targeted, while others were concerned about protecting the public image. He questioned where those now speaking about the “Oommen Chandy school of politics” had been at the time. He also maintained that he had not received any personal benefits in Chandy’s name. Mr Unnithan alleged that the social media attacks against him were being conducted through fake accounts as part of a deliberate campaign rather than being spontaneous criticism. He claimed that the operation was being “controlled from Adoor and from a particular house.” Referring to a flat in Panampilly Nagar and a vehicle bearing the registration number 20-20, he hinted that he possessed information about those involved but declined to disclose further details immediately. “Everything is in my diary, the teacher and the disciple will both be trapped,” he warned, adding that he should not be unnecessarily provoked. He warned that if forced to reveal everything, “the respectable public image of certain people will be torn apart.” Mr Unnithan said he had always been “a lone fighter” within the party and had stood with former Congress leader K Karunakaran and Oommen Chandy “without expecting positions or personal gains.”

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Responding to allegations concerning his family, Mr Unnithan asserted that his son had never joined the BJP. Taking an apparent dig at Padmaja Venugopal, he said it was “the children of those who had secured everything” within the Congress who had crossed over to the BJP.

✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Spontaneous (Adjective)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Spontaneous' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Information (Adjective / Verb)
महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Information' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।
✓ Syn: Restrictive, Counteractive, Adverse  |  ✖ Ant: Constructive, Supportive, Favorable
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Rift within Congress: Rajmohan Unnithan challenges Shafi Parambil to public debate, warns ‘teacher and disciple will be exposed’", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Unnithan said he was ‘ready to end his political career' if Shafi Parambil could prove that his allegations were baseless.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Rift within Congress: Rajmohan Unnithan challeng' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Rift within Congress: Rajmohan Unnithan chall' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Rift within Congress: Rajmohan Unnithan chall' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Unnithan said he was ‘ready to end his political career' if Shafi Parambil could prove that his allegations were baseless." (Hinglish Arth: उन्नीथन ने कहा कि अगर शफी परम्बिल साबित कर सकें कि उनके आरोप निराधार हैं तो वह 'अपना राजनीतिक करियर खत्म करने के लिए तैयार हैं')
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Rift within Congress: Rajmohan Unnithan challenges Shafi Parambil to public debate, warns ‘teacher and disciple will be exposed’"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Taking an apparent dig at Padmaja Venugopal, he said it was “the children of those who had secured everything” within the Congress who had crossed...
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Taking an apparent dig at Padmaja Venugopal, he said it was “the children of those who had secured everything” within the Congress who had crossed..." (Hinglish Arth: पद्मजा वेणुगोपाल पर स्पष्ट रूप से कटाक्ष करते हुए उन्होंने कहा कि यह कांग्रेस के भीतर "उन लोगों के बच्चे थे जिन्होंने सब कुछ सुरक्षित कर लिया था" जो भाजपा में चले गए थे।)

articles.title: After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal announce alliance for Punjab Assembly election
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Prime Minister Narendra Modi hails the move as ‘putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first’

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Six years after parting ways because of differences over the three farm laws, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and its oldest ally, the Shiromani Akali Dali (SAD ), reunited ahead of the Assembly election in Punjab, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailing the move as “putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first”. The announcement of the return of the SAD to the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) headed by the BJP was made at a press conference held at the BJP’s headquarters in New Delhi, and addressed by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal, and BJP president Nitin Nabin. Seat adjustment details are yet to be ironed out, according to Mr. Nabin, who said talks in this regard were ongoing, while Mr. Shah clarified that the SAD would continue to hold the status of “elder brother” or the more dominant partner in the State, with a claim to the Chief Minister’s post if the alliance came to power. “It is usually the elder brother who has a claim to the CM’s post,” Mr. Shah said. The alliance’s goal was to make Punjab drug-free by December 31, 2029, and make sure that law and order, development, and issues pertaining to farmers were addressed, the Home Minister also said. Mr. Badal hailed the long history and personal equations between senior leaders of the BJP, the late former PM Atal Behari Vajpayee and L.K. Advani, with his own father, late CM of Punjab, Parkash Singh Badal, who had, between the three of them, fashioned the alliance in 1996. “This is not a political alliance; it’s an alliance of people’s sentiments,” Mr. Sukhbir Badal said, emphasising Hindu- Sikh unity and harmony, as did Mr. Nabin in his remarks. The PM would be attending a public meeting in Moga on December 8, Mr. Sukhbir Badal said, marking the birth anniversary of Parkash Singh Badal. VIDEO | Delhi: During a joint press conference, Union Home Minister Amit Shah (@AmitShah) says, "BJP, the Akali Dal, and the NDA will contest in Punjab, and we will announce several key points in our manifesto. But, I want to make one thing very clear: eliminating drugs from Punjab will be our primary goal, eliminating corruption in Punjab will be our primary goal, and strengthening nationalist forces in Punjab will also be our primary goal. The current government in the state, led by Kejriwal Ji, had come to power promising to eliminate drugs within three months. They promised to eliminate drugs, but the problem has not been eradicated; it has increased. In 2017, Rahul Gandhi Ji had promised that drugs would be eliminated within one term. He made that promise, but his party also did nothing to address the drug problem. Now, I want to reiterate a promise that I made there: by December 31, 2029, we will make Punjab completely drug-free." (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/bIyFWTfmBd) While the contours of the exact seat-sharing agreement are yet to be decided, in the past, the BJP contested 23 out of the 117 seats in the fray, a situation that is likely to change, with the BJP being given more seats, albeit still fewer than the SAD. 🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #9 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal announce alliance for Punjab Assembly election

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 05:12:09 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Prime Minister Narendra Modi hails the move as ‘putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first’

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Six years after parting ways because of differences over the three farm laws, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and its oldest ally, the Shiromani Akali Dali (SAD ), reunited ahead of the Assembly election in Punjab, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi hailing the move as “putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first”. The announcement of the return of the SAD to the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) headed by the BJP was made at a press conference held at the BJP’s headquarters in New Delhi, and addressed by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal, and BJP president Nitin Nabin. Seat adjustment details are yet to be ironed out, according to Mr. Nabin, who said talks in this regard were ongoing, while Mr. Shah clarified that the SAD would continue to hold the status of “elder brother” or the more dominant partner in the State, with a claim to the Chief Minister’s post if the alliance came to power. “It is usually the elder brother who has a claim to the CM’s post,” Mr. Shah said. The alliance’s goal was to make Punjab drug-free by December 31, 2029, and make sure that law and order, development, and issues pertaining to farmers were addressed, the Home Minister also said. Mr. Badal hailed the long history and personal equations between senior leaders of the BJP, the late former PM Atal Behari Vajpayee and L.K. Advani, with his own father, late CM of Punjab, Parkash Singh Badal, who had, between the three of them, fashioned the alliance in 1996. “This is not a political alliance; it’s an alliance of people’s sentiments,” Mr. Sukhbir Badal said, emphasising Hindu- Sikh unity and harmony, as did Mr. Nabin in his remarks. The PM would be attending a public meeting in Moga on December 8, Mr. Sukhbir Badal said, marking the birth anniversary of Parkash Singh Badal. VIDEO | Delhi: During a joint press conference, Union Home Minister Amit Shah (@AmitShah) says, "BJP, the Akali Dal, and the NDA will contest in Punjab, and we will announce several key points in our manifesto. But, I want to make one thing very clear: eliminating drugs from Punjab will be our primary goal, eliminating corruption in Punjab will be our primary goal, and strengthening nationalist forces in Punjab will also be our primary goal. The current government in the state, led by Kejriwal Ji, had come to power promising to eliminate drugs within three months. They promised to eliminate drugs, but the problem has not been eradicated; it has increased. In 2017, Rahul Gandhi Ji had promised that drugs would be eliminated within one term. He made that promise, but his party also did nothing to address the drug problem. Now, I want to reiterate a promise that I made there: by December 31, 2029, we will make Punjab completely drug-free." (Full video available on PTI Videos - https://t.co/bIyFWTfmBd) While the contours of the exact seat-sharing agreement are yet to be decided, in the past, the BJP contested 23 out of the 117 seats in the fray, a situation that is likely to change, with the BJP being given more seats, albeit still fewer than the SAD. The alliance had won 93 seats in the 1997 Assembly election, with the SAD winning 75 seats and the BJP winning 18 seats. After losing power to the Congress in 2002, the alliance returned to office in 2007 with 68 seats and retained power in 2012 with an identical tally, bucking Punjab’s trend of voting out incumbent governments.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: The SAD walked away from the NDA in 2020, with party MP Harsimrat Badal also resigning her position as Minister in the Modi government at the Centre over the three farm laws that sought to re-engineer agri-commerce, igniting months-long protests on Delhi’s borders. To a question by the media on what the SAD had to say about the farm laws now, Mr. Shah answered that since the farm Bills had been withdrawn by the government, “there is no point in asking the question”.

🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal announce alliance for Punjab Assembly election", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Prime Minister Narendra Modi hails the move as ‘putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first’.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal announc' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal anno' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal anno' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Prime Minister Narendra Modi hails the move as ‘putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first’." (Hinglish Arth: प्रधान मंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी ने इस कदम को 'पंजाब और पंजाबियों के कल्याण को पहले स्थान पर रखने' वाला कदम बताया।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal announce alliance for Punjab Assembly election"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Shah answered that since the farm Bills had been withdrawn by the government, “there is no point in asking the question”.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "Shah answered that since the farm Bills had been withdrawn by the government, “there is no point in asking the question”." (Hinglish Arth: शाह ने जवाब दिया कि चूंकि सरकार ने कृषि बिल वापस ले लिया है, इसलिए "सवाल पूछने का कोई मतलब नहीं है"।)

articles.title: Sonia Gandhi recalls ‘pull of power’ while deciding against becoming PM in 2004
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Polity: Constitutional Amendments, Supreme Court Judgements, Parliamentary Bills & Governance Schemes
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: She said it was a lesson about power that ‘once you have it, you may find excuses to keep it.’

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi has said she felt the "pull of power" while deciding on whether she should take up the prime ministership in 2004, as she thought that she owed it to party workers who had rallied across the country during the election campaign to accept the post. She said it was a lesson about power that "once you have it, you may find excuses to keep it". The observations came during a conversation with her son Rahul Gandhi and daughter Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, a video of which was shared by them on social media platforms. In the video shared days after the launch of Sonia Gandhi's memoir 'Belonging: A Journey Of Love' , the three are seen reminiscing about moments of joy, laughter and pain they felt at various points in time. In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi shared the video and said, "Ma's journey of Belonging has been full of enormous love and terrible tragedy, and she has met all of it with dignity and courage." The proposal didn't go according to plan and neither did my seventh birthday. The decision in 2004 gave some of us relief but others joy. There was an intention behind withdrawing Papa's security. And even after 500+ pages there are some things Ma has left out of her book. Priyanka and I sat down with our mother to talk through all of it. Going back to those memories brought back the joy, the laughter and even the pain we felt at the time. Ma's journey of Belonging has been full of enormous love and terrible tragedy, and she has met all of it with dignity and courage. In the video, Sonia Gandhi talks in detail about the internal conflict she faced while deciding whether to take up the Prime Minister's post after the Congress-led UPA's victory in the 2004 Lok Sabha elections. She asserts that she did not want power. Talking about the time, Rahul Gandhi says there was a situation unfolding and "we were witnessing the situation from the inside". "On the one hand there was mum saying maybe, maybe not. On the other side there were seven people. There is one gentleman over there who is the best possible PM," he recalls, referring to Manmohan Singh.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: "The interesting thing is there is only one man who can be PM because of his qualities, capabilities, and there are six-seven dreamers who cannot be. Then my mother decides - 'No (not taking up premiership)'; there is actually joy in the room," he says.

🏛️ Political, National & Polity Paragraph #12 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 Sonia Gandhi recalls ‘pull of power’ while deciding against becoming PM in 2004

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 05:10:10 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: She said it was a lesson about power that ‘once you have it, you may find excuses to keep it.’

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi has said she felt the "pull of power" while deciding on whether she should take up the prime ministership in 2004, as she thought that she owed it to party workers who had rallied across the country during the election campaign to accept the post. She said it was a lesson about power that "once you have it, you may find excuses to keep it". The observations came during a conversation with her son Rahul Gandhi and daughter Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, a video of which was shared by them on social media platforms. In the video shared days after the launch of Sonia Gandhi's memoir 'Belonging: A Journey Of Love' , the three are seen reminiscing about moments of joy, laughter and pain they felt at various points in time. In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi shared the video and said, "Ma's journey of Belonging has been full of enormous love and terrible tragedy, and she has met all of it with dignity and courage." The proposal didn't go according to plan and neither did my seventh birthday. The decision in 2004 gave some of us relief but others joy. There was an intention behind withdrawing Papa's security. And even after 500+ pages there are some things Ma has left out of her book. Priyanka and I sat down with our mother to talk through all of it. Going back to those memories brought back the joy, the laughter and even the pain we felt at the time. Ma's journey of Belonging has been full of enormous love and terrible tragedy, and she has met all of it with dignity and courage. In the video, Sonia Gandhi talks in detail about the internal conflict she faced while deciding whether to take up the Prime Minister's post after the Congress-led UPA's victory in the 2004 Lok Sabha elections. She asserts that she did not want power. Talking about the time, Rahul Gandhi says there was a situation unfolding and "we were witnessing the situation from the inside". "On the one hand there was mum saying maybe, maybe not. On the other side there were seven people. There is one gentleman over there who is the best possible PM," he recalls, referring to Manmohan Singh.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: "The interesting thing is there is only one man who can be PM because of his qualities, capabilities, and there are six-seven dreamers who cannot be. Then my mother decides - 'No (not taking up premiership)'; there is actually joy in the room," he says.

महत्वपूर्ण विश्लेषणात्मक शब्द — इस लेख में 'Situation' मुख्य प्रभाव और नीतिगत स्थिति को स्पष्ट करता है।

चुनाव — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Election' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🏛️ Political, National & Polity passage on "Sonia Gandhi recalls ‘pull of power’ while deciding against becoming PM in 2004", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. She said it was a lesson about power that ‘once you have it, you may find excuses to keep it.’.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Sonia Gandhi recalls ‘pull of power’ while decid' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Sonia Gandhi recalls ‘pull of power’ while de' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Sonia Gandhi recalls ‘pull of power’ while de' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "She said it was a lesson about power that ‘once you have it, you may find excuses to keep it.’." (Hinglish Arth: उन्होंने कहा कि यह शक्ति के बारे में एक सबक है कि 'एक बार यह आपके पास हो जाए, तो आप इसे बनाए रखने के लिए बहाने ढूंढ सकते हैं।')

A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. Then my mother decides - 'No (not taking up premiership)'; there is actually joy in the room," he says.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. articles.title: Sri Lanka’s Opposition lawmakers accuse government of preventing parliamentary debate on Imran Khan’s release
articles.examRelevance: Current Affairs & GS-II: Bilateral Treaties, Global Summits (UN/G20/BRICS/Quad) & Strategic Diplomacy
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Cannot entertain motion that could impact bilateral ties, said the Sri Lanka government

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Opposition lawmakers in Sri Lanka have accused the government of preventing a parliamentary debate on the release of jailed former Prime Minister of Pakistan Imran Khan. Last week, the state-run Daily News reported that the Sri Lankan Parliament was scheduled to hold an adjournment debate on November 21, 2026, on a motion moved by Opposition MP Ajith P. Perera, from the main Opposition party Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB or United People’s Power), calling for Mr. Khan’s release on humanitarian grounds. The debate did not take place. Mr. Perera expressed disappointment and said it was “regrettable that the motion has been rejected even before being debated.” Defending the government’s position, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Arun Hemachandra said the government did not wish to entertain matters that could create “diplomatic tensions” or affect ties with Sri Lanka’s bilateral partners. However, Mr. Hemachandra observed that Mr. Perera was free to express his personal views on the matter during the time allocated to him in Parliament. Addressing Parliament on Monday (November 23, 2026), SJB MP and Leader of the Sri Lanka Muslim Congress Rauff Hakeem attacked the government for pursuing a “transactional” foreign policy, rather than one based on principles. Pakistan, he said, had been “a longstanding friend” of Sri Lanka, supporting the island during difficult times. He recalled Pakistan’s assistance during the pandemic and Mr. Khan’s crucial intervention in urging the Gotabaya Rajapaksa government to end its mandatory cremations policy during the pandemic that had caused enormous distress among the island’s Muslim community. Sri Lanka and Pakistan have historically maintained close bilateral ties, regardless of the party in power in either country. Mr. Khan visited Colombo in February 2021, when he was Prime Minister. Gotabaya Rajapaksa was President of Sri Lanka at the time. Mr. Khan’s two-day visit was received very well by the local media as well as cricketing fans on the island, known for its passion for the game.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Further, Mr. Hakeem slammed the government’s position on the Palestine issue, contending that statements of support at international fora meant little without substantive domestic action. Sri Lanka’s ruling Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna [JVP or People’s Liberation Front] has historically supported the Palestinian cause. After its ascent to power in 2024, the National People’s Power coalition that the JVP leads has maintained ties with Israel and has continued to send Sri Lankan workers to Israel. In an interview to The Hindu in May 2026, Deputy Minister Mr. Hemachandra said: “We separated our Free Palestine stand and our diplomatic relationship with Israel as two different things. I think any country should have that choice. And when we take the opportunity to send workers to Israel, that does not change our stand on Palestine.”

Perera, from the main Opposition party Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB or United People’s Power), calling for Mr. Khan’s release on humanitarian grounds. The debate did not take place. Mr. Perera expressed disappointment and said it was “regrettable that the motion has been rejected even before being debated.” Defending the government’s position, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Arun Hemachandra said the government did not wish to entertain matters that could create “diplomatic tensions” or affect ties with Sri Lanka’s bilateral partners. However, Mr. Hemachandra observed that Mr. Perera was free to express his personal views on the matter during the time allocated to him in Parliament. Addressing Parliament on Monday (November 23, 2026), SJB MP and Leader of the Sri Lanka Muslim Congress Rauff Hakeem attacked the government for pursuing a “transactional” foreign policy, rather than one based on principles. Pakistan, he said, had been “a longstanding friend” of Sri Lanka, supporting the island during difficult times. He recalled Pakistan’s assistance during the pandemic and Mr. Khan’s crucial intervention in urging the Gotabaya Rajapaksa government to end its mandatory cremations policy during the pandemic that had caused enormous distress among the island’s Muslim community. Sri Lanka and Pakistan have historically maintained close bilateral ties, regardless of the party in power in either country. Mr. Khan visited Colombo in February 2021, when he was Prime Minister. Gotabaya Rajapaksa was President of Sri Lanka at the time. Mr. Khan’s two-day visit was received very well by the local media as well as cricketing fans on the island, known for its passion for the game.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Further, Mr. Hakeem slammed the government’s position on the Palestine issue, contending that statements of support at international fora meant little without substantive domestic action. Sri Lanka’s ruling Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna [JVP or People’s Liberation Front] has historically supported the Palestinian cause. After its ascent to power in 2024, the National People’s Power coalition that the JVP leads has maintained ties with Israel and has continued to send Sri Lankan workers to Israel. In an interview to The Hindu in May 2026, Deputy Minister Mr. Hemachandra said: “We separated our Free Palestine stand and our diplomatic relationship with Israel as two different things. I think any country should have that choice. And when we take the opportunity to send workers to Israel, that does not change our stand on Palestine.”

🌐 International & Geopolitics Paragraph #22 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 Sri Lanka’s Opposition lawmakers accuse government of preventing parliamentary debate on Imran Khan’s release

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 06:15:56 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Cannot entertain motion that could impact bilateral ties, said the Sri Lanka government

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Opposition lawmakers in Sri Lanka have accused the government of preventing a parliamentary debate on the release of jailed former Prime Minister of Pakistan Imran Khan. Last week, the state-run Daily News reported that the Sri Lankan Parliament was scheduled to hold an adjournment debate on November 21, 2026, on a motion moved by Opposition MP Ajith P. Perera, from the main Opposition party Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB or United People’s Power), calling for Mr. Khan’s release on humanitarian grounds. The debate did not take place. Mr. Perera expressed disappointment and said it was “regrettable that the motion has been rejected even before being debated.” Defending the government’s position, Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Arun Hemachandra said the government did not wish to entertain matters that could create “diplomatic tensions” or affect ties with Sri Lanka’s bilateral partners. However, Mr. Hemachandra observed that Mr. Perera was free to express his personal views on the matter during the time allocated to him in Parliament. Addressing Parliament on Monday (November 23, 2026), SJB MP and Leader of the Sri Lanka Muslim Congress Rauff Hakeem attacked the government for pursuing a “transactional” foreign policy, rather than one based on principles. Pakistan, he said, had been “a longstanding friend” of Sri Lanka, supporting the island during difficult times. He recalled Pakistan’s assistance during the pandemic and Mr. Khan’s crucial intervention in urging the Gotabaya Rajapaksa government to end its mandatory cremations policy during the pandemic that had caused enormous distress among the island’s Muslim community. Sri Lanka and Pakistan have historically maintained close bilateral ties, regardless of the party in power in either country. Mr. Khan visited Colombo in February 2021, when he was Prime Minister. Gotabaya Rajapaksa was President of Sri Lanka at the time. Mr. Khan’s two-day visit was received very well by the local media as well as cricketing fans on the island, known for its passion for the game.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Further, Mr. Hakeem slammed the government’s position on the Palestine issue, contending that statements of support at international fora meant little without substantive domestic action. Sri Lanka’s ruling Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna [JVP or People’s Liberation Front] has historically supported the Palestinian cause. After its ascent to power in 2024, the National People’s Power coalition that the JVP leads has maintained ties with Israel and has continued to send Sri Lankan workers to Israel. In an interview to The Hindu in May 2026, Deputy Minister Mr. Hemachandra said: “We separated our Free Palestine stand and our diplomatic relationship with Israel as two different things. I think any country should have that choice. And when we take the opportunity to send workers to Israel, that does not change our stand on Palestine.”

लेन-देन संबंधी — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Transactional' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
International (Adjective)
अंतरराष्ट्रीय — इस अनुच्छेद में 'International' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile

Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🌐 International & Geopolitics passage on "Sri Lanka’s Opposition lawmakers accuse government of preventing parliamentary debate on Imran Khan’s release", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Cannot entertain motion that could impact bilateral ties, said the Sri Lanka government.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'Sri Lanka’s Opposition lawmakers accuse governme' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'Sri Lanka’s Opposition lawmakers accuse gover' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'Sri Lanka’s Opposition lawmakers accuse gover' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Cannot entertain motion that could impact bilateral ties, said the Sri Lanka government." (Hinglish Arth: श्रीलंका सरकार ने कहा, ऐसे प्रस्ताव पर विचार नहीं किया जा सकता जो द्विपक्षीय संबंधों को प्रभावित कर सकता हो)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "Sri Lanka’s Opposition lawmakers accuse government of preventing parliamentary debate on Imran Khan’s release"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. And when we take the opportunity to send workers to Israel, that does not change our stand on Palestine.”.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "And when we take the opportunity to send workers to Israel, that does not change our stand on Palestine.”." articles.title: What do lemurs and opera singers share?
articles.examRelevance: Prelims & GS-III: ISRO/DRDO Missions, Quantum & High-Tech, Biodiversity, Ramsar Sites & Climate Action
fullParagraphs: 1. Core Context & Background: Recently, a study showed how indri lemurs use the same method opera singers use to ensure their vocals reach the audience at the back. In conversation with one of the researchers, Dr Chiara De Gregorio from the University of Warwick

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Have you seen opera performers sing? You might notice how their mouths move according to how high their pitch needs to be. Imagine finding out a primate in the rainforests of Madagascar has been doing the same, possibly even before opera began? With a pointy snout, large eyes and usually a long tail, you might have encountered this primate in one of your favourite movies, Madagascar. Remember King Julien, who loved to sing and dance? He was a type of lemur! So were Maurice and Mort, the two characters always around him. Endemic (naturally found only in) to the island of Madagascar, lemurs are primates with diverse activity patterns, and even though they share a resemblance with other primates, they evolved independently from monkeys, apes, etc. They are considered to be the world’s most endangered mammals by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN). This is mostly due to habitat loss, hunting and even unstable conservation efforts due to political and financial instabilities. While most lemurs might survive in captivity, there are specific species like the indri which can only survive in their natural habitat, making it extremely important for us to protect the forests and their home. Today, let’s talk about this very species — the indri or babakoto! One of the larger lemur species, the indri is the only singing lemur in the world. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement One of the larger lemur species, the indri is the only singing lemur in the world. These black-and-white-coated primates are known for their loud, often complex, and haunting territorial songs. They often sing as duets or group choruses and even use opera-like vocal techniques to reach higher pitches. This was, in fact, a quite recent discovery. Researchers from the University of Warwick and the University of Turin found that the world’s only singing lemur opens its mouth wider on higher notes, just like a trained soprano. The new study, published in PLOS Computational Biology , shows the first direct evidence that wild indris coordinate their mouth opening with the frequency of their songs. The research team analysed 83 video recordings of 19 wild indris, combining field audio with markerless motion-tracking technology. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement “The opera singers back in the day, before mics became a thing, used to tweak the shape of their mouth to sing louder and to reach farther to the audience sitting at the back. Imagine finding the same technique being used in the middle of a rainforest in Madagascar,” laughed Dr Chiara De Gregorio, corresponding author and Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Warwick.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Human singers are trained to widen their mouths as pitch rises, aligning the resonant frequencies of the vocal tract with the harmonics of the voice and amplifying the sound. For an animal communicating through a thick forest, it could make the difference between a song that carries and one that doesn’t.

🚀 Science, Tech & Environment Paragraph #30 of 30 (24 NOV)

📰 What do lemurs and opera singers share?

📌 Published: 24 Nov 2026, 05:46:37 PM
🎙️ Desi Hinglish Voice Educator • 🚂 Live Train Line Highlight & Screen Lock

1. Core Context & Background: Recently, a study showed how indri lemurs use the same method opera singers use to ensure their vocals reach the audience at the back. In conversation with one of the researchers, Dr Chiara De Gregorio from the University of Warwick

2. Constitutional / Economic / Policy Analysis: Have you seen opera performers sing? You might notice how their mouths move according to how high their pitch needs to be. Imagine finding out a primate in the rainforests of Madagascar has been doing the same, possibly even before opera began? With a pointy snout, large eyes and usually a long tail, you might have encountered this primate in one of your favourite movies, Madagascar. Remember King Julien, who loved to sing and dance? He was a type of lemur! So were Maurice and Mort, the two characters always around him. Endemic (naturally found only in) to the island of Madagascar, lemurs are primates with diverse activity patterns, and even though they share a resemblance with other primates, they evolved independently from monkeys, apes, etc. They are considered to be the world’s most endangered mammals by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN). This is mostly due to habitat loss, hunting and even unstable conservation efforts due to political and financial instabilities. While most lemurs might survive in captivity, there are specific species like the indri which can only survive in their natural habitat, making it extremely important for us to protect the forests and their home. Today, let’s talk about this very species — the indri or babakoto! One of the larger lemur species, the indri is the only singing lemur in the world. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement One of the larger lemur species, the indri is the only singing lemur in the world. These black-and-white-coated primates are known for their loud, often complex, and haunting territorial songs. They often sing as duets or group choruses and even use opera-like vocal techniques to reach higher pitches. This was, in fact, a quite recent discovery. Researchers from the University of Warwick and the University of Turin found that the world’s only singing lemur opens its mouth wider on higher notes, just like a trained soprano. The new study, published in PLOS Computational Biology , shows the first direct evidence that wild indris coordinate their mouth opening with the frequency of their songs. The research team analysed 83 video recordings of 19 wild indris, combining field audio with markerless motion-tracking technology. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement “The opera singers back in the day, before mics became a thing, used to tweak the shape of their mouth to sing louder and to reach farther to the audience sitting at the back. Imagine finding the same technique being used in the middle of a rainforest in Madagascar,” laughed Dr Chiara De Gregorio, corresponding author and Honorary Research Fellow at the University of Warwick.

3. Way Forward & Exam Conclusion: Human singers are trained to widen their mouths as pitch rises, aligning the resonant frequencies of the vocal tract with the harmonics of the voice and amplifying the sound. For an animal communicating through a thick forest, it could make the difference between a song that carries and one that doesn’t.

अंतरराष्ट्रीय — इस अनुच्छेद में 'International' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।

✓ Syn: Comprehensive, Influential, Decisive  |  ✖ Ant: Superficial, Ineffective, Fragile
Conversation (Noun)
बातचीत — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Conversation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
Conservation (Noun)
संरक्षण — इस अनुच्छेद में 'Conservation' का प्रयोग एक महत्वपूर्ण प्रशासनिक और विश्लेषणात्मक अर्थ में किया गया है।
✓ Syn: Significant, Substantial, Strategic  |  ✖ Ant: Insignificant, Negligible, Trivial
🧠 2 ANALYTICAL EXAM QUESTIONS BASED ON THIS EDITORIAL:
Q1. Based on a critical reading of the above 🚀 Science, Tech & Environment passage on "What do lemurs and opera singers share?", which of the following statements accurately reflects the central analytical observation of the text?
A. Recently, a study showed how indri lemurs use the same method opera singers use to ensure their vocals reach the audience at the back.
B. Contrary to the passage, the issue of 'What do lemurs and opera singers share?' requires zero institutional or regulatory intervention at any level.
C. The passage argues that all empirical data and statutory mechanisms related to 'What do lemurs and opera singers share?' should be permanently discontinued.
D. The author contends that 'What do lemurs and opera singers share?' has no bearing on public governance, economy, or citizen welfare.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (A) — Sahi Jawab Option (A) hai. Is passage ki mukhya line saaf batati hai: "Recently, a study showed how indri lemurs use the same method opera singers use to ensure their vocals reach the audience at the back." (Hinglish Arth: हाल ही में, एक अध्ययन से पता चला है कि इंद्री लेमर्स उसी पद्धति का उपयोग करते हैं जो ओपेरा गायक यह सुनिश्चित करने के लिए करते हैं कि उनकी आवाज़ पीछे बैठे दर्शकों तक पहुंचे।)
Q2. Which of the following key analytical points or conclusions is explicitly highlighted by the author in the passage regarding "What do lemurs and opera singers share?"?
A. Advocating complete policy paralysis and ignoring ground-level implementation challenges.
B. For an animal communicating through a thick forest, it could make the difference between a song that carries and one that doesn’t.
C. Dismissing constitutional accountability and relying solely on unverified short-term measures.
D. Recommending the immediate suspension of all regulatory and scientific assessments mentioned in the text.
✅ Correct Answer: Option (B) — Sahi Jawab Option (B) hai. Lekhak ne passage ke vishleshan mein is baat par zor diya hai: "For an animal communicating through a thick forest, it could make the difference between a song that carries and one that doesn’t." (Hinglish Arth: घने जंगल में संचार करने वाले एक जानवर के लिए, यह उस गीत के बीच अंतर कर सकता है जो प्रसारित होता है और जो नहीं करता है।)
